artigo.texto: A chinesa CATL, apontada como a maior fabricante mundial de baterias, abriu um escritório comercial na Argentina para apoiar sua expansão no mercado local de armazenamento de energia, segundo relatos da imprensa argentina citados pelo South China Morning Post. A empresa pretende partir de projetos de baterias para a rede elétrica em Buenos Aires e alcançar aplicações em minas, centros de dados e parques eólicos da Patagônia. A CATL já fornece equipamentos ao maior projeto de armazenamento do país. Também apresentou seus sistemas a 35 companhias interessadas em uma licitação governamental para armazenamento. Na semana anterior à publicação, a fabricante conversou com geradoras de energia e bancos em Buenos Aires, embora não tenham sido informados valores de investimentos, contratos ou metas comerciais. Principais fatos e números - A CATL abriu um escritório comercial na Argentina. - A unidade servirá de base para a expansão no mercado argentino de armazenamento de energia. - A empresa já fornece o maior projeto de armazenamento do país. - Os mercados visados incluem minas, centros de dados e parques eólicos da Patagônia. - A CATL apresentou seus sistemas a 35 empresas interessadas em uma licitação governamental. - A fabricante conversou com geradoras de energia e bancos em Buenos Aires. Por que isso importa para empresários e investidores A presença comercial da CATL pode ampliar o acesso de empresas argentinas a sistemas de armazenamento para redes elétricas, mineração, centros de dados e geração eólica. Fornecedores, financiadores e operadores de infraestrutura podem encontrar oportunidades em instalação, integração, manutenção e crédito para novos projetos. Ao mesmo tempo, a expansão dependerá do resultado da licitação governamental e da conversão das conversas comerciais em contratos. Como a fonte não informa valores, cronogramas, capacidade dos sistemas ou compromissos firmes, ainda não é possível dimensionar o investimento nem seu efeito efetivo sobre o mercado argentino.

artigo.texto: ZutaCore and Munters Unveil Waterless Chip-to-Rooftop Cooling Architecture for AI Data Centers Key Highlights - Z₂O uses dielectric fluid and two-phase cold plates to transfer processor heat to rooftop equipment, where Munters SyCool rejects it to outdoor air. - The reference design is built around 625-kW IT blocks, with 500 kW of liquid cooling and 125 kW of air cooling. - The modeled pPUE comparison assumes Dulles, Virginia weather, constant full IT load and an 80/20 liquid-to-air cooling split. - ZutaCore says the first installation uses an ASRock Rack server with NVIDIA HGX B300, while independent operating results have not yet been reported. ZutaCore has introduced a new waterless cooling architecture designed to simplify AI data center thermal management by extending two-phase liquid cooling from the processor to the facility's rooftop heat rejection equipment. Unveiled at Supercomputing 2026 (SC26) in Chicago, the ZutaCore Z₂O architecture, developed in partnership with Munters, eliminates several components traditionally associated with liquid-cooled data centers, including cooling distribution units (CDUs), liquid-to-liquid heat exchangers, facility water loops and water-based cooling towers. The architecture uses a sealed dielectric fluid that absorbs heat directly from processors through two-phase cold plates. As the fluid boils, vapor carries heat to rooftop equipment, where it condenses and returns through the same loop. Munters SyCool technology provides heat rejection to the outdoor air, eliminating the need for cooling water. The approach represents an effort to address two increasingly significant constraints on AI infrastructure development: the availability of electrical power and the growing concern over water consumption. Reducing the Energy Cost of AI Cooling According to ZutaCore, the reference architecture developed with Munters achieves a modeled annualized partial power usage effectiveness (pPUE) of 1.03, compared with 1.115 for a conventional high-efficiency chilled-water system. Those figures translate into approximately 74% less energy consumed by cooling infrastructure, based on the modeled difference in facility overhead. The calculations use hourly weather data from Dulles, Virginia, assuming a constant 100% IT load and an 80/20 split between liquid and air cooling. The figures represent modeled performance rather than independently verified operating results. Z₂O is designed around repeatable 625-kW IT blocks, consisting of 500 kW of direct-to-chip liquid cooling and 125 kW of air cooling. The modular approach is intended to support new construction, existing facilities and prefabricated data center deployments. The architecture also incorporates N+1 heat-rejection redundancy and redundant UPS-supported pumps. ZutaCore's HyperCool Cloud software provides system monitoring. "AI operators have fought hard for every megawatt, and they should not be spending it on moving heat," said Dan Wood, ZutaCore's chief product officer. Implications for Data Center Development For developers facing increasingly restrictive power allocations, reducing the electrical requirements of cooling infrastructure could free additional capacity for revenue-producing computing equipment. Eliminating cooling towers, chillers and CDUs could also reduce mechanical infrastructure costs, simplify construction and shorten commissioning schedules. The extent of those benefits will depend on site conditions, system integration and actual operating performance. The elimination of cooling water consumption is particularly relevant in markets where water availability has become a significant consideration in data center permitting and community acceptance. ZutaCore said the first Z₂O installation uses an ASRock Rack server incorporating NVIDIA's HGX B300 platform with integrated two-phase cooling. The architecture also supports ZutaCore's HyperCool and recently introduced OmniTherm cold plates, allowing future processor upgrades without requiring changes to the underlying facility cooling loop. The announcement follows ZutaCore's $100 million-plus Series C funding round earlier this year, which included investments from Mitsubishi Electric, Carrier Ventures and Samsung Electronics. The larger significance of Z₂O is its attempt to extend liquid cooling optimization beyond the server rack. While most direct-to-chip technologies focus on efficiently extracting heat from processors, ZutaCore and Munters are targeting the supporting mechanical infrastructure that contributes to overall facility energy consumption. Whether the modeled performance advantages can be consistently achieved across different climates and operating loads remains to be demonstrated. Nevertheless, the architecture highlights the growing importance of treating cooling as an integrated facility design decision rather than an individual component of the IT infrastructure.

artigo.texto: Governo Lula avalia contestar restrições dos EUA à venda de chips para data centers no Brasil Medida anunciada pela gestão Trump coloca o país entre cinco países que precisarão de autorização para comprar equipamentos avançados utilizados em inteligência artificial O governo do presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva avalia a possibilidade de contestar as novas restrições anunciadas pelos Estados Unidos à venda de chips avançados de inteligência artificial para data centers instalados no Brasil. A medida, divulgada nesta segunda-feira, inclui o país em uma lista de cinco nações que passarão a depender de autorização do governo americano para importar esses componentes, utilizados em grandes centros de processamento de dados. - 'Certamente não é uma má ideia': Trump defende volta de Huang ao comando da Nvidia - Bessent: Secretário do Tesouro dos EUA tenta evitar retorno de Huang e pede reformulação 'drástica' na Nvidia Segundo interlocutores, uma eventual negociação com os Estados Unidos ou contestação das regras não está descartada. Até o momento, porém, o assunto não provocou preocupação significativa dentro do Executivo, e ainda não há uma definição sobre a adoção de medidas em resposta à decisão americana. A avaliação é de que os Estados Unidos têm amplo controle sobre a produção e o fornecimento desses chips, fundamentais para o funcionamento de sistemas avançados de inteligência artificial, o que dá ao país grande influência sobre sua comercialização no mercado internacional. Procurado, o Ministério do Desenvolvimento, Indústria, Comércio e Serviços disse que o governo brasileiro tomou conhecimento do comunicado do Departamento de Comércio dos EUA e acompanha com atenção eventuais desdobramentos da medida. "Importante destacar que não se trata de proibição de exportações de semicondutores avançados para o Brasil nem para os demais países citados no comunicado, mas sim de necessidade de autorização para que as operações se concretizem, motivo pelo qual não é possível avaliar, no momento, o efeito concreto da medida sobre as importações brasileiras desses insumos", diz o texto. Os data centers são instalações que reúnem servidores e equipamentos responsáveis por armazenar e processar grandes volumes de informações. Com o avanço da inteligência artificial, esses centros passaram a demandar chips cada vez mais potentes, capazes de realizar os cálculos necessários para desenvolver e operar a tecnologia. A nova norma foi anunciada pelo Departamento de Comércio dos Estados Unidos e também atinge Indonésia, Malásia, Cingapura e Tailândia. O objetivo é impedir que empresas chinesas tenham acesso à tecnologia americana por meio de centros de dados localizados em outros países, contornando as restrições já impostas por Washington. - Terras-raras, espionagem e controle sobre chips: Os temas que vão marcar a cúpula de Trump com Xi nesta semana Desde 2022, os Estados Unidos limitam a venda de chips avançados para a China, exigindo autorizações para a exportação de determinados componentes e equipamentos utilizados em sua fabricação. As regras foram reforçadas em 2023 e agora passam a incluir novas exigências para países considerados pelo governo americano mais suscetíveis ao desvio dessas tecnologias. - Wall Street Journal: Trump deve classificar Nvidia e outras empresas como 'campeãs nacionais' de IA Integrantes do governo brasileiro lembram que houve, anteriormente, preocupação com uma possível falta de chips no mercado internacional, diante do aumento da demanda por equipamentos destinados à inteligência artificial. Essa preocupação, no entanto, é considerada superada. Pelas novas regras, as empresas atingidas precisarão obter licenças do governo americano para importar determinados chips avançados. A regulamentação prevê exceções para companhias sediadas nos Estados Unidos, desde que cumpram exigências de informação, e estabelece que os pedidos de autorização serão analisados individualmente pelas autoridades americanas.

artigo.texto: LOWELL, Mich. — The debate over a potential data center in Lowell Charter Township is continuing, with township leaders now considering new rules for future developments. WATCH: Lowell Township leaders review proposed ordinance for potential data center developments During Monday night's township board meeting, an advisory committee presented a nearly 30-page proposed ordinance outlining requirements developers would have to meet before a data center project could move forward. The proposal received mixed reactions from neighbors. “I think this ordinance has some work to do still,” one neighbor said during public comment. Another neighbor described the proposal as “a great first start.” Tristam Harrington, who has been following the townships data center discussions, said he came into Monday night's meeting skeptical of the proposed ordinance. “We have one chance to get this right because once it goes in, it's over,” Harrington said to the Township Board Monday night. “If we don't put all of the proper and detailed and effective safeguards in place, we have run the real risk of ruining this community forever.” The proposed ordinance would establish requirements for where data centers could be built, how they operate, and what developers must do to protect surrounding communities. That includes addressing concerns such as noise, water consumption, environmental impacts, and emergency response- issues neighbors have raised throughout more than 20 meetings since the project was first announced last November. PREVIOUS COVERAGE: No decision reached after lengthy Lowell Township meeting on Microsoft data center proposal The advisory ordinance committee recommended bringing in third-party consultants to help further develop the proposal and address any remaining gaps. Township Supervisor Jerry Hale agreed with that recommendation. “I think that we do need to hire all the experts to fill in the gaps,” Hale said. After hearing the committee's presentation, Harrington said he came away with a better understanding of the work being done to address neighbors' concerns. “I feel really encouraged by the process and everything that they've done,” Harrington said. “I think we're going to be in a much better position moving forward.” What's next? The proposed ordinance will now go to the Lowell Charter Township Planning Commission for review and recommendations. Township leaders are encouraging members of the advisory committee to participate in that review. “There's still a lot of steps in the process to get to a final ordinance legally,” Township Attorney Bradley Fowler said. After the Planning Commission reviews the proposal, a public hearing will need to be scheduled and held before the ordinance returns to the township board for further consideration. FOX 17 will continue following the township's discussions and provide updates as the process moves forward.

artigo.texto: QUINCY TOWNSHIP, MI (WTVB) – Developers of a proposed battery storage facility in Quincy Township will hold an open house Tuesday to answer community questions, ahead of their application for approval of the project. EDF proposed the Santina Energy facility earlier this year on a 45-acre site in Quincy Township, with about 20 to 25 acres designated for battery equipment. The company says the site on Boone Road was selected partly because it is near ITC transmission lines along the Indiana Northeast Railroad right-of-way. The Bloomington, Minnesota-based company will hold the open house Tuesday from 5:00-7:00 p.m. at Quincy Middle School, with project information and a site plan available for the public to view and comment on. Quincy Township recently adopted new zoning rules and a compatible renewable energy ordinance to maintain local control over projects of this type, limiting battery systems to industrial zones, while EDF proposed an agricultural site. Under state law, EDF could ask the State Public Service Commission to provide approval, regardless of local zoning.

artigo.texto: 36Kr Exclusive | A sodium-ion battery cathode material manufacturer has secured tens of millions of yuan in strategic investment from Jintou Zhiyuan, and its 10,000-ton production line will be put into mass production in Q4. Source / Enterprise This article contains about 3100 words, with an estimated reading time of 8 minutes Author: Ou Xue Editor: Yuan Silai Hard Krypton learned that Nayuan New Materials Technology (Wuxi) Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as "Nayuan New Materials"), a sodium-ion battery cathode material enterprise, has recently completed tens of millions of yuan in Series A financing, with strategic investment from Jintou Zhiyuan. The funds raised in this round will be mainly used for the construction of the advanced battery terminal integrated intelligent manufacturing base in Ma'anshan Economic Development Zone, and support the development of anode-free batteries and overseas market expansion at the same time. Nayuan New Materials was founded in 2022 by a team of German returnee doctors who have deep roots in the battery industry for many years. Dr. Liu Zhongqing, the founder, once worked at the Forschungszentrum Jülich in Germany (Europe's top energy research institution), studied under Martin Winter, academician of the German Academy of Engineering, and has been engaged in the development and research of battery materials and products at the University of Oxford and Schott AG, the global leading advanced materials enterprise based in Germany. Liu Zhongqing believes that the evolution path of sodium-ion battery cathode materials can be summarized into three stages: layered oxides dominated from 2022 to 2023, the industry shifted to NFPP from 2024 to 2025, and NFS will gradually see volume growth starting from 2026. The logic behind this is: Layered oxides share similar processes with ternary lithium batteries, which were easy to industrialize when lithium prices were high in the early stage, but their cost performance disappeared after lithium prices plummeted, and they also have potential safety hazards. NFPP is closer to lithium iron phosphate, with traceable manufacturing processes and application scenarios, so it took the lead in achieving volume growth. NFS has the highest technical difficulty — soft materials produced by low-temperature sintering are prone to absorb water, and are prone to decompose and generate gas under high voltage. At present, Nayuan New Materials has formed two polyanion material systems of NFS (sodium iron sulfate) and NFPP (sodium iron phosphate pyrophosphate), with a supporting recycling material system. According to Hard Krypton, the team of Nayuan New Materials has created the original NFS "soft and hard combination + skeleton building" technology, which solves the technical bottlenecks of single NFS material including low compaction density, poor high-temperature cycle performance and easy gas generation through the "AB material system" composed of hard additives and main materials. For NFPP, the "ultra-fusion synthesis technology" is adopted to greatly reduce the powder resistance of materials and improve material performance. NFS (sodium iron sulfate) material (Source / Enterprise) The company has a clear division of labor for the two materials: NFS is targeted at non-ultra-long cycle scenarios such as consumer electronics, light power, UPS and start-stop in the short term, and forms significant cost advantages at the PACK end with its 3.6V high voltage platform. NFPP is targeted at large-scale energy storage and artificial intelligence AIDC scenarios, focusing on long cycle life and high compaction density. NFPP (composite sodium iron phosphate) material (Source / Enterprise) The company judges that NFS does not contain phosphorus, and its BOM cost is less than 10,000 yuan per ton, while NFPP contains phosphorus element with raw material cost ranging from 15,000 to 18,000 yuan per ton. The raw material price difference between the two is about 10,000 yuan per ton. Besides, NFS is the only material that is not affected by the price fluctuation of lithium iron phosphate. Compared with NFPP, it is more suitable for price-sensitive scenarios such as light power, and can replace the existing lead-acid batteries. At present, the NFS material of Nayuan New Materials has achieved mass production on the 1000-ton pilot verification production line in Jiangxi in 2025, adopting the second-generation spray process. The company is further developing the adaptation scheme of hard additives and AB material system to expand the application boundary of materials. In the field of anode-free batteries, the company has made large investments, advancing from small soft packs below 1Ah in the early stage to the development of large cells at 10Ah and 20Ah levels, and plans to produce a complete battery pack of 6020 or 7220 system for on-board verification by the end of this year. At present, the company is cooperating with Schott AG from Germany (solid-state sodium-ion battery development project). Schott provides solid electrolytes while Nayuan provides cathode materials and anode-free solutions, which gradually promotes the transition of battery technology from pure anode-free liquid state to anode-free semi-solid state and full solid state. Interface optimization and nano solid electrolyte coating are carried out on the cathode side, and SEI interface treatment is carried out on the anode side. It is expected that the density of sodium-ion batteries will be increased to 250-320 Wh/kg in the future, and further applied in emerging scenarios such as vehicles, low-altitude aircraft and robots. At the same time, the company is extending its business to terminal integration. A representative from Nayuan New Materials told Hard Krypton that this extension does not mean the change of its main business. artigo.texto: Demand for data centers continues to put the pedal to the metal, driven in part by artificial intelligence and the need for more computing capacity. But as developers look for places to build, their attention is on rural America rather than traditional tech hubs. Pinion principal Quint Shambaugh says it’s not just about acreage, but access to the infrastructure needed to support these large-scale facilities. “In North America the primary market data center supply reached 10,903 megawatts in the first half of 2026. That is up over 30 percent from the previous year and vacancy, so open spaces in data centers, still remained under 2 percent. So lots of them are getting built. The ones that are getting built are full and then even to add to that, 80 percent of new construction, so construction that isn’t even up and running yet, that capacity is already sold so it is pre-leased. So a data center currently right now that’s not on the market and that’s getting built, 80 percent of it is already pre-leased.” What does it take to power these data centers? The scale and density of newer builds need a lot of energy. “So AI workloads are driving dramatically higher, and power densities are driving dramatically higher, too. With some AI high-density racks consuming as much as 80 to 100 homes amount of electricity. So with one rack in one data center, it can consume that much energy. And the U.S. data center industry is expected to require roughly 30 gigawatts of new power demand annually to support continued AI growth. So when we look at this, really the core issue is power availability and it is really the dominant constraint of this entire industry.” That’s why access to power infrastructure, water, and land is making rural areas attractive. “Rural assets are becoming exceptionally strategic and are something that these companies are very interested in. Site selection increasingly depends on a combination of power access, transmission infrastructure, fiber connectivity, water resources, and land that you can develop on. All these assets are commonly found in rural America as you all know, and developers are pursuing locations beyond traditional areas and traditional hubs because of grid constraint.” But even when all the assets are in place, there are other challenges that impact whether a project moves forward. “Industry studies are consistently showing that delays in power delivery, permitting, or stakeholder alignment can be more impactful than the actual cost of the site itself. So it’s not the land that’s holding people up, it’s the actual communities that are slowing down these projects. As we recently saw in the midterm elections, I think it was 40 out of 41 ballot initiatives went against data centers. So the two biggest constraints right now, number one is power, but number two is community constraints.” As data center development continues to expand, rural areas with the right mix of infrastructure and resources are expected to remain at the center of site selection discussions.

artigo.texto: The development of next-generation electric vehicles, portable electronics, and advanced energy-storage systems calls for lithium metal batteries that combine high energy density with long-term cycling stability. However, conventional lithium metal anodes face two major challenges: producing uniform ultrathin lithium foils at scale and preventing uneven lithium deposition and continuous lithium consumption during battery operation. Addressing both limitations, a research team has developed a screen-printing strategy that integrates patterned lithium arrays with a chemically reinforced interphase. The resulting ultrathin anodes demonstrate promising performance in both liquid- and solid-state lithium metal batteries, offering a practical approach to high-energy-density battery design. Why This Innovation Matters Ultrathin lithium anodes can substantially reduce inactive lithium mass and increase battery energy density. Yet molten lithium spreads poorly on copper substrates, making it difficult to manufacture uniform, defect-free ultrathin foils. During cycling, unstable interphases and non-uniform lithium deposition further accelerate lithium consumption and dendrite formation. These problems become particularly serious when the lithium inventory is limited. Therefore, achieving scalable fabrication while maintaining stable electrode-electrolyte interfaces is essential for practical high-energy-density batteries. Innovative Design and Mechanism The research introduces a mask-assisted screen-printing method that forms regularly distributed lithium microdiscs on copper rather than relying on continuous molten-lithium coating. By controlling the dimensions and spacing of the patterned arrays, the researchers produced anodes with equivalent lithium thicknesses of 10-28 µm, overcoming the limitations imposed by poor lithium wettability. Meanwhile, Mg(TFSI)2 is introduced into molten lithium to generate a multicomponent nanocomposite containing inorganic species such as LiF, Li3N, Li2S, and Li-Mg compounds. These components provide lithiophilic nucleation sites and contribute to an inorganic-rich solid electrolyte interphase. Together, the discrete architecture and modified interphase promote uniform lithium deposition, reduce mechanical stress, and suppress dendrite growth and parasitic reactions. Outstanding Performance The Li@Mg(TFSI)2 array anodes demonstrate excellent electrochemical stability. In liquid-electrolyte full cells paired with LiFePO4 cathodes, the system maintains a specific capacity above 130 mAh g-1 and Coulombic efficiency exceeding 99.8% over 260 cycles. With high-loading cathodes, the anodes also support stable cycling for up to 120 cycles. The calculated stack-level energy densities reach 504 Wh kg-1 and 1071 Wh L-1 for the 20 µm-equivalent anode configuration. Applications and Future Outlook Importantly, this strategy is compatible with both liquid- and solid-state battery systems. In solid-state cells, the spaces between lithium microdiscs accommodate volume changes, while the reinforced interphase helps maintain stable electrode-electrolyte contact. The successful integration of ultrathin lithium arrays with high-loading cathodes highlights the potential of this approach for future high-energy battery technologies. By combining scalable electrode fabrication with interfacial and structural engineering, this work offers a promising route toward more energy-dense and durable lithium metal batteries.

artigo.texto: South Korea will join the Open Coalition of Committed Carbon Markets (OCCCM), a new international cooperation group aimed at enhancing collaboration on mandatory carbon markets, including emissions trading systems. Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment Kim Sung-hwan announced South Korea's official membership in the OCCCM during a high-level meeting at the 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31) held in Antalya, Turkey, on November 16. The carbon market alliance was proposed by Brazil at COP30 last year and officially launched in May this year with participation from major carbon market operators, including the European Union and China. As of November, 13 countries have joined the coalition. Member countries will share experiences in operating mandatory carbon markets, including emissions trading systems and carbon taxes, and discuss measurement, reporting, and verification (MRV), carbon accounting, and the use of high-quality offset mechanisms. Mandatory carbon markets are systems where governments impose a price on greenhouse gas emissions or regulate emission levels, requiring companies to secure emissions allowances or pay carbon taxes based on their emissions. The carbon market alliance adopted operational regulations in May and established a work plan in September. Countries that operate or are preparing to implement national mandatory carbon markets or carbon pricing systems can participate. During the high-level meeting, Minister Kim will highlight that South Korea was the first in East Asia to introduce a national emissions trading system in 2015, currently managing over 70% of the country's greenhouse gas emissions. He will also share experiences in designing and operating the emissions trading market and the MRV system established in a manufacturing-centered industrial structure, as well as the operation of offset mechanisms. Additionally, he will outline the policy direction for transitioning from a fossil fuel-based economy to a 'carbon-free electricity nation' and introduce the 'Korea Green Transformation (K-GX)' strategy announced by the government last month. The high-level meeting will adopt a COP31 declaration welcoming new member countries and committing to develop the carbon market alliance as a central cooperation body for international collaboration on mandatory carbon markets. Member countries will discuss priorities for 2027 and launch a working group to implement the work plan. Minister Kim stated, "Based on the experience gained from operating the emissions trading system for 12 years, we will actively contribute to the activities of the carbon market alliance and continue to play a leading role in advancing global decarbonization and achieving carbon neutrality through international cooperation." * This article has been translated by AI. artigo.texto: The Turkish business sector is embracing global carbon markets by leveraging the UN climate change summit, the 31st Conference of the Parties (COP31), being held in Antalya. The summit serves as a platform for firms and stakeholders to discuss emerging financial regulations and sustainability standards. Alongside the summit, a carbon market conference was hosted by SEKA Investment and financial services firm StoneX. The conference highlighted that mandatory global carbon trading volumes topped $100 billion per year. Serhat Kisakurek, managing partner at SEKA Investment, said the strong attendance by Turkish firms at COP31 showed the sector’s commitment to the new economic ecosystem, despite some uncertainties over initial carbon pricing. Kisakurek noted that carbon compliance has become a key factor in securing long-term deals and accessing affordable financing for corporations. While industrial giants have adapted to green frameworks, small- and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) are lagging behind, he said, urging these firms to follow suit to maintain their global competitive edge. He added that Türkiye has a significant regional advantage in the green transition due to its established climate laws and regulatory infrastructure supporting compliance. Alfredo Nicastro, global director of carbon markets at StoneX, said the summit is connecting private sector innovators with policymakers, while the global turnout at the event continues to demonstrate growing momentum in Türkiye’s green financial sector. He added that COP31 represents a turning point for Türkiye in becoming a central carbon trading hub for the EU and the wider region.

artigo.texto: Ford Starts Michigan Battery Cell Output With CATL-Licensed Technology Cells from the $3 billion plant are shipping for Fathom pickup prototypes. Ford plans to ramp production next year. Ford began battery-cell production in Marshall, Michigan, in October and has started shipping cells for prototypes, a step toward bringing lower-cost lithium iron phosphate batteries into future U.S. vehicles. The shipments are headed to prototypes of the Fathom, Ford’s small electric pickup. The roughly 2 million-square-foot facility represents a $3 billion investment. Ford is in the early stages of certifying its manufacturing processes as it prepares to increase output. The project is part of Ford’s effort to adopt lithium iron phosphate, or LFP, cells for U.S. vehicles. The battery chemistry originated in the United States but was commercialized largely in China. Ford licensed technology and manufacturing support from Chinese battery maker CATL to help establish LFP production more quickly. Alan Clarke, Ford’s vice president of advanced development projects, said the company needs to move quickly to produce affordable electric vehicles in the United States. He described CATL as the best supplier to provide the technology and help Ford learn how to make LFP cells. The Marshall plant is expected to be capable of producing 40 battery cells per minute, equivalent to 20 gigawatt-hours of annual capacity for electric vehicles and energy storage. That is below Ford’s earlier plan for as much as 40 gigawatt-hours a year, amid a pullback in electric-vehicle plans at Ford and across the industry. The facility is highly automated, and Ford says its planned production pace will help reduce battery costs. It also has room to add capacity if needed. The project has drawn criticism from some lawmakers and U.S. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy over Ford’s ties to CATL. In September, Duffy wrote to Ford CEO Jim Farley, expressing concern that the company’s ties to Chinese businesses could harm Ford and the U.S. auto industry. The White House praised Ford’s domestic jobs and manufacturing the following day. Ford plans to ramp up cell production next year. The Fathom pickup is expected to launch in the fourth quarter of 2027.

artigo.texto: During the November 17, 2026, Board of Supervisors meeting, the majority of the Board voted to pause action on legislative data center and electrical substation applications for up to 12 months, the maximum allowed by Virginia law. A previous legal opinion from the Loudoun County Attorney indicated that a moratorium to stop all data center approvals is not legal. The Board made the pause retroactively effective as of September 15. The Board’s reason for considering pausing action on legislative applications is to allow time for the county to complete the ongoing review of current data center policies and regulations. The project proposes amendments to the Loudoun County 2019 Comprehensive Plan and Loudoun County Zoning Ordinance pertaining to data center standards and locations. Amendments to the comprehensive plan and zoning ordinance have the potential to impact existing and new legislative applications for data centers. That project is expected to wrap up in the summer of 2027. The Board’s pause will end when the Board adopts comprehensive plan and zoning ordinance amendments as part of the Data Center Standards and Locations project. Under the terms of the pause, the Board's final votes on data center and substation applications would be deferred for up to one year. Virginia law requires action on such legislative applications within one year. The one-year period begins at the time applications are first submitted to the Planning Commission. During the Board’s pause, developers may continue to submit applications that propose or would allow for data center and substation uses. County staff will continue to review applications and schedule the Planning Commission’s public hearing; however, the Board’s intent is to pause any Board of Supervisors public hearings and Board votes on such applications until after the Data Center Standards and Locations project is complete. The pause would not cause any applications to become inactive. The Board’s action has the potential to impact 33 legislative applications that are currently active. The Board may consider exceptions to the pause for legislative applications that involve electric grid reliability or if the statutory period for a decision is about to expire. The action does not apply to legislative applications for properties located within the Route 28 Tax District. The Board’s action does not impact applications that are subject to administrative processes. The Board previously approved an end to by-right data center development, requiring all data center projects to come before the Board for a vote through the county’s special exception process. More information about the Board’s adopted resolution on pausing action on legislative applications for data centers and substations is available in the Board’s November 17 staff report. Additional information about data centers is available on Loudoun County’s website online at loudoun.gov/DataCenters and information about various transmission line initiatives is available at loudoun.gov/TransmissionLines. # # #

artigo.texto: Quick summary - Hundreds rallied at the state Capitol Wednesday for passage of the POWER Act, which would regulate data centers. - The bill’s Senate sponsor said the bill is a “big solution” for a “big problem.” - The legislation would, among other things, require big tech companies to pay for the energy used to power giant data centers. SPRINGFIELD — Hundreds of residents and environmental advocates rallied at the state Capitol Wednesday to urge lawmakers to regulate data centers. The residents came via bus, car and Amtrak from around the state to call for passage of the POWER Act, a bill that would require data centers to pay to create the energy they consume, mandate transparency around water use, limit noise levels and diesel generator use, ensure local community benefit agreements, and more. The bill failed to progress during the spring legislative session, but advocates hope to see it passed during the veto session. “Illinoisans are tired of fighting alone for basic protections without help from the state legislature,” said Lori McKiernan, a Springfield community organizer and Sierra Club member. “Time is up. Our legislators must take action on data centers.” Over the summer break, lawmakers have been meeting with environmental advocates, organized labor and representatives of the data center industry to negotiate the details. The Senate Energy and Public Utilities Committee was set to hold a hearing on the POWER Act at 4:30 p.m. Wednesday. Sen. Ram Villivalam, D-Chicago, is the lead sponsor of the Senate bill. He called the roughly 1,000-page bill a “big solution” for a “big problem,” and described the legislation as the “most comprehensive data center legislation in the nation.” “You’re here because this matters,” Villivalam told the crowd. “When something affects your families, your homes, your neighbors, and of course our bills, your voices deserve to be heard.” Battling big tech Data centers have existed for years in Illinois, housing servers and hardware that store data and power the digital world, supporting email, video streaming and other web services. But in recent years, as major technology firms race to create generative artificial intelligence, they have begun to build hyperscale data centers — massive buildings and campuses that sometimes consume the energy of a small city. Their actual and projected energy consumption have driven up energy costs for regular residents and small businesses. The rally comes shortly after the release of two reports from state agencies proposed delaying the planned closures of 11 fossil fuel plants, as required under the state’s landmark energy bill, in order to guarantee enough energy supply to meet the growing demand. But environmental advocates don’t want to see the state’s landmark climate goals delayed to power hyperscale data centers. “Big tech, they’re counting on us to be intimidated by their big money. They’re counting on us to be overwhelmed by the fight in front of us,” Illinois Environmental Council organizer Cate Caldwell said at the rally. “But as I look at this crowd today, I think big tech should be intimidated by us.” There won’t be a vote this week, but lawmakers could take up the issue when they return for their final days of the veto session next month. artigo.texto: Hithium has signed a memorandum of understanding with the University of Cambridge to collaborate on long-duration energy storage research, battery technology and the commercialisation of academic work. The agreement was signed during the Global Energy Storage Colloquium in Xiamen, China, on 12 November. Hithium said the partnership will combine Cambridge’s work in materials science, engineering and fundamental research with its own experience in battery development, long-duration energy storage and large-scale deployment. The two organisations plan to establish joint management and research mechanisms, develop research projects, facilitate scientific exchanges and support the translation of research into industrial applications. Hithium said Cambridge researchers will contribute to work on fundamental scientific questions and emerging energy storage technologies, while the manufacturer will provide engineering validation and industrial application scenarios. No individual research programmes, funding commitments or development timescales were disclosed. The partnership comes as Hithium expands its focus on lithium iron phosphate batteries designed for longer-duration stationary storage. BESTmag reported in August that Hithium began production at its $1.8 billion LFP long-duration energy storage manufacturing park in Shandong. The 80-hectare development includes battery cells, modules and complete storage systems alongside materials and upstream processing. The company’s current LDES strategy includes large-format LFP cells intended for discharge durations of four to eight hours. Hithium was also ranked as the world’s second-largest supplier of BESS cells in the first half of 2026, behind CATL. Hithium and Cambridge strengthening bridge from research to deployment Hithium and Cambridge said the collaboration is intended to strengthen links between fundamental battery research, product development and industrial deployment. The agreement also forms part of Hithium’s plans to expand its international research network through partnerships with universities and research institutions. The Xiamen colloquium at which the agreement was signed brought together researchers and industry representatives to discuss battery materials, degradation and lifetime prediction, grid integration, power electronics, thermal-runaway detection and virtual power plants. Hithium said it intends to use the collaboration to bring technical challenges encountered in commercial energy storage projects into academic research, while accelerating the engineering validation of research findings. artigo.texto: [Ibase Gaming FY2026 Q3 Earnings Call] First Three Quarters Revenue Only NT$98.73 Million, Loss of NT$4.54 Per Share — Taiwan's Ibase Gaming Bets on ASEAN 20MW Energy Storage and AI Optical Communications for 2027 Transformation Taiwan's Ibase Gaming (6441.TW) has fallen into a slump. In an online earnings call on November 18, the company reported financial results for the first three quarters of 2026: cumulative revenue of just NT$98.73 million (approximately $3.0 million), less than half of the NT$235 million (approximately $7.1 million) posted for all of 2025 and a steep decline from NT$540 million (approximately $16.4 million) for all of 2024. Cumulative gross loss reached NT$105 million (approximately $3.2 million), with after-tax net loss of NT$242 million (approximately $7.3 million) and a loss per share of NT$4.54. This marks the second consecutive year of losses for Ibase Gaming, with no sign of the losses narrowing. "This has indeed been a challenging year for Ibase Gaming," Liao Yi-chung, special assistant to the chairman, said in his opening remarks, acknowledging that the company faces short-term operating pressure while also building the foundation for its next phase of growth. Financial Highlights at a Glance Three Headwinds Combine to Turn Gross Margin Negative Liao attributed this year's weak performance to three factors. First, demand in the U.S. unregulated gaming market has been weak, contracting at least 40% to 50% this year, with customers adjusting both procurement volumes and schedules. Second, existing products are gradually reaching the end of their life cycles, while the next-generation Gaming PC platform still requires customer testing, system integration and validation; during the transition between old and new products, mass-production ramp-up has fallen short of expectations. Third, revenue has fallen rapidly, but fixed operating costs cannot be reduced proportionally in a short period, dealing a severe blow to gross margin and operating profit. "When revenue falls rapidly, existing fixed operating costs cannot be adjusted in tandem, which relatively increases the cost burden," Liao explained. The financial statements show that Ibase Gaming's gross margin for the first three quarters of 2026 was -107%, a marked deterioration from -10% for all of 2025 and far worse than the positive 21% gross margin in 2024. It is worth noting that although cumulative revenue for the first three quarters fell sharply year over year, monthly revenue disclosures show that third-quarter 2026 revenue was about NT$60 million (approximately $1.8 million), up 25.3% from the same period in 2025, indicating that the revenue decline was concentrated mainly in the first half. October revenue of NT$30 million (approximately $910,000) was up 456.3% year over year, also hinting at a recovery from a low base. Still, cumulative revenue for the first three quarters was only NT$98.73 million, and returning to 2025 levels for the full year will remain difficult. Short-Term Debt-Servicing Capacity Flashes Warning Signs Amid the operating losses, Ibase Gaming's financial structure has also deteriorated. As of the third quarter of 2026, total assets had fallen to NT$1.563 billion (approximately $47.5 million), while total liabilities climbed to NT$760 million (approximately $23.1 million), raising the liabilities-to-total-assets ratio from 31% at the end of 2024 to 48%; shareholders' equity fell to NT$803 million (approximately $24.4 million). The current ratio plunged from 150.52% at the end of 2024 to 80.56%, while the quick ratio dropped from 80.71% to 31.90%. "This reflects that the company is indeed facing some management pressure on working capital and short-term liquidity," Liao acknowledged. Going forward, in addition to improving revenue and profitability, the company will place greater emphasis on the efficiency of capital deployment, including inventory management, project payment terms and control of accounts-receivable cash flow. New Businesses Emerge as Bright Spots: ASEAN 20MW Energy Storage and AI Optical Communications Orders Secured Despite the weak core business, Ibase Gaming delivered tangible results in its new business initiatives, providing one of the few bright spots at the earnings call. In the energy business, the company secured an ASEAN 20MW industrial energy storage project this year, extending from pure equipment supply to site demand analysis, project planning and third-party vendor integration — an important milestone in entering large-scale energy storage system integration. In AI optical communications, Ibase Gaming established Guangchi Technology in 2026 to enter bonding and assembly contract manufacturing for silicon photonics thermal components, and has already won orders from a major U.S. client. Liao said this business "is no longer just an early-stage technology deployment, but has begun to enter the stage of actual manufacturing and commercialization," adding that the company is actively expanding capacity and plans to extend into the assembly and testing of finished high-speed optical communications modules. In addition, Ibase Gaming is advancing a modular AI computing center (AIDC) solution that integrates AI servers, energy storage, power management and cooling systems, and is currently in talks with several potential clients. Liao, however, was cautious about this business, stressing that project amounts are usually high and that the company "will certainly be prudent and then some." Three Directions for 2027 in a Push to Return to Profit Looking ahead to 2027, Liao outlined three operating directions: improving business commercialization efficiency, improving the operating profit structure, and strengthening cash flow management. artigo.texto: Here’s What’s Next for Missoula Data Centers Missoula County is moving closer to stricter rules on data centers. But it could be another year before permanent rules are in place. Last week, county commissioners accepted a new staff report finding that data centers have "very real impacts" on public health, safety, and the environment. The report names more than a dozen potential concerns, including those brought up in public hearings, such as noise, water use, and climate change. That vote gives staff the go-ahead to begin working on permanent rules, although there could still be some delays in the process outside the county's control. Eye on the Legislature The report also raised the question of whether Montana's "Right to Compute Act" could override any local zoning policies, with staff suggesting it could be best to wait until after the Legislative session to see if there's a change in state law. That may mean the county could have to extend the current moratorium on data centers for an additional year. "No gap" promise for data center controls Commissioner Dave Strohmaier promises the county will keep the situation under control until a final policy is in place. "To give folks some level of comfort, there will be no gap," Strohmaier said in support of the motion. "Either we have permanent zoning in place by the end of this moratorium period or the more likely case in a separate action, from today is that we will extend the moratorium. So again, there will be no gap." READ MORE: Missoula County Considers Data Center Zoning Advocates are also urging commissioners to push state regulators to ensure data centers, not residential ratepayers, cover the cost of their massive power and transmission demands. And the county says it intends to play a role in power rate setting by the Montana Public Service Commission. 5 Montana Towns Companies Are Targeting For New AI Data Centers Gallery Credit: Chris

artigo.texto: Os sistemas de armazenamento de energia em baterias têm ampliado sua gama de aplicações no setor elétrico. No Brasil, um dos exemplos mais recentes é o da Agropecuária Larssen, no oeste do Paraná, na qual a Weg implantou, em parceria com a integradora Lenz, dois sistemas BESS associados à geração fotovoltaica. A principal instalação utiliza um sistema BSCW400, da WEG, com 300 kW de potência e 645 kWh de capacidade de armazenamento, conectado a uma usina fotovoltaica de 300 kW. O equipamento atende uma granja com capacidade para produzir 70 mil ovos por dia, cuja continuidade do fornecimento de energia é particularmente importante. Em caso de falha na rede, o BESS assume as cargas em aproximadamente 40 milissegundos, evitando uma interrupção perceptível na operação. O segundo sistema tem 100 kW de potência e 215 kWh de capacidade. Juntos, os dois sistemas somam 400 kW de potência e 860 kWh de armazenamento. Além de funcionar como fonte de emergência e backup das instalações, a bateria pode ser carregada com energia solar nos períodos de menor tarifa e utilizada posteriormente no horário de ponta, reduzindo a necessidade de compra de eletricidade mais cara da rede. Outra aplicação está em Uberlândia (MG), na qual a BYD forneceu baterias para um projeto desenvolvido pela Cemig em parceria com a Alsol Energia Renováveis. O sistema tem 1,26 MVA de potência máxima e 1,36 MWh de capacidade de armazenamento e opera integrado a uma usina fotovoltaica. Diferente da aplicação na Agropecuária Larssen, em Uberlândia o BESS atua junto à geração fotovoltaica para mitigar a intermitência da fonte renovável. A solução usa baterias LiFePO4 da BYD para armazenar energia solar e liberá-la posteriormente, aumentando a flexibilidade e deslocando o consumo para momentos mais adequados. Essa capacidade aumenta a flexibilidade do sistema elétrico e pode facilitar a integração de fontes variáveis, como solar e eólica, ao aproximar a oferta de energia do perfil de consumo. Em uma escala maior, a ABB participou do desenvolvimento de um BESS da Universal Power Solutions Inc. (UPSI), em Limay, na província de Bataan, nas Filipinas. O empreendimento tem potência de 50 MW capacidade e foi projetado para reforçar a confiabilidade e a estabilidade da rede elétrica. Nesse caso, o papel da bateria é diferente. Em vez de atender principalmente a um consumidor individual ou armazenar a energia de uma usina solar, o sistema funciona como infraestrutura de suporte à rede, podendo armazenar energia e disponibilizá-la em momentos de maior necessidade. A solução fornecida pela ABB utiliza arquitetura modular e pré-engenheirada, com sistemas de baterias, gerenciamento de energia, inversores, transformadores,equipamentos de média tensão e proteção e controle. A expansão das aplicações também vem acompanhada de novos modelos de negócio. Além da venda tradicional, a empresa oferece o modelo BESS-as-a-Service, assumindo projeto, instalação, comissionamento e manutenção, enquanto o cliente paga pelo serviço. A proposta busca reduzir a barreira do investimento inicial e permitir que empresas utilizem o armazenamento para reduzir custos de energia, gerenciar picos de demanda, aumentar a resiliência do fornecimento e aproveitar melhor a geração renovável.

artigo.texto: Israel risks becoming a pollution haven in the global race to build AI data centers As the Electricity Authority opens the door to another 1,000MW of data center capacity, the Environmental Protection Ministry warns of rising emissions, health costs and pressure on the country's natural gas reserves. The Electricity Authority has announced plans to position Israel as a global leader in connecting data centers to the power grid. But a senior official at the Ministry of Environmental Protection is warning of significant consequences. "Air pollutant emissions will rise by more than 10% once data centers with a capacity of 3,000 megawatts are established, causing economic damage through increased morbidity and mortality, lost workdays and other costs," she said. The ministry estimates that Israel’s rapid push to establish data centers will cause approximately NIS 2 billion in annual economic damage from the additional electricity generation they require, plus more than NIS 1 billion from the operation of backup generators. The anticipated costs also include higher greenhouse gas emissions and faster depletion of Israel’s natural gas reserves. Beyond the financial damage, the ministry warns of an increase in annual deaths caused by air pollution, which is already responsible for an estimated 5,500 premature deaths in Israel each year. AI is reshaping the global energy landscape, as major technology companies race to build massive data centers around the world. According to the latest forecast from the International Energy Agency (IEA), electricity consumption by data centers is expected to nearly double, from 485 terawatt-hours in 2025 to 950 TWh in 2030, accounting for approximately 3% of global electricity consumption. Over the same period, electricity consumption by data centers dedicated to artificial intelligence is expected to triple. For comparison, 950 TWh is slightly more than Japan’s current annual electricity consumption. In the United States, data centers are expected to account for nearly half of the projected growth in electricity demand through 2030. Local communities are increasingly bearing the costs of this technological expansion, including higher air pollution from facilities that operate polluting backup generators, consume vast amounts of electricity and require large quantities of water for cooling. Data centers are also affecting electricity prices. According to the Federal Reserve, wholesale electricity prices rose by 6.9% last year, driven in part by demand from these facilities. Opposition to data center developments is growing in communities around the world, where residents are also concerned about the large tracts of land these facilities occupy. In the United States, the issue even influenced this month's midterm elections. A September poll by Quinnipiac found that nearly three out of four Americans opposed having a data center in their community. During the elections, 41 ballot measures concerning data centers were put to a vote, with voters rejecting the proposed developments in all but one case. In an NBC exit poll, 23% of voters said data centers were a "decisive" factor in their congressional vote, while another 33% described them as a "significant" factor. The day after the election, Nvidia lost $450 billion in market value. OpenAI has since pledged to use closed-loop cooling systems and to pay for the electricity consumed by its data centers. It has also moved to rebrand its facilities as "computing campuses." In July, the Electricity Authority froze the processing of grid connection requests for data centers with electricity demands exceeding eight megawatts, after approving 2,000MW of capacity. Developers had submitted requests totaling 27,000MW, roughly three times Israel's current electricity consumption and well above the country's record peak demand. The authority recently announced plans to release an additional 1,000MW of capacity, potentially enabling the construction of facilities as large as 200MW, a scale not yet seen elsewhere in the world. "Realizing this allocation is expected to result in data centers accounting for approximately 20% of national electricity consumption, positioning Israel among the world's leaders in the integration of data centers relative to total consumption," the Electricity Authority said. Opening the door to these large facilities is expected to require the construction of at least three new polluting power plants in Israel to meet their electricity needs. But alongside the potential economic benefits, the expansion carries significant environmental and public-health costs that will ultimately be borne by Israeli residents. The concern is that, at a time when communities in other countries are increasingly resisting data center developments, Israel could become a "backyard" for the sector's pollution. In a sharply worded letter, Shuli Nazar, Deputy Director General for Environmental Regulation and Risk Prevention at the Ministry of Environmental Protection, warned of a broad range of risks. In addition to increased air pollution and the resulting rise in morbidity and mortality, she said, higher greenhouse gas emissions would make it harder for Israel to meet its climate targets. According to Nazar, offsetting the additional emissions from data centers would require Israel to set a target of approximately 45% renewable energy by 2035, about 10 percentage points higher than the target recommended by the Electricity Authority. There is considerable skepticism within the energy sector about whether Israel can meet even its existing renewable energy targets. Nazar also warned that implementing the Electricity Authority's plan would accelerate the depletion of Israel's domestic natural gas reserves and shorten their expected lifespan. artigo.texto: Mintech will jointly develop diagnostic equipment with Terra Leader for use in solid-state battery manufacturing processes. Mintech said on Nov. 17 that it signed a memorandum of understanding (MOU) with Terra Leader, a company specializing in digital pressure control, to develop and commercialize diagnostic solutions for solid-state battery manufacturing. The two companies will combine Mintech's electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) technology with Terra Leader's precision pressure-control technology. EIS analyzes internal battery resistance to assess battery condition and performance. Solid-state batteries use solid electrolytes instead of liquid electrolytes, making the contact condition between electrodes and electrolytes an important factor affecting performance. Technologies that maintain uniform pressure during manufacturing and precisely analyze the condition of electrode-electrolyte interfaces are therefore critical. The companies plan to develop an integrated solution that performs temperature and pressure control alongside electrochemical analysis in a single piece of equipment. The goal is to improve manufacturing efficiency and measurement reproducibility by analyzing battery cells without transferring them to separate equipment, while maintaining their manufacturing conditions. Mintech plans to expand its battery diagnostics business, which has primarily focused on lithium-ion batteries, into the solid-state battery sector. It will pursue commercialization targeting global battery manufacturers and materials companies.

artigo.texto: POSCO Group has signed a long-term lithium supply agreement with Chinese battery manufacturer CATL. POSCO Group said on November 18 that it had signed a contract to supply lithium to CATL over three years, from 2026 through 2028. The company did not disclose the supply volume or contract value, citing a non-disclosure agreement (NDA) with the customer. Deliveries under the contract have already begun. CATL holds approximately 40% of the global electric vehicle battery market and supplies batteries to major automakers worldwide. The long-term agreement gives POSCO Group a stable customer base in China, the world’s largest electric vehicle battery market. POSCO Group has expanded its customer base in China from battery materials producers to battery cell manufacturers. In August, the group also agreed to cooperate on lithium supply with Ronbay Technology, China’s largest producer of ternary cathode materials. The companies agreed to collaborate on supplying lithium produced from ore and brine, as well as recycled lithium recovered from spent batteries. POSCO Group is also expanding its lithium production capacity. POSCO Holdings completed the upstream processing facilities at its second brine-based lithium plant in Argentina in October. Including its first plant, the group’s annual production capacity in the country has increased to 48,000 metric tons. The company plans to complete downstream processing facilities at the Yulchon Industrial Complex in South Jeolla Province in 2027 to convert lithium carbonate into battery-grade lithium hydroxide. Lithium is a core business under POSCO Group’s “Triple Core” strategy announced in July. The group plans to establish annual lithium production capacity of 173,000 metric tons by 2033 and generate more than 1.8 trillion won in operating profit from its lithium business by 2035.

artigo.texto: Enlight and Shemen join race for Israeli data centers with 150MW Haifa project The companies plan to invest in a facility at Hof Shemen, with a NIS 334 million electricity guarantee and a 25-year land lease. The project enters a crowded market as developers compete for the remaining 1,000MW of capacity earmarked for data centers. New names are joining the growing list of entrepreneurs seeking to establish data centers in Israel. Enlight and Shemen Real Estate announced this morning that they have signed an agreement to develop a 150-megawatt data center at Hof Shemen in Haifa. The two companies will jointly establish a special-purpose vehicle (SPV) for the project and have already submitted an application to connect the facility to the electricity grid. Under the Electricity Authority’s regulatory framework, applicants must provide financial guarantees to secure grid connections. The guarantee required for the project is estimated at NIS 334 million, which the two companies will fund in equal shares. The data center is planned to cover between 41 and 82 dunams. The project’s SPV will lease the land from Shemen for 25 years. Annual lease payments will start at NIS 27,000 per dunam during the development phase, gradually rising to NIS 433,000 per dunam once the data center becomes operational. Enlight has also secured an option to purchase 50% of the land designated for the data center at a minimum price of NIS 6.32 million per dunam. The price may increase under a pre-agreed mechanism, and the option can be exercised 30 months after the agreement was signed. Enlight and Shemen are joining a growing field of developers competing for approximately 1,000 megawatts of additional electricity capacity earmarked for data centers. Under the regulatory framework published by the Electricity Authority, up to 20% of Israel’s national electricity supply, equivalent to approximately 3,000 MW, is expected to be allocated to data centers by 2030. Of that amount, approximately 2,000 MW is accounted for by connection requests that have already been approved. The remaining 1,000 MW has become the focus of intense competition among developers seeking to build data centers. For Enlight, a renewable energy company, this is not its first investment in an Israeli data center. In March 2025, it won a tender issued by the Israel Land Authority to build a data center alongside a solar energy facility in Ashalim, in the Negev. Shemen Yielding Real Estate is the successor to Shemen Industries, a company previously engaged in oil production. It is held by Memorandum, a company owned by Haim Fink (44.2%); Zvika Ben-Zvi (22.1%), who also owns logistics company Orsher; and real estate investment fund JTLV3 (22.1%).

artigo.texto: South Korea Joins 'Open Coalition on Compliance Carbon Markets' as New Member International carbon market partnership South Korea to take part in talks on setting rules Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment Kim Seonghwan is being interviewed by The Asia Business Daily at the Han River Flood Control Office in Dongjak-gu, Seoul. 2026.9.21 Photo by Kim Hyunmin View original image South Korea has officially joined the Open Coalition on Compliance Carbon Markets (OCCCM), an international partnership on carbon markets involving the European Union (EU), China and other participants. As a new member, South Korea has secured voting rights at the coalition's high-level meetings and will take part in discussions on international carbon market rules, including Internationally Transferred Mitigation Outcomes and offset credits. Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment Kim Seonghwan officially announced South Korea's membership at a high-level meeting of the coalition held on the sidelines of the 31st Conference of the Parties to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (COP31) in Antalya, Türkiye, on the 16th. The coalition is an international partnership that shares experience with compliance carbon markets, such as greenhouse gas emissions trading systems and carbon taxes, and promotes mutual understanding and cooperation among its members on topics including measurement, reporting and verification (MRV), carbon accounting and high-quality offset systems. Brazil proposed the coalition at COP30 last year, and it was launched in May this year with major carbon market operators, including the EU and China, as its core participants. Thirteen countries are currently members. South Korea joined after receiving an invitation from the EU in June, as a follow-up to Korea-EU summit diplomacy. To become a member, a country or regional economic integration organization must have or be developing a domestic compliance carbon market or carbon pricing system. Members can exercise voting rights at high-level meetings. With its membership, South Korea will be able to participate in future discussions on international carbon market rules, including the generation of Internationally Transferred Mitigation Outcomes (ITMOs) under Article 6 of the Paris Agreement and the establishment of common principles for high-integrity offset credits. artigo.texto: PIERCE TOWNSHIP, OH. — The halls of the Pierce Township Center overflowed with residents looking to listen and participate in a conversation on the future of data centers in their community. After getting through all the other agenda items, trustees were able to discuss the final two motions. Both were written by Trustee Allen Freeman, who explained the action the trustees would take. "We've pushed it back to the zoning commission with more definition of what we want to try to see. And what that is, is that we've asked them to give us changes to our code that would prohibit data centers inside of Pierce Township. The second motion does the same thing; it just prohibits small nuclear power plants," Freeman said to me after Wednesday's meeting. After the first motion passed, Freeman explained to residents that this is only a first step. “This is the beginning step of the process; this is not the end, this is the beginning. So, it clarifies what we want the zoning commission to go and do," Freeman said. Watch to see the data center decisions made by Pierce Township Trustees Wednesday night: Data centers have been the subject of many township discussions in just the last few months. “I want to help the zoning committee, and I want to help you all with the ability to show that the property that has been proposed for a data center is not appropriate," Pierce Township Resident Lisa Harris Hollister said Wednesday night. The resident was referring to a San Francisco-based company that proposed a 300-megawatt data center in Pierce Township earlier this year. A Crane Data Centers representative presented to the Pierce Township Zoning Commission on Sept. 1. The project includes three 200,000-to-300,000-square-foot buildings on 300 acres of wooded hillside across the street from the now-closed Walter C. Beckjord Generating Station. Pierce Township has a moratorium on data center construction through May 31, 2027. On Oct. 6, the zoning commission met at the Locust Corner Elementary School gymnasium. Several residents shared their concerns regarding data centers in Pierce Township with the commission. After the meeting, resident Kathy Cummins spoke with me about why she thinks a data center isn't right for that space. “This particular site that we're talking about is already a polluted site," Cummins said. And her worries stretch beyond that. “Environmental, it's noise, pollution, you name it," Cummins said. One resident did stand behind data centers. “I don’t think it’s right. I don’t think it’s a good idea to just ban something," he said. Freeman's original motion had a 250 megawatts or greater threshold written, but he removed that number and changed his motion during Wednesday's meeting. The trustee explained to me why he made that change. "There are data centers, there are the commercial-type data centers that are used by hospitals and banks and others, and we don't really want to eliminate those. Those have been around for 50 years or more, so we don't really want to work through those. But it's really the hyperscale that we want to really focus on and those are the ones we would like to have prohibited from Pierce Township. They just don't fit into the character of the township," Freeman said. Freeman explained what the next step will look like. "The zoning commission is going to have a December meeting. So, during that meeting, they'll start to organize around, as they've already said to me before they left, they'd like to have a consultant on board, so that's going to start to have that discussion of how we're going to go about doing that," Freeman said. The next zoning commission meeting is Dec. 1, and the next board of trustees meeting is Dec. 9.

artigo.texto: Restrição para chips de data centers: EUA ainda têm a melhor tecnologia; entenda Governo de Donald Trump está preocupado em manter vantagem na disputa tecnológica com o país asiático O governo dos Estados Unidos decidiu restringir exportações de chips e servidores usados na infraestrutura de processamento de dados para sistemas de inteligência artificial (IA) para empreendimentos em países que possam fornecer capacidade de computação para empresas chinesas, mesmo fora da China, como os componentes fabricados pela Nvidia. A nova norma coloca o Brasil, ao lado de Indonésia, Malásia, Tailândia e Cingapura, na mira das restrições, informou em comunicado o Departamento de Comércio dos Estados Unidos. - Terras-raras, espionagem e controle sobre chips: os temas que vão marcar a cúpula de Trump com Xi nesta semana - Após decisão dos EUA: Governo Lula avalia contestar restrições dos EUA à venda de chips para data centers no Brasil O aperto na restrição busca impedir que a China tenha acesso à capacidade computacional que utilize processadores projetados por empresas americanas mas esteja instalada em terceiros países. Mas qual é o objetivo do governo de Donald Trump? Embora temam o avanço da China na produção de chips de inteligência artificial (IA), os Estados Unidos mantêm ampla vantagem sobre os rivais. Segundo a consultoria Epoch AI, o Ascend 950, principal chip da Huawei, entrega performance equivalente à metade do que entregam os chips H100, da Nvidia, que foram lançados em 2022 — atualmente, a companhia fundada por Jensen Huang já comercializa o H200. A consultoria afirma que a gigante chinesa deve permanecer entre três e quatro anos atrás da Nvidia até, pelo menos, 2030. - 'Certamente não é uma má ideia': Trump defende volta de Huang ao comando da Nvidia Em agosto do ano passado, a DeepSeek tentou treinar a segunda geração de seu grande modelo, o DeepSeek 2, com chips Ascend 950, o que gerou atrasos no projeto. Um ano depois, a Z.ai surpreendeu ao afirmar que, durante o período de testes do GLM 5.3, usou apenas chips chineses para gerar as respostas do modelo, o que foi um sinal de avanço moderado, já que a chamada “inferência” é uma tarefa menos custosa para os chips do que o treinamento de modelos. Os chineses enfrentam alguns gargalos. Um deles é a limitação da high bandwidth memory (HBM, ou memória de alta largura de banda), usada nos chips de IA. A Epoch estima que, se a Huawei usasse somente HBMs feitos na China, atingiria apenas 1% da capacidade de produção de poder computacional da Nvidia. Além disso, a China não tem equipamento especializado para produzir chips de alto rendimento — a holandesa ASML tem o domínio global de máquinas de fotolitografia para a indústria de semicondutores e nunca exportou para a China. Em outubro, uma startup chinesa apresentou um maquinário do tipo, mas analistas estimam que o país está pelo menos uma década atrasado no segmento. Ainda não é possível avaliar o impacto no Brasil da decisão dos EUA de exigir que operadoras de data centers de cinco países obtenham licença prévia para comprar chips avançados de IA — governo, empresas e entidades admitem que preferem esperar para compreender esse movimento. No entanto, há um entendimento de que a determinação do governo Donald Trump cria diferenças competitivas entre as empresas isentas de licença, como as americanas, e as demais. Isso poderia abalar os planos do governo Lula de conquistar a soberania digital, pois as companhias brasileiras terão de se sujeitar às regras. Foi uma reação parecida à de janeiro de 2025, quando Joe Biden, em final de mandato, restringiu o acesso a chips de computador e tecnologias para desenvolvimento de IA. Na época, o Brasil foi enquadrado no grupo dois, sujeito a controles intermediários de acesso à tecnologia. As cotas impediam que as empresas desses países importassem mais de 1,7 mil GPUs de ponta por ano. Assim que tomou posse, Trump revogou a regra.

artigo.texto: Key Takeaways - BYD started in a rented factory in Shenzhen and entered the auto industry through an acquisition in 2003. - BYD has produced more than 19 million NEVs, and its exports rose 93.75% year-on-year in the first 10 months of 2026. BYD (HKEX: 1211) marked its 32nd anniversary on Wednesday with a look back at how it grew from a battery maker in Shenzhen into an automaker with factories in Thailand and Brazil. In its anniversary article, BYD traced its origins to November 18, 1994, when more than 20 people started the business in a rented factory in Shenzhen. The company entered the lithium-ion battery industry in 1996. In 2003, BYD entered the auto industry by acquiring Xi'an Qinchuan Automobile. It launched its first mass-produced car, the F3, in 2005, followed by the F3DM plug-in hybrid sedan in 2008. BYD then expanded into commercial vehicles. It entered the new energy bus market in 2009 and built an electric bus factory in Lancaster, California, in 2013. In 2015, BYD unveiled a strategy covering the entire new energy vehicle (NEV) supply chain and a range of markets. It broadened its electrification efforts beyond passenger cars, buses and taxis to include logistics, ports and mining. As NEV output rose, BYD began building passenger cars overseas. Its 5-millionth NEV rolled off the production line in August 2023. In 2024, BYD completed its first overseas passenger car factory in Rayong, Thailand, where it produced its 8-millionth NEV. On November 18 that year, cumulative NEV production reached 10 million vehicles. BYD began production at its Brazilian factory in 2025, and its 14-millionth NEV rolled off the line there. All 8 of the company's roll-on/roll-off car carriers entered service that year. Earlier this month, BYD announced that its 19-millionth NEV had rolled off the production line, 124 days after it produced its 17-millionth. Chairman and president Wang Chuanfu said on Tuesday at the APEC CEO Summit in Shenzhen that BYD had produced more than 19 million NEVs in total. Wang said BYD's Thai factory can produce 150,000 vehicles a year and employs about 6,000 people, more than 95% of them local hires. The company also plans to expand local sourcing and research and development in its overseas markets. BYD exported 1,513,154 NEVs in the first 10 months of 2026, up 93.75% year-on-year. Over the same period, its sales in China fell 27.81% to 2,108,590 vehicles, while global sales declined 2.16% to 3,621,744 vehicles. In March, BYD unveiled its second-generation Blade Battery and new flash charging technology. According to the company, the technology can charge a battery from 10% to 70% in 5 minutes and from 10% to 97% in 9 minutes.
