artigo.texto: The Duxbury Planning Board is looking to offer next year’s Town Meeting up to six new or updated zoning laws, including regulations for battery energy storage systems, members announced this week. On Monday at the Selectboard’s meeting at Town Hall, Planning Board Chairwoman Kristin Rappe said members of her committee had been meeting weekly to ready the zoning alterations for the March 13, 2027 Town Meeting. One of the more consequential proposals is a new bylaw to regulate battery energy storage systems. Known as BESS, these systems use lithium-ion batteries to store electricity, most often produced from renewable sources, and release it to the power grid when the energy is needed during peak usage hours. In Duxbury, a plan to put a BESS on residentially zoned land on West Street last year caused an uproar with hundreds of residents objecting to it. Proponents did not move forward with that project, but the experience showed the Planning Board that it needed to find a way to regulate BESS, since the state’s clean energy regulations require the town to address these systems. While the town can’t prohibit BESS in Duxbury, it can pass a law that sets town standards to protect the health and safety of residents, said Rappe. Passing regulations does not mean the town is welcoming these systems, said Selectboard member Brian Glennon. The proposed bylaw would establish regulations for siting a BESS on land in town. These include setbacks and screening required for when the system is built, safety mechanisms for when it is running and a decommissioning and financial surety for when it would no longer be in service. Many battery energy storage systems are large and take up multiple acres. One of the newest and the largest is in Medway and was completed this year. That site is 10.6 acres with the BESS taking up 5.2 acres and producing 250 MW, according to the state Department of Public Utilities. Duxbury’s proposed BESS zoning law could limit these systems to lots that are at least 250,000 square feet, or nearly six acres. This is because the system would be required to have 200-foot setbacks on all sides with a minimum lot size of 500 by 500 feet. The locations would also be required to have a perimeter buffer and fencing, access roads large enough for fire trucks and a water cistern and fire hydrant. Also, no BESS could be sited in the Dunes, Flood Hazard, Wetlands Protection, Aquifer Protection or Waterfront Scene Area overlay districts. Rappe said the Planning Board studied other towns’ regulations before writing its own. Also, board members kept two principles in mind for the new rules: They must not endanger the health, safety and welfare of residents and they must protect the environment. In addition, the new zoning proposal needed to meet three tests, she said. These include adoption at Town Meeting, approval by the state Attorney General and being defensible in court. “There is a very long list of things we’ve done to try to make sure that Duxbury and its citizens are kept safe,” she said. “The consequences of not passing it are that we have no local regulations, no control, and it could be sited almost anywhere.” This bylaw is not to encourage BESS in town but to have a process to regulate them if they are proposed, said Rappe. The Planning Board held a public information session on BESS on Nov. 16. Selectboard members had a few questions for the Planning Board on the BESS bylaw but they praised the effort so far. “Great job,” said Glennon, “You’ve done a lot of hard work on this.” “We need to put something in place even if we abhor to have to do this,” said Selectboard Vice Chairman Fernando Guitart. “When it comes to town, at least we have some measure of control, so that’s going to be the key selling point. We have to convince Town Meeting.” In addition to the BESS bylaw, the Planning Board is proposing five other law changes. One of the less complicated proposals includes updates to certain sections of the town’s current zoning law to ensure the language is consistent with changes to Chapter 40A, the state law that regulates local zoning bylaws. That law was updated in July. A second proposal amends the existing Flood Hazard Area Overlay District as specified by the Massachusetts Department of Conservation and Recreation. According to Rappe, this action will not affect residents’ flood insurance. The board is also proposing to update over 60 definitions and terms in the zoning bylaw. Many are language updates such as changing the term “Board of Appeals” to “Zoning Board of Appeals” or changing “Chairman” to “Chair.” There are two other more substantial zoning bylaw changes. One is to update the Inclusionary Housing section to encourage more affordable housing and the other would replace the Residential Conservation Cluster zoning with something called the Open Space Residential Development District. Any zoning bylaws proposed for Town Meeting will be reviewed by both the Selectboard and Planning Board at public hearings before the meeting.

artigo.texto: Supply Runs from 2026 to 2028, Expanding POSCO’s China Market Presence While the Deal Follows Recent Agreements With SK On and Longbai Group POSCO Group has signed a long-term contract to supply lithium for electric vehicle batteries to China’s CATL for three years from 2026 to 2028. Photo provided by POSCO Group. POSCO Group is strengthening its penetration of the Chinese market by signing a long-term lithium supply contract with China’s CATL, the world’s largest electric vehicle battery manufacturer. Following a lithium supply contract with SK On and business cooperation with China’s Ronbay Group earlier this year, the group is expanding its global lithium sales network by securing CATL as a client. POSCO Group announced on Nov. 18 that it has signed a contract with CATL to supply lithium required for electric vehicle battery manufacturing for three years from 2026 to 2028. Supply under the contract is currently underway, and the specific supply volume and contract amount have not been disclosed. CATL is a company that holds approximately a 40% share in the global electric vehicle battery market and supplies batteries to major automakers in China and other countries. Through this contract, POSCO Group plans to expand its lithium sales base in China and strengthen long-term transactions with global battery manufacturers. Currently, POSCO Group is expanding its production capacity centered around the Hombre Muerto salt lake in Argentina, which it acquired in 2018. In 2024, the group completed the construction of its first lithium hydroxide plant with an annual production capacity of 25,000 tons, and additionally completed the upstream process of its second plant in October. The second plant can produce 23,000 tons of lithium carbonate annually, and POSCO Group plans to link this with a subsequent process scheduled to be completed in South Korea in 2027. Once the domestic subsequent process is completed, the group will have a lithium hydroxide production system with an annual capacity of 50,000 tons, including the existing first plant. The group is also operating domestic lithium production facilities utilizing Australian ore. POSCO Pilbara Lithium Solution, a joint venture between POSCO Holdings and Australia’s Pilbara Minerals, has built a lithium hydroxide production facility with an annual capacity of 43,000 tons at the Yulchon Industrial Complex in Gwangyang, South Jeolla Province. Along with the expansion of its production base, the group is consecutively signing long-term supply contracts with battery companies. In February, it signed a contract to supply up to 25,000 tons of lithium to SK On by 2028. This volume is sufficient to produce batteries for approximately 400,000 electric vehicles and will be utilized in SK On’s electric vehicle battery business in Europe and North America. Following this, in August, the group signed a strategic business agreement with Chinese cathode material company Ronbay Group in the fields of lithium supply and waste battery recycling. The two companies are pursuing cooperation to supply recycled lithium, as well as Argentine brine lithium and Australian ore lithium. The group has secured supply contracts not only for lithium raw materials but also in the cathode material business. In September, its battery materials affiliate POSCO Future M signed a contract to supply lithium iron phosphate (LFP) cathode materials worth approximately 1.1 trillion won (about $825 million) to SK On. The supply period is from 2027 to 2029. Based on this, POSCO Future M plans to respond to the battery materials market for energy storage systems (ESS) as well as electric vehicles.

artigo.texto: Democrats Plan Grid Rule Overhaul; Data Centers Could Pay $35 Billion More in Power Bills Over a Decade After winning majorities in both chambers of Congress, the U.S. Democratic Party is pushing a federal permitting overhaul, one aim of which is to accelerate federal environmental review of various energy projects so that data center operators can more easily obtain power. But the overhaul contains another layer of design: Democrats want data centers to bear the extra costs of connecting to the grid themselves, rather than passing those expenses on to utility companies and other ratepayers. According to a report by Cnyes, a consulting firm Grid Strategies estimates that federal-level grid rule changes alone could force data centers to pay an additional $35 billion (approximately NT$1.2 trillion) over the next decade; if states make full use of other provisions in the bill, they could collect a combined additional $13.6 billion (approximately NT$450 billion). Democratic Senator Sheldon Whitehouse said that once the bill passes, the situation in which data centers "free-ride" on the power system will end. He noted that going forward, when data centers connect to the grid, they must bear the resulting extra costs themselves and cannot pass the expenses on to utility companies, leaving other ratepayers to foot the bill. The legislation has drawn sharply divided reviews in Washington. Some environmentalists opposed to the permitting bill criticize it as effectively a "gospel" for tech companies that could accelerate the buildout of natural gas-fired data centers; supporters see it as the starting point for Democrats taking a tougher stance on artificial intelligence companies. Note: Amounts are based on Grid Strategies' report estimates; NT$ conversions use reference exchange rates. How the new rules will be implemented remains subject to many variables. Texas is home to one of the largest concentrations of U.S. data centers, but the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) has no jurisdiction over Texas's main grid, raising questions about whether federal rules can be applied uniformly. In addition, utility regulators in some states still need to work out the details and establish how transmission costs will be allocated. Another key unknown is whether higher power bills will prompt tech companies to exit the public grid. Dozens of planned off-grid data center projects have already emerged in the industry, using generation methods that include less efficient gas turbines and even converted jet engines. Related analysis indicates that if data centers supply their own power with such facilities, greenhouse gas emissions would be 31% to 90% higher than connecting to the public grid. Opponents are also concerned about knock-on land-use effects. Aaron Weiss, executive director of the nonprofit environmental group Western Priority Center, believes the new bill could trigger a data center construction boom across American land, and that once it takes shape, it will be difficult to reverse. From an industry perspective, the overhaul has a two-sided effect for data center operators. Faster permitting would help shorten timelines for securing power and ease the supply bottlenecks constraining artificial intelligence computing expansion; but if grid connection costs must be borne by the operators themselves, large operators' operating expenses will rise markedly, and their cost structure could shift from one-time construction spending to long-term power bill burdens. For utilities and ordinary ratepayers, if the new system is implemented, it is expected to ease the upward pressure that data center electricity use puts on power prices. The market's next focal points are whether the bill's provisions can address grids beyond federal jurisdiction, such as Texas's, and how quickly state regulators allocate transmission costs. If power bills become too heavy a burden and the share of tech companies turning to self-built generation rises, that will simultaneously affect demand for natural gas equipment, the logic of data center site selection, and discussions of related emissions rules. artigo.texto: A national ballot could let up to 375,000 hectares of New Zealand farmland into the emissions trading scheme (ETS) by the end of 2050 if every hectare on offer is taken up, Federated Farmers has warned. The group wants the country’s next government to scrap that ballot and extend last year’s limits on whole-farm conversions to all eight classes of farmland. In a column on Tuesday, Richard Dawkins, the group’s meat and wool chair, said five of the six parties it asked before the election had committed to stopping the incentives that drive whole farms into permanent carbon forestry. National, the senior partner in the current coalition, was the only one with a cross beside its name, as the country waits to learn who will form its next government. “But it was a brake, not a stop,” Dawkins said of last year’s Climate Change Response Amendment Act. Whilst he credits the law as a step forward, he warns the scheme can still make converting a whole sheep and beef farm to exotic trees more attractive than producing food. As Wood Central’s election guide showed, the parties went into the vote with plans ranging from National keeping forestry in the scheme with a carbon price floor held until 2031, to Labour pausing new forestry registrations during an urgent review, and the Greens taking forestry out of it altogether. Carbon forestry compass: where New Zealand’s parties stand Hover over or tap a party to read its policy and how it answered Federated Farmers. Hover over or tap a party on the compass. Positions follow each party’s stated policy on forestry in the emissions trading scheme, ordered by how far it would go, from keeping today’s rules on the left to taking forestry out of the scheme on the right. The points are evenly spaced and are not scored. The six parties are the ones Federated Farmers asked in its 2026 voter guide whether they would commit to stopping the incentives that drive whole farms into permanent carbon forestry, with answers as it reported them. Wood Central takes no political stance on the 2026 New Zealand general election and invites all parties contesting it to provide a contribution to the masthead. Carbon forestry compass: hover over or tap each party to see where it stands on forestry in the emissions trading scheme, and how it answered Federated Farmers. (Graphic Credit: Wood Central) For now, farmers can register up to 25 per cent of their land in Land Use Capability (LUC) classes 1 to 6 as exotic forest in the scheme, on a scale that ranks farmland from 1, the most versatile, to 8, the most limited. Yet Dawkins said another 15,000 hectares of class 6 country can go in every year through the ballot, over and above that allowance, whilst classes 7 and 8 sit outside the restrictions altogether. Indeed, the first ballot this year was more than twice oversubscribed, he said, with applications covering 12,079 hectares for the 5,500 on offer, and the year's second ballot closed on Friday. That 375,000 hectares, he warned, comes before the 25 per cent allowance or any class 7 and 8 land is counted. And it is a fight Dawkins has taken onto the land, too, with his column picturing him and vice chair Simon Cameron taking a break from cutting down pine trees in Gisborne this year. Yet National's Forestry Minister, Todd McClay, told a farmer debate in the Waikato during the campaign that it was "the first full year that the sale of valuable farmland for conversion to trees has stopped." Dawkins is not convinced. He said National's cross was hard to reconcile with the party's own promise to stop large-scale conversions. Already, sales have slowed sharply since the peak years of 2021 and 2022, with Beef + Lamb New Zealand counting an initial 15,743 hectares of sheep and beef farmland sold into forestry last year, Wood Central reported in August. Back in August last year, Dawkins warned that the real threat lay in the hill country, saying class 6 and 7 land "is not 'marginal land' as it's often described by foresters." Foresters, for their part, have long argued the opposite, with Matt Wakelin, president of the New Zealand Forest Owners Association (FOA) when the limits were announced, warning that much of the country's class 6 land was ill-suited to food production but ideal for planting trees. Restricting it, he said, would push planting onto marginal or less productive land, which "will have an impact on future timber and fibre supply, jobs and forestry's ability to support New Zealand in meeting its climate change obligations." More recently, the FOA's chief executive, Dr Elizabeth Heeg, said planting intentions had fallen since the whole-farm rules took effect, with the outlook for new commercial forests this year cut by more than two-thirds from the 60,000 hectares planted in each of the previous two years. Uncertainty over the scheme was "dampening long-term investor confidence in the forestry sector," she said in January. At the same time, Dawkins cited Simon Upton, the Parliamentary Commissioner for the Environment, who has called for a fundamental rethink of the ETS and forestry's role within it. Upton described the scheme as "essentially rudderless" in his Adrift report in August. Before polling day, Dawkins took his case straight to National in a column, writing that the party "needs to strengthen its restrictions, not just stand by them." artigo.texto: Ford Begins U.S. Battery Cell Output With CATL Technology at $3 Billion Michigan Plant Ford Motor has begun making battery cells in the United States, using technology licensed from China's CATL, as the automaker pushes to put cheaper lithium iron phosphate batteries into its next generation of electric vehicles. The cells are being built at a roughly 2 million-square-foot plant in Marshall, Michigan, about 100 miles west of Detroit, at a cost of $3 billion. Output started last month and the cells are now shipping, the company said Wednesday. They will go into prototypes of the Fathom, a midsize electric pickup that CEO Jim Farley has positioned as competitive with Tesla and Chinese rivals. The project represents a milestone for Ford, the largest producer of U.S. vehicles, and a step toward wider use of LFP chemistry in American-made cars. The technology was developed in the United States but was largely commercialized in China, where it now underpins much of the world's low-cost EV supply. Ford says the Marshall site can turn out 40 cells a minute, equal to 20 gigawatt-hours a year for vehicles and its energy storage business. That is half the 40 gigawatt-hours once planned, a reduction the company attributes to a pullback in EV demand across the industry. The plant is highly automated, and Ford said it is still certifying its processes, with cell production set to ramp up next year ahead of the Fathom's expected launch in the fourth quarter of 2027. Alan Clarke, Ford's vice president of advanced development projects, said licensing the technology was the quickest route to affordable EVs. "If we want to get to being able to produce affordable EVs in the United States, we need to also do it the fastest way possible," Clarke said during a tour of the facility. "CATL being the biggest in the world means that they're the best supplier to get us that technology and help us learn ourselves how to produce LFP cells." The arrangement has drawn criticism in Washington. In September, U.S. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy wrote to Farley expressing "profound concern" about Ford's ties to Chinese companies, which the agency said could harm the automaker and the broader U.S. auto industry. Ford dismissed the letter as a "wrongheaded attempt to capture headlines" and pointed to its construction of a domestic battery plant while competitors keep importing cells from China. The White House followed the letter a day later by praising Ford for its American jobs and manufacturing. The scrutiny comes as Washington tightens its review of Chinese links to U.S. companies, even while President Donald Trump meets this week with Chinese leader Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin. Ford said it still expects the project to qualify for a federal tax credit for battery manufacturing. For the industry, the start of cell production at Marshall offers a test of whether U.S. automakers can adopt Chinese-developed LFP know-how at home without running afoul of policymakers. Several carmakers are shifting to the chemistry because it costs less than nickel-based cells and is considered more durable, a combination that matters as buyers weigh affordability. Ford's ability to scale the plant toward its original capacity, and to secure incentives, will shape how quickly that shift reaches American assembly lines. artigo.texto: POSCO Signs 3-Year Lithium Supply Deal With CATL, Securing China's Battery Giant POSCO Group has signed a long-term lithium supply contract with China's CATL, the world's top player in the global electric vehicle battery market. According to POSCO Group on the 18th, the two companies agreed to a three-year contract to supply lithium used in EV battery manufacturing from 2026 through 2028, and shipments under the agreement are already underway. Specific volumes and the contract value were not disclosed. The deal gives POSCO Group a stable sales channel in China, the world's largest EV battery market. CATL holds about 40% of the global EV battery market and supplies batteries to automakers in China and around the world. A POSCO Group official said the two companies "agreed to work together to solidify a long-term partnership and build a stable raw material procurement system." Lithium is a core material directly tied to battery production costs, and its price is highly volatile, making stable sales channels critical for producers and raw material supply chain management critical for battery makers. The contract extends the strategy Chairman Chang In-hwa has emphasized: securing quality resources preemptively and diversifying global customers. POSCO Group has expanded its lithium business based on the raw material procurement and development capabilities it built in the steel business. After securing mining rights to Argentina's Hombre Muerto salt flat in 2018, it completed a 25,000-ton-per-year lithium hydroxide Plant 1 there in 2024, and in October it finished the raw material production facilities for brine lithium Plant 2. That site produces 23,000 tons of lithium carbonate a year, which is brought to the Yulchon Industrial Complex in Gwangyang, South Korea's South Jeolla Province, and refined into battery-grade lithium hydroxide. The Yulchon refinery, targeted for completion in the first quarter of next year, will have a capacity of 25,000 tons per year. Once completed, Argentina's brine-based lithium hydroxide capacity will rise to 50,000 tons per year. Adding the 43,000 tons of ore-based capacity secured at the Yulchon complex by POSCO Pilbara Lithium Solution, a joint venture with Australia's PLS Group, brings total capacity to 93,000 tons per year. POSCO Group plans to build Plants 3 and 4 in Argentina to expand local brine-based lithium product capacity to 100,000 tons per year by 2033. Note: Argentina Plant 2 produces 23,000 tons of lithium carbonate a year, which is brought to Yulchon and refined into lithium hydroxide. POSCO Group previously signed a long-term lithium supply contract with South Korea's SK On in February. It will supply up to 25,000 tons from this year through 2028, with the volumes destined for EV battery projects in Europe and North America. With a long-term customer among South Korean battery makers and now the global No. 1, POSCO Group's lithium sales channels span South Korea, China, Europe and North America. The contract illustrates how both raw material producers and demand-side companies are prioritizing supply chain stability amid growing lithium price volatility. POSCO Group aims to boost the profitability of its lithium business by expanding capacity and increasing long-term supply contracts with global battery makers. However, with volumes and value undisclosed, the specific impact of the deal on earnings has yet to be determined. artigo.texto: ETRI Uses Cross-Server Memory Sharing to Ease AI Data Center Expansion Bottleneck A technology has emerged that could ease the memory shortage that has become a bottleneck for expanding artificial intelligence (AI) data centers. By letting an entire data center share the memory installed in each server, the approach could provide immediate relief from the current memory supply crunch. South Korea's Electronics and Telecommunications Research Institute (ETRI) said on the 19th that EMP, its in-house cross-server memory sharing software, is being piloted at the University of Southern California (USC) Center for Advanced Research Computing. The center operates a high-performance computing (HPC) cluster of about 500 servers. EMP is system software that links servers in a data center over ultra-high-speed networks, allowing one server to borrow spare capacity from another when its own memory runs short. Its key feature is that it can push past the memory limits of individual servers without adding separate hardware. The test results are notable. A server with only 448 gigabytes (GB) of its own memory completed a large-scale genomic analysis requiring about 1.8 terabytes (TB) after EMP was applied, borrowing roughly three-quarters of the memory it needed from other servers. Performance per unit of memory improved by as much as 2.3 times. With demand for AI training and data processing surging, data center operators face a heavy burden in securing massive amounts of memory. Equipping every server with memory sized to peak demand drives up upfront investment, while idle memory sits unused when workloads are light. ETRI expects EMP to reduce this inefficiency and raise utilization of existing equipment. Still, the technology is unlikely to fundamentally reduce new memory demand. Performance was found to decline somewhat when borrowing another server's memory compared with using local memory. Ko Kwang-won, head of ETRI's AIDC Research Division, said, "Its significance lies not so much in raising the efficiency of a single memory as in sharing memory across multiple servers," adding, "From a hyperscaler's perspective, it amounts to gaining a temporary stopgap before new memory arrives." He added, "These days it takes a long time to secure memory, and this technology can put out the immediate fire," but "companies that need to boost data center performance will ultimately bring in more memory." Industry watchers see the technology helping accelerate the buildout of AI data centers. Because memory supply is a key variable in data center construction, the ability to operate resources flexibly should make supply forecasting considerably easier. The pilot was conducted at USC's request. ETRI plans to broaden the scope of testing with USC researchers to include genome assembly, protein analysis and weather forecasting. Drawing on operating experience gained at a large US data center, it will expand deployment to South Korean high-performance computing centers, universities and research institutions, and pursue commercialization. "Based on our US pilot experience, we will develop this into a core system software that raises resource utilization efficiency at South Korean AI data centers," Ko said. ETRI said inquiries about adoption are continuing from other universities and departments after news of the large US data center pilot spread. The technology is drawing attention because it arrives as a structural shortage of memory semiconductors persists. As AI server expansion gathers pace, demand for server memory including high-bandwidth memory (HBM) has surged, and data center operators cannot guarantee memory procurement schedules even as they draw up expansion plans. Analysts say that if cross-server resource sharing is commercialized, it could serve as a buffer that helps pace near-term expansion. artigo.texto: Li Auto's Eight-Year Partnership with CATL Frays: Debt-Collection Emails, Supply Cutoffs and a Self-Developed Battery Breakthrough Li Auto (02015.HK/LI.US) and CATL (300750.SZ) have maintained a deep eight-year tie, but that bond is loosening due to battery supply shortfalls and disagreements over responsibility. On November 19, the topic "CATL calls police on Li Auto" trended on social media, pushing the pair once regarded as a model of supply-chain partnership into the center of public debate. Although both sides still publicly call each other "strategic partners," the cracks are clearly visible — from capacity fulfillment and recall liability to the full rollout of self-developed batteries. The conflict became public in September 2025. According to a report by Yijian Auto, during the production ramp-up of the Li Auto i8, Li Auto staff and a logistics fleet arrived at CATL's Liyang plant to collect goods but were blocked outside the factory grounds. At the time, the i8 was underperforming market expectations, and Li Auto wanted to pause battery production, while CATL demanded that it take delivery of all batteries produced, with inventories at one point exceeding 10,000 units. The batch was later reported to have quality problems and delivery was suspended, leaving large numbers of trucks stranded on the road outside the plant. CATL called police, citing suspected disruption of traffic order and safety-production risks. What truly pushed the relationship to the brink was the Li Auto MEGA fire and recall incident. In November 2025, a MEGA caught fire, and the investigation pointed to a coolant anti-corrosion defect that carried a risk of thermal runaway. Li Auto planned to recall more than 11,000 vehicles. At a meeting with CATL, the battery maker suggested addressing the issue at a single point rather than conducting a large-scale recall, saying "there's no need; this matter can be played down." When Li Auto executives asked whether CATL would share liability if another spontaneous fire occurred, CATL did not respond. Financial reports show Li Auto lost 1.1 billion yuan (approximately $165.0 million) due to the recall, but insiders say the actual cost exceeded 2 billion yuan (approximately $300.1 million), all funded from the company's cash flow. The supply shortfall was equally striking. In the fourth quarter of 2025, Li Auto placed orders for 8,000 i6 battery packs with CATL but ultimately received only 4,000, with CATL citing insufficient capacity. The i6 had accumulated about 40,000 orders at the time; hampered by the battery shortage, only 29,000 were delivered in 2025, with nearly 10,000 orders forced to be postponed to 2026. A battery executive at an automaker said a supplier capacity deviation of within 15% is acceptable, but more than 50% constitutes a massive supply failure. CATL has its own explanation. At its third-quarter 2025 earnings call, company executives said that due to short-term capacity constraints, some orders had to be diverted to peer companies. Data from the China Passenger Car Association (CPCA) shows that in September 2025, China's domestic passenger vehicle retail sales reached 2.241 million units, a record high, of which battery-electric retail sales were 838,000 units, up 32.3% year on year. Mid-to-high-end BEV models priced above 200,000 yuan (approximately $30,000) accounted for 20% to 25%, precisely CATL's main battleground. That month, about 50 to 80 passenger vehicle models were equipped with CATL batteries, with lithium iron phosphate accounting for 70%. Li Auto's response was to accelerate in-house development. At its March 2026 earnings call, Li Auto Executive Director and President Ma Donghui said that starting in 2026, all models would adopt a dual-battery路线 using both "Li Auto brand" and CATL-branded batteries. At an August 26 second-quarter earnings briefing, Li Auto Chairman Li Xiang further clarified that starting in the second half of the year, self-developed batteries would gradually be installed across all models. On September 7, Li Auto announced that its self-developed batteries had been installed in the L8, L6 and i8, with full coverage of all models to follow; the new-generation MEGA and the all-new i9 would use CATL batteries for their first deliveries before fully switching to self-developed batteries, while the 2026 i6 would use self-developed batteries across the lineup. Capacity anxiety had long troubled management. According to insiders, Li Xiang was anxious about battery capacity almost every day during that period. "The anxiety was that there was no move to make — your fate is in someone else's hands, and that's hard to take." Capital-level moves were more direct. In September 2026, Li Auto injected 2.65 billion yuan (approximately $397.6 million) into Sunwoda Power, becoming its second-largest shareholder. Sunwoda is one of the contract manufacturers for the cells of the "Lianshan" battery that Li Auto unveiled on October 20. artigo.texto: Trina Storage and the Swedish company OX2 signed a framework agreement for the supply of battery energy storage systems (BESS) with an approximate capacity of 3 GWh. The equipment will be used in projects in Finland, Sweden, Poland, and Italy, most of which are expected to become operational by 2028. The agreement is part of OX2 expansion of its European energy storage portfolio and includes standalone installations and hybrid solutions linked to renewable generation projects. According to the planned schedule, the projects will reach financial close between 2026 and 2027. Trina Storage will supply BESS systems in four European countries Trina Storage, Trinasolar’s energy storage division, will provide battery systems for various projects developed by OX2 in the European market. The agreement includes approximately 3 GWh of storage capacity, distributed among facilities located in Finland, Sweden, Poland and Italy. The collaboration will allow progress in the development of a portfolio of projects that combines stand-alone BESS systems with installations integrated into renewable energy plants. Although the companies have not detailed the individual capacity of each project or the economic value of the agreement, OX2 anticipates that most of the facilities will begin operating in 2028, once the financing, construction and commissioning stages are completed. These systems will allow electricity to be stored and supplied later according to the operational needs of the network. Energy storage is gaining importance in Europe The growing incorporation of solar and wind power generation there is a growing need for technologies that bring flexibility to European electricity systems. In this scenario, BESS systems allow energy to be stored for certain periods and supplied when generation or demand conditions require it. Furthermore, they can contribute to the stability of electrical networks through regulation and rapid response services, depending on the technical and commercial characteristics of each installation. For OX2, this technology represents a growth opportunity in both independent projects and hybrid solutions that combine renewable production and storage. Paolo Romanacci, OX2 operations director, highlighted that the company’s storage business continues to grow through both development methods. The executive also expressed his satisfaction at establishing a long-term collaboration with Trina Storage, which will allow progress in the execution of OX2 European project portfolio. OX2 expands its investments in solar energy and batteries in Poland The new collaboration with Trina Storage comes after OX2 announced further investments in renewable generation and energy storage in the Polish market. In June 2026, the company announced investment decisions for two projects, one being the Lion photovoltaic park and the other a battery storage facility in Osiek Jasielski. The Lion solar park, located in the municipality of Sława, in the Lubusz Voivodeship, will have a maximum capacity of 165 MWp and will be one of the largest photovoltaic projects developed by OX2 in Poland. Once operational, it is estimated to produce approximately 184 GWh of electricity per year, a volume equivalent to the annual consumption of about 51,000 homes, according to estimates announced by the company. Furthermore, Osiek Jasielski BESS installation will have a capacity of 50 MW and a storage capacity of 120 MWh. This project represents OX2’s first investment in battery storage in Poland. Both initiatives are part of the company’s expansion in the Polish electricity sector and reflect its interest in combining renewable generation assets with storage technologies. Finland promotes new high-capacity BESS systems Finland has also become a relevant market for OX2 growth in energy storage, in February 2026, the company reached a seven-year agreement with Statkraft for the optimization of two BESS facilities currently under construction. The projects will have a combined capacity of 235 MW and a total energy capacity of 470 MWh. One of the facilities will have 110 MW of power and 220 MWh of storage, while the second will have 125 MW and 250 MWh. Both systems will be located next to the Kannisto wind farm project in Halsua and the Korkeamaa wind farm project in Soini, and are scheduled to become operational in 2028. Under the terms of the agreement, Statkraft will take over the commercial optimization of the batteries, with the aim of managing its participation in the electricity market and taking advantage of the opportunities associated with system flexibility. These investments demonstrate the growth of OX2 storage portfolio in Northern Europe, where BESS systems are becoming increasingly important to complement renewable generation. The 3 GWh agreement reinforces OX2 expansion in Europe The alliance between Trina Storage and OX2 represents a new step in the development of large-scale energy storage projects in Europe. The planned supply of 3 GWh will support a significant part of the Swedish company’s European portfolio, while it moves forward with the financing and execution of new facilities. The financial closings planned between 2026 and 2027 will be crucial to completing the projects included in the agreement. With most of the facilities scheduled to become operational in 2028, the collaboration seeks to expand the availability of storage systems and strengthen the integration of renewable energy into the electricity markets of Finland, Sweden, Poland, and Italy. artigo.texto: Giant Batteries Replace Gorgas Coal-fired Power Plant A utility-scale battery energy storage system (BESS) is a large-scale rechargeable battery installation connected to the electric grid that stores electricity and discharges it when needed, according to Alabama Power Company. The utility now has its first site operating in the Walker County town of Parrish. The company says the facility was able to become operational in October, six months ahead of schedule. From Coal to Cells The first-of-its-kind BESS in Alabama is located on the 7-acre site of the former Gorgas coal-fired power plant, built in 1917. That plant was shut down in 2019 due to federal environmental regulations and high compliance and retrofit costs. The battery storage facility replacing it is generally a net environmental benefit by helping grids use more renewable energy and cut fossil-fuel emissions. The property has now been repurposed to boost Alabama Power’s reliability during peak power needs, such as high HVAC usage during extreme summer heat or winter cold. Gorgas BESS construction manager Cameron Key said in an Alabama Power release that the giant batteries are charged during nonpeak times so they can be accessed when needed. “This facility is designed to support our peak loads, to be able to put that additional power out that’s needed.” Megapack Muscle The company describes the facility as providing a totally different way for Alabama Power to be ready to supply power for customers in emergency power situations. The Tesla Megapacks, large-scale, pre-assembled rechargeable lithium-ion battery systems, are connected to 46 medium-voltage transformers and linked through a control house to a switchyard that ties directly into Alabama Power’s high-voltage grid. The Gorgas BESS is capable of storing 150 megawatts of electricity, enough to power roughly 9,000 homes for two hours. The system can charge in just over two hours, enabling it to absorb excess energy when demand is low and discharge when the grid needs support, particularly during peak usage times. Alabama Power is developing additional storage and hybrid projects at the Clearview Solar and Battery Energy Storage Facility in Macon and Bullock counties. One side benefit of the batteries, according to company officials, is that the battery storage facilities will help Alabama absorb surging data center power demand. artigo.texto: Key Takeaways - BAIC Motor aims to free up capital through the sale, while its parent is working with CATL to bring more models onto the battery maker's swap network. - The assets have an appraised value of about 278 million yuan ($41.4 million). BAIC Motor (HKEX: 1958) plans to sell assets tied to 112 battery swap stations through a public tender to free up capital tied up in non-core assets. Its wholly owned subsidiary, BAIC Powertrain, plans to submit a notice of the proposed sale to the China Beijing Equity Exchange (CBEX) by the end of November, BAIC Motor said in a Hong Kong stock exchange filing on Tuesday. BAIC Powertrain plans to sell its entire interest in the assets, which include inventory, fixed assets, construction in progress and intangible assets used in station operations. A September 30 appraisal using the cost approach valued the assets at about 278 million yuan ($41.4 million), excluding tax, about 1.54% above their unaudited book value. The listing price will be at least as high as the appraised value ultimately filed with the authorities. The winning bid will determine the sale price. At the time of the filing, BAIC Powertrain had yet to identify a buyer or sign a sale agreement. BAIC Motor estimates that a sale at the appraised value in 2026 would lift its consolidated profit for the year by about 3.52 million yuan after transaction costs. BAIC Powertrain plans to use the proceeds to fund its operations and development. The proposed sale comes as BAIC Motor's parent, Beijing Automotive Group (BAIC Group), expands its battery swap partnership with CATL (HKEX: 3750). BAIC Group said in October that it would bring compatible models from several of its brands onto CATL's Choco swap network and make dealership sites available for new swap stations. The partners aim to serve 1 million vehicles. On November 13, BAIC Group's Arcfox brand launched a LiDAR-equipped battery swap version of the Beta S3 and a battery swap version of the Beta T1. Both use CATL's battery swap system for passenger vehicles. Arcfox said it would offer a battery swap version of every model in its lineup next year. Battery swap stations are expensive for automakers to build and maintain, BAIC Group chairman Zhang Jianyong said at the launch. Battery makers can benefit from economies of scale in both construction and operation, he said. BAIC began researching battery swap technology in 2011, making it one of the first automakers in China to invest in the field, Zhang said. He said BAIC Group and CATL would draw on their respective strengths to build China's first battery swap network capable of serving about 1 million vehicles. ($1 = 6.7118 yuan)

New study shows the true scale of data center emissions Harvard researchers examined 403 of the largest U.S. data centers over a year, between May 2024 and April 2025. The estimated numbers: 28.3 million tons of carbon dioxide and 82 terawatt-hours of electricity from fossil fuels. The first reactions from the expert community agree that the estimate is realistic. In his opinion, advanced AI will eventually help find ways to use energy more efficiently. Another potential upside is the heat coming from data centers; capturing it can provide heat to homes and businesses in the area. Country representatives need to reach an agreement by the end of this week. Australia’s Chris Bowen, who is leading the negotiation, said some countries have already rejected the latest 18-page draft. The event reflects a year of global warming that caused wildfires in Europe and glacier melting in Nepal. Other crises, like wars and the rising cost of living, limit political motivation. artigo.texto: Japan yesterday said that Southeast Asian nations would be able to access its crude oil storage facilities as part of efforts to prepare the region for a future energy crisis. The announcement came as ASEAN leaders met in Manila, where energy security has been high on the agenda. Addressing regional leaders, Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi said her country’s “hydro-tanks” would be available for use under the proposed initiative for cooperation on oil stockpiling. Photo: AFP ASEAN members have been grappling with fuel shortages and price hikes after the Middle East conflict squeezed the flow of crude to the region. The regional bloc has previously called for “unimpeded” passage through the Strait of Hormuz, which was closed following US-Israeli strikes on Iran. Under the Japanese POWERR Asia initiative, ASEAN nations would be able to use Japan’s excess storage capacity for crude oil. “We have suggested to utilize our crude oil stockpiling facilities in Japan, which is not utilized,” Japanese Ministry of Foreign Affairs press secretary Toshihiro Kitamura told reporters on the sidelines of the ASEAN summit. “By utilizing those unused facilities in Japan, we can stockpile the other countries’ crude oil and in case of crisis... It’s a kind of joint stockpiling system,” he said. Japan has 254 days’ worth of oil reserves, he said, while at the outbreak of the Middle East war in February some ASEAN countries had less than a month’s worth. An ASEAN-backed study for joint stockpiling of oil has also recommended using facilities in Thailand and Indonesia, but Kitamura said a final decision had not been made. “It’s under specific discussion,” Kitamura said. “But as a government in Japan, we are ready to work with ASEAN countries to utilize our own facilities.” Longer term, Tokyo plans to assist ASEAN states to build their own “stockpiling facilities.” “I think this is very important in order to prepare ourselves for future possibilities, crises,” he said. Philippine Secretary of Energy Sharon Garin said a memorandum of cooperation signed with Japan on Monday included assistance to “put up many more facilities to store more oil, whether [that] is diesel, gas or crude oil,” in the archipelago nation. “What this means is the Philippines will be more prepared in ensuring there is adequate oil for our homes and businesses, whatever the situation is,” Garin told reporters. “With our reserves in place, we would be better positioned to support our transport, markets, and industries,” she said. artigo.texto: Spain's government is seeking to tighten restrictions on one of Europe's fastest-growing data center booms, as the country's Socialist prime minister prepares to fight an election. Investors like Amazon, Microsoft and Blackstone-backed QTS are on tenterhooks. The measure, which doesn't need parliamentary approval, could be approved by Pedro Sánchez's cabinet by next week, and is widely expected to pass ahead of the Nov. 29 elections. It could potentially cost one of Europe's fastest-growing tech regions billions of dollars in investment. The government first introduced the decree in August, partly in response to concerns over energy demand and prices. After fierce opposition, it put forward a revised version on Oct. 26, but the proposal still includes strict renewable-energy requirements. "These requirements could pose insurmountable barriers and act as an effective moratorium," S&P said in an October report. The proposed rules would require 80% of electricity used by data centers to come from renewable sources matched hour by hour, with projects potentially losing grid access if they fail to comply. Projects already in development or awaiting grid connections would also be subject to the rules, with a five-year transition period to comply. Data center buildout faces public backlash Data center build-out has quickly become a prominent political issue around the world. In the U.S. midterm elections, CBS exit polls found data centers were a major influence for more than half of voters. In Spain, concerns over the water and energy demands of data centers are increasingly part of the election debate as the country faces mounting pressure to expand its electricity grid to meet the demand. CBRE estimates that while developers have announced 10.5 GW of data center capacity across Spain and Portugal, only about 4.5 GW is currently considered realistically deliverable because of grid, permitting and infrastructure constraints. Alberto Nadal, the opposition center-right Popular Party's deputy secretary for the economy, has said a conservative government would repeal the decree. Recent polling shows the Popular Party leading, with several seat projections putting the PP and far-right Vox together above a parliamentary majority. Aragón at center of debate Aragón, a landlocked region in the country's northeast, governed by the Popular Party, has emerged as one of Europe's fastest-growing digital infrastructure hubs and is at the center of opposition to the draft rules. The region has attracted investors with fast-track permits, abundant renewable energy and land, and international cable connections. Aragón president, Jorge Azcón, wants to turn it into the "Virginia of Europe," referring to the U.S. state with the world's highest density of data center sites. Aragón is set to receive more than 60 billion euros ($66 billion) in data center and digital infrastructure investment over the next decade. But concerns are growing among residents over noise, water use and pressure on the electricity grid. Investment versus resources Pilar Alegría, leader of the Socialist Party in Aragón, told a Nov. 15 rally that the election would be decisive for the region's future and for protecting its natural resources. She highlighted the Ebro River, which runs through Aragón, and raised concerns about the resources used by data centers in a region vulnerable to drought. Popular Party leader Alberto Núñez Feijóo, speaking the same day, sought to reassure investors. "It would be a mistake to squander that advantage through poor planning or regulation that creates uncertainty for investors," Feijóo said. Eva Valle, Aragón's economy minister, has also called for the decree to be scrapped. "It is necessary to halt the approval of this decree, which abounds in harmful conditions placed on the sector," she said at an AWS-organized event on Oct. 27, accusing the government of pursuing "a political agenda." Amazon Web Services and Microsoft have said their investment plans in Aragón remain unchanged, while urging Spain to provide long-term legal certainty and regulatory predictability. Google has already put a multibillion-euro data center project on hold pending greater regulatory certainty, according to a report in Spanish newspaper El Mundo, which cited anonymous sources. Google did not immediately respond to a request for comment from CNBC. SpainDC, which represents the data-center industry in the country, said the decree would give the group's members the most restrictive data center framework in the European Union and could put 80% to 90% of investment at risk. "We are going to use all the institutional, regulatory and legal avenues at our disposal" to challenge the decree, said SpainDC president Emilio Díaz.

artigo.texto: The town doesn’t have a stoplight for traffic — and, as the November 3 election showed, it doesn’t have a red light for data centers either. It was the only place in the country where voters approved one of these facilities, and it wasn’t close: the margin was 3 to 1. The tale is a clue to the future of data centers around the country. Applied Digital, a Dallas-based data center company, wants to build a $3 billion facility in the Harwood area. It would be the largest such facility in the state, covering 1.8 million square feet, the equivalent of 31 football fields. The company had told voters that the alternative was putting the center next door in Fargo, and that convinced Harwoodians that “we might as well get the tax benefits and the tax revenue from it,” as Mayor Blake Hankey put it. He expected the city would get $1.65 million, six times its existing total property tax revenue. And then there were the promised 200 new jobs for the region. Harwood stood in sharp contrast with the rest of the country. Gallup found in March that 71 percent of those surveyed were opposed to data center construction. NBC’s exit polling on November 3 found that data centers were a crucial factor for 69 percent of people voting for Congress. It was little wonder that some of the biggest champions of the centers scurried for cover, including Pennsylvania Governor Josh Shapiro (a Democrat who won big anyway) and Texas Governor Greg Abbott (a Republican who lost by a stunning margin), and who just a year before had proclaimed the state would be the “epicenter of AI development.” Analysts are still sorting out this stunning result, but several things are clear. Local residents didn’t like the idea of big developers draining local water, putting contaminated water back into the ground, gobbling up enormous amounts of electricity, and putting noisy complexes not far from their homes. Frightening warnings that AI is lurking to control us, perhaps somehow building the capacity to kill us all, surely didn’t help. Six in ten Americans are afraid of riding in self-driving cars. It’s broadly ironic that the revolt against technology has happened at precisely the time Americans have become more dependent on the devices in virtually everyone’s pocket. But that’s not all that’s jingling in pockets. A Brookings analyst projected that by 2032, data center and related investment will total $10.3 trillion. That, the Wall Street Journal said, would be “the biggest economic get in US history,” far greater than the Gilded Age railroads or the interstate highway system. Amazon, Microsoft, and Google combined for more than $720 billion in data center investment this year, three times the amount just two years ago. In Texas alone, data center construction accounts for more than one-fourth of the state’s gross domestic product. That sets up a looming dilemma. Harwood voters showed what a green light looks like, but just about everywhere else, voters flashed red. In Texas, Abbott hit a yellow caution light, calling for an audit of planned water and energy usage before giving new centers the green. But Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa wants red, calling for a complete ban until “laws can be passed by the legislature to protect Texans.” That won’t be easy to do. Democrats won the state house for the first time in 24 years, but Republicans have a comfortable 19-12 margin in the state senate and that’s going to make it hard for the legislature to pass anything restricting data centers. Hinojosa has promised executive action to shut down data center construction, but she can’t do that unilaterally. She’d have to rely instead on three separate regulatory commissions, including the agency regulating the state’s Electric Reliability Council, which is still struggling to right itself after the 2021 weather disaster that almost shut down the state’s whole power grid. The governor gets to make appointments to those commissions, but vacancies occur on a rotating basis and she won’t be able to get controlling appointments for several years. Moreover, appointments to some commissions require senate confirmation, and that’s going to be tough with Republicans holding the upper chamber. And then there’s the tsunami of cash and potential construction jobs building up in every corner of the state. Add the zoning issues lurking in the background. In Texas, for example, cities and towns have zoning power but counties don’t, so if a data center developer plans a project just outside a city limit, there might be nothing to stop it except the property owner’s agreement to sell the property. All these complications make it much harder for the light to stay red for long. One investment bank estimates that perhaps only 2 to 4 percent of planned data centers will ultimately be stopped. With so much money at stake, Harwood’s green light is ultimately the most likely signal to find.

artigo.texto: Data centers: acordo entre Amazon e Blackstone abrange 13 prédios em Indiana e no Mississippi (Adobe Stock/Divulgação) Repórter de Inteligência Artificial e Tecnologia Publicado em 16 de novembro de 2026 às 10h10. Última atualização em 16 de novembro de 2026 às 10h11. A Amazon anunciou em 16 de novembro de 2026 a venda do controle de 13 prédios de data centers nos Estados Unidos, avaliados em US$ 5 bilhões, para a Blackstone Digital Infrastructure Trust (BXDC), veículo imobiliário administrado por uma afiliada da Blackstone. A Amazon Web Services (AWS) continuará ocupando todos os imóveis como inquilina, com contratos de prazo médio inicial de 12 anos, que podem chegar a 32 anos com as renovações, e reajuste de 2,75% ao ano. A Amazon receberá dinheiro e ficará com 24,9% das duas sociedades conjuntas que serão donas dos complexos, localizados em Indiana e no Mississippi, que somam 647 megawatts de capacidade. É o primeiro investimento da BXDC desde o IPO, em maio, e a conclusão está prevista para até o fim de 2026. O modelo lembra a sociedade fechada pela Meta com fundos da Blue Owl, em 2025, para o complexo Hyperion, na Louisiana. A Amazon vai passar de proprietária a sócia minoritária e inquilina de 13 prédios de data centers recém-construídos nos Estados Unidos. Em acordo anunciado nesta segunda-feira, 16, um veículo imobiliário administrado por uma afiliada da Blackstone comprará o controle das sociedades que ficarão com os imóveis, avaliados em US$ 5 bilhões. A Amazon Web Services (AWS), braço de computação em nuvem do grupo, vai alugar todos os prédios e continuar usando a infraestrutura. A operação dá à Amazon uma forma de levantar dinheiro com instalações que já construiu e manter a capacidade disponível para seus clientes. Em troca, a companhia assume aluguéis com prazo inicial médio de 12 anos. Se todas as opções de renovação forem exercidas, a média sobe para 32 anos. O reajuste previsto é de 2,75% ao ano, e a própria Amazon garante os pagamentos da subsidiária. Os US$ 5 bilhões correspondem à avaliação bruta dos dois complexos. Na conclusão da operação, a Amazon vai transferir os imóveis para duas sociedades conjuntas, uma para cada complexo, e receber dinheiro e uma fatia de 24,9% em cada uma. A Blackstone Digital Infrastructure Trust, negociada na Bolsa de Nova York sob o código BXDC, ficará com os outros 75,1%. O pagamento em dinheiro será financiado por duas fontes. A BXDC espera aportar US$ 1,9 bilhão em recursos levantados no IPO. Subsidiárias das sociedades conjuntas devem contratar cerca de US$ 2,5 bilhões em empréstimos hipotecários, garantidos pelos próprios imóveis. Como parte do financiamento também cobrirá custos da transação, a soma dessas duas fontes indica o volume de recursos mobilizados, e o valor líquido a ser recebido pela Amazon ainda depende dos termos do fechamento. É o primeiro investimento da BXDC desde a abertura de capital, em maio. A oferta inicial foi de US$ 1,75 bilhão e, depois que os bancos exerceram integralmente a opção de vender ações adicionais, a captação líquida chegou a cerca de US$ 1,9 bilhão. A conclusão da compra está prevista para até o fim de 2026, sujeita às condições do acordo. O acordo reúne nove prédios no norte de Indiana, no mercado de data centers da região de Chicago, e quatro no Mississippi. Juntos, eles somam 647 megawatts de capacidade elétrica para equipamentos de TI. O número indica a potência que a infraestrutura pode disponibilizar a equipamentos como servidores e sistemas de rede. Para a BXDC, a compra dá acesso a prédios novos com um contrato para ocupar 100% do portfólio. Para a AWS, a locação mantém disponíveis os imóveis de que a operação depende. O contrato segue o modelo conhecido como triple net, em que o inquilino arca, além do aluguel, com despesas como impostos imobiliários, seguro e manutenção. A aquisição foi precificada a uma taxa inicial de capitalização de 7%. O indicador relaciona a renda operacional anual dos imóveis ao valor atribuído a eles. Ele serve para avaliar o preço pago pelo portfólio. O retorno para o acionista da BXDC também depende do custo da dívida e das demais despesas da operação. A parceria permite à Amazon recuperar parte do capital investido nas instalações e continuar usando os prédios. O dinheiro entra no fechamento. Os aluguéis serão pagos ao longo dos anos, com reajuste anual. Para o investidor imobiliário, o atrativo é justamente o fluxo de pagamentos de uma única locatária, respaldado pela garantia da Amazon. Prasad Kalyanaraman, vice-presidente de infraestrutura da AWS, afirmou no comunicado que a parceria permite à empresa continuar ampliando sua operação à medida que cresce a demanda dos clientes. No terceiro trimestre, a receita da AWS cresceu 39%, para US$ 46 bilhões. A expansão exige investimentos em terrenos, energia e prédios, além dos chips e servidores instalados neles. O acordo com a Blackstone traz um investidor para a parte imobiliária dessa conta. A Meta recorreu a uma sociedade com fundos da Blue Owl em outubro de 2025 para desenvolver o complexo Hyperion, na Louisiana. Os fundos ficaram com 80%, e a Meta, com 20%. Os US$ 27 bilhões divulgados naquele acordo correspondem ao custo estimado de desenvolvimento, incluindo construção e infraestrutura de energia, refrigeração e conectividade. No caso da Amazon, os US$ 5 bilhões são a avaliação de imóveis já construídos, que a AWS continuará usando como inquilina. A AWS vai alugar todos os 13 prédios. A Amazon também manterá 24,9% das sociedades que serão donas dos imóveis. Os US$ 5 bilhões são o valor bruto atribuído aos dois complexos. Na conclusão do negócio, a Amazon receberá uma parcela em dinheiro e manterá uma participação minoritária nas sociedades. A BXDC espera concluir a transação até o fim de 2026. O fechamento depende das condições do acordo e do financiamento previsto. artigo.texto: Data center moratorium extension recommended for Bloomington BLOOMINGTON (25News Now) -Bloomington’s planning commission recommends pushing the data center moratorium out for another 12 months. Since the first public event, staff made several changes to their proposed rules, based on public feedback. The commission voted to recommend extending the current moratorium for a year, instead of another six months, to come up with data center regulations. Some of the proposed changes include banning non-disclosure agreements about data centers, no matter what size the center would be, and higher fines for developers who violate city regulations. Some stakeholders, like the Citizens’ Utility Board, sent a representative who said he was pleased with proposed regulations on energy. “Relating to the energy use provisions of the ordinance, I’ve read through the draft, and I find them to be more than reasonable, really, they look a lot better than other ordinances I’ve seen around the state,” said Scott Allen of CUB. The planning commission recommended the moratorium that expires on Nov. 27 should be extended for a year, but the city council will take final action on that. artigo.texto: Data center moratorium passes in Michigan City MICHIGAN CITY, Ind (WSBT) — Michigan City pressing pause on new data center development. The Common Council approved a temporary moratorium Tuesday night. But, Google's project already under construction is exempt, raising questions from residents. Protesters gathered outside City Hall before the vote calling for stronger environmental protections. While the council approved the moratorium, protestors are more worried about the google development already underway. The newly approved ordinance temporarily blocks permits and other city approvals for future data center projects. Council members also discussed the need for equipment and safeguards to address noise and air pollution. With equipment, applied for a fine exhaust, for noise, so that the exhaust isn’t going to be polluting the air around the development, into the neighborhood, into the schools that are around there and just making the whole quality of life issue better for everybody. Donald Pryzbylinski, Michigan City Common Council The ordinance requires two public workshops within 90 days, giving residents a chance to weigh in on future zoning and environmental regulations.

artigo.texto: German energy giant RWE has just broken ground on a colossal 262.5-megawatt-hour (MWh) battery that is capable of supplying roughly 21,000 households with electricity during peak evening hours. The 62.5-megawatt (MW) battery is reportedly RWE’s first battery energy storage system (BESS) in Italy. Located in the city of Ragusa in Sicily, it will be fitted with 42 containers housing lithium-ion batteries. RWE representatives revealed that the system will have a total storage capacity of 262.5 megawatt-hours (MWh). It will be capable of delivering its maximum output for four hours. This will be enough to cover the evening peak electricity demand of around 21,000 Italian households. The company expects to commission the project by the end of 2027. “The start of construction of our Ragusa battery storage marks an important milestone,” Sopna Sury, CEO of RWE Renewables Europe & Australia, said. “We have been operating in Italy for many years, using the energy from the wind and the sun.” Power for peak demand Sury explained that the battery will support the balance between electricity supply and demand. “In a world of growing renewable energy, battery storage systems are crucial for stabilizing the grid and ensuring that electricity is used when it is needed most,” Sury continued. More from Energy See All Unlike conventional power plants, renewable energy sources depend on weather conditions. Battery storage systems can store excess electricity when production is high and release it when the demand increases. RWE said its new battery will provide balancing energy to stabilize the electricity grid. It will also feature technology capable of delivering grid-forming services such as instantaneous reserve, also known as inertia. Apart from installing the batteries, RWE will build the necessary grid infrastructure, including a high-voltage transformer that will link the system to the 150-kilovolt (kV) electricity grid. “[The] Ragusa battery will be capable of covering the evening peak demand of around 21.000 households for four hours,” Sury added. More battery capacity With the project, RWE aims to expand its battery storage business across Europe and other parts of the world. The company currently operates approximately 1.7 gigawatts (GW) of battery storage capacity worldwide. At the same time, another three GW are under construction. Additionally, RWE has established a strong presence in Italy’s renewable energy market. It currently operates 18 onshore wind farms, one solar power plant, and three agrivoltaic facilities. Together, these projects have an installed capacity of approximately 670 MW. This is enough to supply renewable electricity to more than 550,000 Italian households. The company is also constructing 200 MW of additional wind and solar capacity across the country. The Ragusa project will complement these renewable energy operations. Meanwhile, RWE plans to develop further battery storage capacity in Italy alongside its existing wind and solar projects. “We look forward to establishing further battery storage capacity in Italy soon – in addition to wind and solar power – in order to support Italy in building a resilient energy system,” Sury said in a press release. He explained that the expansion will make Italy’s electricity grid more reliable.

artigo.texto: Sam Altman disse em 16 de novembro de 2026 que as pessoas devem poder comprar bastante RAM para seus computadores. No fórum Silicon Valley & The World, da Semafor, ele também manteve seu argumento condicional: durante uma escassez, compartilhar memória em centros de dados poderia permitir um uso mais contínuo. Altman ainda elogiou a experimentação com computadores em casa. Quando a memória está escassa, a ideia de compartilhá-la é um argumento sobre eficiência na alocação; não substitui a escolha de ter RAM no próprio computador. O que Altman disse sobre a RAM dos usuários? Altman afirmou que as pessoas devem poder comprar muita RAM para seus PCs. A fala esclareceu comentários anteriores em que ele criticou o baixo uso da memória em computadores pessoais, mas não abandonou sua defesa de avaliar como a memória escassa poderia ser aproveitada. A distinção é importante: defender uma forma de distribuir um recurso limitado não equivale a defender restrições à compra de memória. Altman também disse que considera positiva a possibilidade de as pessoas experimentarem com seus computadores em casa. Por que ele defende compartilhar memória durante uma escassez? O argumento de Altman é que memória reunida em centros de dados poderia ser compartilhada e usada com mais continuidade do que a memória instalada em dispositivos pessoais, que pode ficar ociosa em certos momentos. Ele apresentou isso como uma possibilidade de eficiência quando há escassez, não como uma medição comparativa de uso. Há uma diferença prática para quem quer executar inteligência artificial no próprio computador: o processamento local depende do hardware do usuário, enquanto o argumento de Altman considera a memória compartilhada em centros de dados. Ele reconheceu que essa possibilidade tem contrapartidas e que a eficiência teórica não precisa determinar a decisão no mundo real. A memória é um entre vários gargalos de infraestrutura Ao falar sobre as necessidades da OpenAI, Altman citou diferentes restrições em momentos distintos: memória, montagem de racks, capacidade de centros de dados e outros componentes. Assim, a memória aparece como uma parte de um conjunto de desafios de infraestrutura. Em 1º de outubro de 2025, a OpenAI anunciou que Samsung Electronics e SK hynix planejavam acelerar a expansão de capacidade, com uma meta de iniciar o processamento de até 900 mil wafers de DRAM por mês. A cifra descreve um objetivo anunciado, não uma produção já alcançada. A OpenAI detalhou o plano e as parcerias.

artigo.texto: Korea has joined the Carbon Market Club of Clubs (OCCCM), an international coalition on carbon markets that includes the European Union (EU) and China. With this, Korea will take part in talks that set rules for the international carbon market, including internationally transferred mitigation outcomes and offset credits. Kim Sunghwan, Minister of the Ministry of Climate, Energy and Environment, announced Korea's entry at a high-level meeting of the Carbon Market Club of Clubs held on the sidelines of the 31st U.N. Climate Change Conference (COP31) in Antalya, Türkiye, on the 16th local time. The Carbon Market Club of Clubs is an international cooperation body that shares experience operating compliance carbon markets such as emissions trading systems and carbon taxes, and discusses measurement, reporting and verification (MRV), carbon accounting, and high-quality offset systems. Brazil proposed creating the group at COP30 last year, and it launched in May this year with the EU, China, and other major operators of carbon markets at its core. Korea joined after receiving an invitation from the EU as a follow-up to Korea-EU summit diplomacy in June. Membership is open to countries or regional economic integration organizations that operate or are developing a domestic compliance carbon market or carbon pricing system. Members have voting rights at high-level meetings. Announcing the accession, Minister Kim said, "Korea was the first in East Asia to introduce and operate a nationwide emissions trading system in 2015," adding, "We now manage more than 70% of the country's greenhouse gas emissions." He added, "We will share with member states our MRV system built for a manufacturing-centered industrial structure, our market design and operation, and our experience running an offset program within the ETS." Kim also said Korea is working to shift from a fossil fuel–based economy to an 'electric nation' centered on zero-carbon power, and introduced the government's Korea Green Transformation (K-GX) strategy released last month. By joining, Korea can now take part in setting international carbon market rules, including creating internationally transferred mitigation outcomes (ITMOs) under Article 6 of the Paris Agreement and establishing common principles for high-integrity offset credits. Meanwhile, the high-level meeting adopted the 'COP31 Carbon Market Club of Clubs Declaration,' which welcomes new members and commits to developing the coalition into a core consultative body for international cooperation on compliance carbon markets.
