artigo.texto: Investing.com -- Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA) has told customers it will stop selling chips to data-centre operators that rent more than half of their graphics processing units (GPUs) to Chinese companies, CNBC reported on Tuesday, as Washington moves to tighten restrictions on China's access to U.S. artificial intelligence technology. The chipmaker has in recent months warned buyers that the proposed Remote Access Security Act (RASA) would give the U.S. government broader authority to control access to cloud services, similar to its powers over physical hardware, CNBC reported, citing two people familiar with the matter. Nvidia also warned that the legislation could expose both chipmakers and buyers to legal risks, the report said. The Financial Times reported earlier this month that Nvidia had verbally told data-centre clients to direct at least 51% of their services to non-Chinese customers under future contracts. RASA passed the U.S. House of Representatives in January but has yet to clear the Senate, CNBC reported. U.S. export controls restrict Nvidia's advanced chips from being sold to China, but regulators have had limited powers to restrict access through cloud services hosted overseas. The Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) announced an interim final rule on Monday aimed at preventing Chinese companies from remotely accessing AI chips, CNBC reported. CNBC reported on Nov. 5 that Chinese artificial intelligence startup Moonshot AI had sought access to Nvidia chips through data centres in Europe. The Trump administration accused Moonshot in July of accessing the chips through data centres in East Asia. U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent on Sunday called for a "dramatic shakeup" at Nvidia following the departure of Chief Executive Jensen Huang, amid reports of an alleged extramarital affair with a woman U.S. authorities reportedly suspect of spying for China, CNBC reported. Bessent suggested that other Nvidia executives should also face scrutiny over compliance with export controls. He told Fox News he wanted to know whether the company had pushed what he described as seemingly illicit sales to boost revenue and earnings.

artigo.texto: Minneapolis Downtown Council CEO calls for veto of data center ordinance MINNEAPOLIS (FOX 9) - A new Minneapolis data center ordinance is setting up a fight between downtown business leaders and the City Council. Downtown business group pushes back Adam Duininck said he has spent the past six months trying to convince council members that some of downtown's 9 million vacant square feet could be used for data centers. He said that could help shift more of the property tax burden away from homeowners and renters. Local perspective: Duininck pointed to the Sleep Number building in downtown Minneapolis as an example he wants to repeat. The building recently sold for $235 million, which was about eight times its previous assessed value of about $30 million, and Duininck credited the AI data center inside for that increase. "We took I think 10 of the council members through the Sleep Number building behind us on a tour," said Duininck. "We want to try to make things easier for people to invest money in the city, it should be a clear process, a clear timeline," said Duininck. The backstory: Duininck said he worked with the council on some regulations, including square footage and location, but said the final approval amendment added at the end could push developers away. "I think it’s just a total non-starter," said Duininck. He said the extra council vote would add more time and risk to projects that already go through the planning commission process. "Every developer would have to plan in time and risk and do a fair amount of community engagement. That sort of thing is going to happen anyways through the planning commission. This is just another step for the city council to insert themselves in the process," said Duininck. What the new ordinance does Late last week, the City Council passed the ordinance after a full ban failed. As part of that compromise, any new data center would need council approval, could go only in existing buildings and could not be the primary use of a building. "We want to make sure that our community is protected from data centers, the impacts that it has on our planet. We want to better understand the impacts that it has on our water, and we want to have a better say on how we shape our city," said Councilmember Aurin Chowdhury, who authored the ordinance. By the numbers: The city says downtown now has eight data centers serving tech companies. City staff said many more around Minneapolis support the computing needs of existing businesses, and council members said they heard from Xcel Energy that there is interest in up to eight more downtown projects. The ordinance also bars data centers from the first or second floor, requires disclosure of energy, water and generator use, calls for a sound attenuation plan and requires a decommissioning plan if a site stops operating. Data centers larger than 50,000 square feet would also have to enter an Xcel Energy program and pay a premium for renewable energy credits, according to Chowdhury. What we don't know: FOX 9 reached out to ask whether Frey will veto the ordinance, but had not heard back. Frey must decide by Nov. 19, and the city's six-month moratorium on data centers expires Nov. 21. Duininck said there are two to three data center projects in talks downtown right now, but he said those projects could be in jeopardy if the ordinance moves forward. "It’s unfortunate and now we’ll have to figure out a way forward," said Duininck. The Source: A Minneapolis City Council press conference, Downtown Council CEO Adam Duininck, property records and past FOX 9 reporting.

artigo.texto: Council rejects ordinance lifting Jackson’s data center ban JACKSON, Miss. (WLBT) - Jackson’s temporary ban on data centers will remain in place following a contentious Jackson City Council meeting on Tuesday. After hearing from multiple residents, the council voted down a decision to lift the ban, which Ward 3 Councilman Kenneth Stokes says is needed to “untie the mayor’s hands” so he can bring in economic development. “The only thing we’re doing is asking the mayor to have the opportunity to listen to some of the proposals that are out there,” he said. “We don’t have a clue what they are, but we know these other cities are getting money. They’re building up.” “Why do we as Jackson, the capital city ... Why can’t we have an opportunity to bring money to this city?” he added. Stokes was joined by Ward 1 Councilman Ashby Foote in supporting rescinding the measure. Council members Vernon Hartley, Kevin Parkinson, Tina Clay, Brian Grizzell, and Lashia Brown-Thomas voted in opposition. The moratorium will remain in place until April 4. While it’s in effect, the city will not accept, process, or approve any applications for permits related to new data center projects or expansion projects for existing data centers. Foote believes the atmosphere at Tuesday’s meeting was part of the reason the repeal ordinance failed. “Council meetings have become very negative. We can’t let that negativity keep the city from pursuing economic development that could get the city back on its feet,” he said. Several people attended the meeting to speak out against the proposal, including Ward 3 resident Jackie Warren Tatum, who thanked the council for putting the moratorium in place. “For months, despite Stokes’ absences, we voiced our concerns regarding the negative impact of data centers. And we’re learning about the spills up in Southaven, the unbearable noise, and many other things,” she said. “Please do not repeal and rescind this moratorium.” Tatum was referring to a chemical spill at the SpaceXSI data center in Southaven. Mississippi Today reports that a contractor caused “5,000 to 6,000 gallons of a propylene glycol mixture to spill into a neighboring drainage ditch.” The Mississippi Department of Environmental Quality (MDEQ) was still determining when it happened, the publication stated. Yolanda Daniel also urged the council to leave the ban in place until the city fully studies data centers and their potential impact on the community. “A moratorium exists precisely to provide the time necessary for fact-finding, public input and evaluation of alternatives. Seeking to terminate that process early raises a simple, but important question: Has the council fully evaluated other economic development opportunities capable of generating jobs, investment, tax revenue, and long-term prosperity for Jackson and Jackson residents?” she asked. “The responsible course remains unchanged. Allow the moratorium to remain.” Want more WLBT news in your inbox? Click here to subscribe to our newsletter. See a spelling or grammar error in our story? artigo.texto: Osaka, Japan-headquartered Kansai Electric Power is acquiring a minority interest in Prospect Power Storage, a 150-MW/600-MWh battery energy storage system (BESS) owned by Elevate Infrastructure and ArcLight Capital Partners. Elevate (a portfolio company of ArcLight) and ArcLight announced the deal on November 16. Prospect Power currently is the largest standalone BESS in commercial operation in the PJM Interconnection, the power grid operator that serves all or part of 13 states across the U.S. Mid-Atlantic and Midwest regions. Prospect Power is located in Rockingham County, Virginia. The companies on Monday said the investment by Kansai is part of Elevate’s strategy “to develop and operate critical energy infrastructure at scale while attracting sophisticated long-term strategic capital.” The groups said the BESS is an important installation in an area with growing electricity demand driven by data centers, artificial intelligence, and electrification. Utility-Scale Battery Energy Storage “Prospect Power demonstrates Elevate’s ability to execute utility-scale battery storage projects from acquisition through commercial operation and deliver flexible capacity where the grid needs it most,” said Joshua Rogol, CEO of Elevate. “As electricity demand accelerates, projects like Prospect Power are increasingly important to strengthening grid reliability and supporting economic growth. We look forward to continuing to bring projects of this scale online across our portfolio.” The groups said that Kansai’s investment “further expands the group of global strategic and institutional investors partnering with Elevate and ArcLight and reinforces the ability of the platform to combine deep energy infrastructure expertise, operational execution, and long-term capital.” “Battery storage is becoming increasingly critical as energy demand grows and power markets require greater flexibility and reliability,” said Angelo Acconcia, managing partner of ArcLight. “Prospect Power demonstrates the value of bringing large-scale storage infrastructure into service in high-growth markets, and Kansai’s investment is a strong validation of both the quality of the asset and the growing need for storage as part of the nation’s power infrastructure.” “Prospect Power is a high-quality operating asset in an important U.S. power market, and we are pleased to partner with Elevate and ArcLight through this investment – our first battery storage project outside Japan,” said Takayuki Doi, executive officer of Kansai’s Global Business. “We look forward to leveraging the experience gained through Prospect Power and exploring opportunities for further collaboration in battery storage and other energy infrastructure in the United States.” Elevate brought Prospect Power into commercial operation in May of this year. The project is fully contracted under a 15-year power purchase agreement with Dominion Energy Virginia. —Darrell Proctor is a senior editor for POWER.

artigo.texto: EUA restringem venda de chips de IA para data centers no Brasil Regra exige licença para exportar semicondutores avançados ao País; medida também restringe oferta de serviços de computação em nuvem. O governo dos Estados Unidos incluiu o Brasil em uma lista de cinco países que passarão a depender de licenciamento específico para adquirir determinados semicondutores avançados utilizados em inteligência artificial. A medida, anunciada hoje (16) pelo Departamento de Comércio norte-americano, também abrange Indonésia, Malásia, Singapura e Tailândia e estabelece tratamento diferenciado para empresas controladas por grupos sediados nos Estados Unidos. A exigência consta da regulamentação provisória Addressing Remote Access to Advanced Semiconductors, identificada pelo código RIN-0694-AK50 e divulgada pelo Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS), órgão responsável pelo controle de exportações norte-americanas. O documento estabelece que a exportação, reexportação ou transferência de semicondutores avançados para os cinco países dependerá de autorização do governo dos Estados Unidos, ressalvadas as exceções previstas. Segundo o Departamento de Comércio, esses destinos apresentam risco de desvio de equipamentos superior ao considerado normal pelas autoridades norte-americanas. Trata-se de uma classificação adotada pelo governo dos EUA para justificar os novos controles, sem identificação, no documento, de operações irregulares específicas realizadas no Brasil. A medida não representa uma proibição geral de comercialização desses processadores. Os pedidos de licença serão analisados individualmente, considerando critérios de segurança nacional e política externa dos Estados Unidos. Empresas norte-americanas terão exceção à exigência A regulamentação estabelece que a nova exigência de licença baseada no país de destino não será aplicada a semicondutores destinados a empresas sediadas nos Estados Unidos ou cuja controladora final tenha sede naquele país, desde que sejam cumpridas as obrigações de informação previstas pelo BIS. Isso significa que a localização dos equipamentos no Brasil não será o único critério considerado. A estrutura societária da empresa destinatária também determinará a aplicação da exigência específica de licenciamento. A exceção, porém, não representa dispensa de todas as demais regras norte-americanas de controle de exportações. Para os pedidos sujeitos à autorização, o BIS informa que considerará a eficácia dos mecanismos nacionais de controle de exportações e o grau de cooperação das autoridades do país destinatário com o governo dos Estados Unidos. O Departamento de Comércio também poderá adotar medidas adicionais contra países que, segundo sua avaliação, tolerem tentativas de contornar as restrições. Entre as possibilidades estão novas exigências de licenciamento, restrições comerciais e inclusão de empresas em listas de controle. Regra também alcança acesso remoto a data centers Além das restrições de exportação para o Brasil e os outros quatro países, a norma cria um mecanismo separado de controle sobre a utilização remota de capacidade computacional instalada em data centers. Nesse caso, o objetivo declarado pelo governo norte-americano é impedir que empresas sujeitas a restrições tenham acesso indireto a processadores avançados por meio de serviços de computação em nuvem oferecidos em outros países. O mecanismo estabelece a necessidade de licença para determinadas operações com semicondutores destinados a data centers que forneçam, direta ou indiretamente, capacidade computacional superior a 12 milhões de unidades agregadas de Total Processing Performance (TPP) a empresas sediadas, ou controladas por companhias sediadas, em Macau ou em países classificados no grupo D:5. O limite considera a capacidade disponibilizada por uma instalação individual ou por diferentes data centers conectados digitalmente. Essa exigência é distinta da nova regra de licenciamento baseada no destino dos semicondutores. Portanto, o limite de 12 milhões de TPP não constitui um teto geral de processamento para data centers brasileiros. A regulamentação também prevê obrigações de identificação dos clientes e verificação de suas estruturas de controle societário. Há uma exceção específica para sistemas comerciais de recomendação, como os empregados por plataformas de comércio eletrônico e redes sociais, vinculada ao controle de acesso remoto, e não à exigência geral de licenciamento aplicável aos cinco países. Restrição surge após sanção do ReData no Brasil A mudança na política norte-americana ocorre dois meses depois da sanção do Regime Especial de Tributação para Serviços de Datacenter (ReData), instituído pela Lei nº 15.504, de 15 de setembro de 2026. O programa brasileiro estabelece incentivos tributários para investimentos na instalação, modernização e ampliação de data centers, incluindo infraestruturas destinadas à computação em nuvem, ao processamento de alto desempenho e ao treinamento e à inferência de modelos de IA. O regime prevê benefícios para a aquisição de equipamentos destinados ao ativo imobilizado de empresas habilitadas, condicionados ao atendimento de contrapartidas estabelecidas na legislação. Entre as obrigações está a disponibilização de pelo menos 10% da capacidade de processamento, armazenamento e tratamento de dados beneficiada pelo regime para o mercado interno, além do cumprimento de requisitos de sustentabilidade e investimentos em pesquisa, desenvolvimento e inovação. A nova exigência norte-americana acrescenta uma condição de licenciamento às operações de aquisição de determinados semicondutores avançados destinados ao Brasil, independentemente dos incentivos tributários previstos na legislação brasileira. Vigência depende de publicação oficial A regulamentação também formaliza a revogação dos dispositivos da chamada AI Diffusion Rule, anunciada em janeiro de 2025, durante o governo Joe Biden. artigo.texto: Agencia Comercial Spirits Ltd Announces Execution of MEP Equipment Supply and Installation Contracts for Phase 1B of Indonesia Data Center Source: GlobeNewswire TAICHUNG, Taiwan, Nov. 18, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Agencia Comercial Spirits Ltd (the “Company”) today announced that on November 13, 2026, its Indonesian operating subsidiary, PT AGCC AITECH INDONESIA (the “Indonesian Subsidiary”), entered into two definitive contracts with separate contractors for the mechanical, electrical and plumbing (“MEP”) works for Phase 1B of the Company’s planned AGCC-JKT01 data center in West Java, Indonesia (the “Data Center”): an equipment supply agreement for the procurement and supply of MEP equipment (the “Supply Contract”) and an installation works contract for the installation of the MEP equipment and systems (the “Installation Contract” and, together with the Supply Contract, the “Contracts”). The Contracts are in addition to the letters of award for the MEP equipment and installation works for Phase 1A of the Data Center previously announced by the Company on September 1, 2026. The aggregate contract price under the Contracts is in a range between US$60 million and US$65 million, exclusive of Indonesian value-added tax. Each Contract is priced on a fixed lump-sum basis and is subject to adjustment only as provided in the relevant Contract, including for variations instructed by the Indonesian Subsidiary. The contract prices are denominated in U.S. dollars and are payable in Indonesian Rupiah at the Bank Indonesia middle rate on the relevant invoice date. The Contracts provide for delivery of the equipment and completion of the installation works during 2027, in accordance with the milestones set out in the Contracts. Each Contract provides for liquidated damages for delay, subject to a cap, and for a defects notification period following taking-over of the installed works. The Indonesian Subsidiary may terminate either Contract for convenience on notice, subject to payment for work performed and other costs reasonably incurred by the relevant contractor. The Contracts relate to the construction of the Data Center and do not themselves generate revenue. Completion of Phase 1B and commencement of operations at the Data Center remain subject to, among other things, performance by the contractors engaged by the Company and its subsidiaries (the “Group”), completion of related construction and power supply works, availability of funding and applicable regulatory approvals. The Contracts do not by themselves guarantee successful completion of Phase 1B or of the Data Center, or operational capacity, customer utilization, revenue, profitability or positive cash flow. About Agencia Comercial Spirits Ltd Agencia Comercial Spirits Ltd is a Nasdaq-listed company with two principal business focuses: (i) its established premium whisky operations; and (ii) the development of AI computing infrastructure and cloud-based computing services. These two lines of business represent the Company’s primary operational pillars, with the Company dedicating substantial resources to the development and scaling of its AI computing infrastructure business. The Company’s whisky operations include procurement and distribution of bottled whisky, procurement and distribution of raw cask whisky, and cask-to-bottle and distribution services, including brand-authorized bottling, packaging and sales, in Taiwan and select international markets. Since early 2026, the Company has launched and been developing its AI Computing Infrastructure Initiative through subsidiaries in Singapore, Indonesia and other jurisdictions. This initiative represents a principal business focus, backed by substantive contractual arrangements for commercial AI computing cloud services and the development of supporting data center, power, network and technical infrastructure. The Company’s historical operating revenue has been derived from its whisky operations, and the AI computing business remains in development and deployment and is subject to significant business, financing, construction, technology, regulatory, customer demand and execution risks. These include statements concerning the manufacture, delivery, installation, testing and completion of the MEP equipment and works; the timing of Phase 1B and of the Data Center; future payments and expenditure under the Contracts; and the Company’s intended development and operation of its AI computing infrastructure business. These statements are based on management’s current expectations and assumptions and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. artigo.texto: Linxon and Fluence form Strategic Collaboration to advance integrated energy storage delivery - Collaboration combines Fluence's energy storage technology with Linxon's Mission Ready EPC approach, building on an initial 200 MWh project award in ERCOT. RALEIGH, N.C. and ARLINGTON, Va., November 17, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Linxon and Fluence Energy, Inc. today announced a strategic collaboration to pursue and deliver battery energy storage system projects through a more integrated OEM-EPC model. The collaboration combines Fluence's energy storage technology and expertise with Linxon's high-voltage engineering, grid integration and project execution capabilities. The collaboration has already contributed to securing a 200 MWh battery energy storage project in Texas' ERCOT market. Linxon and Fluence are also jointly pursuing additional opportunities across the energy storage and grid infrastructure markets. Linxon's high-voltage engineering, grid connection and complex EPC execution capabilities complement Fluence's energy storage technology and expertise. Together, the companies can address customer requirements spanning the battery energy storage system and the infrastructure required to connect it safely and reliably to the grid. Energy storage projects can separate technology supply, grid connection and EPC execution into distinct scopes, creating technical, commercial and schedule interfaces that must be resolved later in the project lifecycle. Linxon and Fluence intend to address these interfaces earlier by coordinating system requirements, engineering, constructability, procurement, commissioning and project execution from the development stage. By aligning technology, engineering, constructability, procurement, project execution and commissioning from the early stages of a project, Linxon and Fluence aim to reduce interfaces, anticipate risks and create a more competitive and predictable delivery model for customers. From managing interfaces to Engineering the Mission together At the center of the collaboration is a simple principle: align the battery system and grid infrastructure through a coordinated approach to planning, integration, and delivery. The objective is not simply to place two separate scopes alongside each other. It is to align technology, grid integration and project execution earlier, allowing the companies to identify interfaces, improve constructability and establish execution readiness before mobilization. Fluence brings its energy storage technology and expertise, while Linxon brings its EPC system integration and execution capabilities through its Mission Ready EPC approach. The collaboration incorporates Linxon's Mission Ready EPC approach, which focuses on preparing projects for successful execution before mobilization. Through early readiness planning, interface management, constructability reviews, risk identification, standardization and local capability development, Mission Ready EPC is designed to improve execution readiness and delivery predictability. The companies intend to apply these principles across future opportunities while maintaining the flexibility required to address customer specifications, market conditions and local project requirements. Together, the companies intend to create an integrated framework that can be applied across projects and markets, improving execution consistency while maintaining the flexibility required for specific customer needs. Building competitiveness before execution Earlier collaboration between the Fluence OEM and EPC is expected to create opportunities for standardized interfaces, repeatable engineering, improved constructability and more coordinated procurement and execution planning. The approach is also intended to support the progressive development of the engineering knowledge, training, field competencies and local delivery ecosystems required for future energy storage deployment. For customers, this can support earlier risk identification, clearer accountability and a more coordinated path from technology selection through grid connection and project delivery. "We want to redefine the traditional relationship between an OEM and an EPC," said Nicolas Sanloup, Managing Director Americas at Linxon. "This is not about one company providing technology and another executing around it. It is about engineering the mission together from the beginning. By combining Fluence's technology expertise with Linxon's Mission Ready EPC approach, our ambition is to anticipate interfaces, build competitiveness into the solution and develop local capabilities ahead of demand." "By bringing technology and EPC execution closer together from the outset, we have an opportunity to simplify project delivery and create a scalable and repeatable approach for our customers," said Jeff Monday, SVP and Chief Growth Officer, Fluence. "This collaboration reflects the purpose of Fluence PACE, our newly launched strategic partner program, which formalizes how we work with select partners whose capabilities complement our strengths. Our work with Linxon demonstrates how that model can support customers while creating opportunities for continued growth." A new way to deliver energy infrastructure The Linxon–Fluence collaboration is designed to move the OEM–EPC relationship from a transactional interface toward an integrated delivery ecosystem, combining technology, project integration and execution around a common mission. For customers, the ambition is clear: fewer interfaces, earlier alignment, greater competitiveness and more predictable execution. One technology strategy. One execution strategy. One mission. About Linxon Linxon is a global leader in Engineering, Procurement, and Construction (EPC) solutions for electrical substations and infrastructure projects. We develop and deliver turnkey infrastructure solutions that power progress, drive growth and benefit communities, clients, and the environment through sustainable engineering excel

artigo.texto: Rochester City Council approves one-year pause on data centers Interim ordinance passes 5-1 after public hearing ROCHESTER, Minn. (KTTC) – The Rochester City Council approved a one-year moratorium on data centers within city limits through passage of an interim ordinance. The Monday evening vote followed a public hearing on the topic. The majority of those who spoke were in support of the measure. The council heard from 10 people. Eight supported the interim ordinance, which was prepared by Rochester’s Community Development Department. Several social and environmental issues were raised. Those opposing the move said a one-year moratorium isn’t necessary for the council to responsibly address potential data center projects. According to city leaders, there are no pending applications. “There’s a lot of questions at this table. There’s a lot of questions in the audience. And we need to know more about how it’s going to impact our community,” said Randy Schubring, Rochester City Council president. The vote was 5-1. Councilmember Shaun Palmer opposed the proposal and raised concerns over the wording of the interim ordinance. In addition to the one-year moratorium, the action authorizes a comprehensive study on best practices related to data center developments. Find stories like this and more, in our apps. artigo.texto: Depois de muito vai e vem durante este ano, o governo definiu as datas para realização do leilão de reserva de capacidade de armazenamento. Falta, no entanto, saber se a legislação que trata da remuneração das baterias chegará intacta ao dia 2 de dezembro. A pouco mais de duas semanas da primeira disputa, uma tentativa de alterar uma regra aprovada há menos de um ano pelo próprio Congresso coloca em dúvida o calendário defendido pelo Ministério de Minas e Energia (MME). A controvérsia está no rateio dos custos de contratação das baterias. A Lei 15.269/2025, que se propõe a fazer uma reforma do setor elétrico, determinou que a despesa seja dividida exclusivamente entre os geradores de energia. Mobilizado pelo próprio setor de armazenamento, o deputado Arnaldo Jardim (Cidadania-SP) apresentou o PL 3.716/2026 para revogar esse dispositivo e submeter o armazenamento à regra geral da reserva de capacidade, que prevê o custeio pelos consumidores de energia elétrica. A proposta tem apoio de diferentes segmentos da geração, mas enfrenta um problema de calendário. Embora tenha recebido regime de urgência na Câmara, o texto precisaria superar as negociações em torno do relatório, ser aprovado pelos deputados e pelo Senado e seguir para sanção presidencial antes dos leilões para produzir efeitos sobre as regras dos certames. Há quem considere, no meio político, difícil concluir todo esse processo no prazo disponível, principalmente pela possibilidade de a proposta se transformar em um instrumento para reavaliar outros pontos da reforma do setor elétrico. O próprio relator do projeto na Câmara, Danilo Forte (PP-CE), tem um histórico de atuação em assuntos que ficaram pendentes na reforma do setor elétrico. Durante a tramitação da MP 1.304/2025, o parlamentar apresentou uma emenda para ampliar o ressarcimento aos geradores eólicos e solares pelos cortes de geração determinados pelo Operador Nacional do Sistema Elétrico (ONS), incluindo restrições associadas à confiabilidade elétrica e limitações de transmissão. Jardim reconheceu publicamente, na última sexta-feira (13/11), que Forte pretende incorporar temas como ressarcimento do curtailment, adicionalidade e descontos pelo uso da rede. O autor da proposta tem defendido um texto mais enxuto justamente para facilitar sua aprovação. O diretor-geral da Agência Nacional de Energia Elétrica (Aneel), Sandoval Feitosa, já pontuou que uma alteração legislativa exigiria a republicação dos editais e a remarcação do leilão. Como a agência trabalha com um intervalo mínimo de 30 dias entre a publicação dos documentos e a realização dos certames, a mudança praticamente afastaria a possibilidade de realizar os certames ainda em 2026. Além dos prazos, há também uma questão econômica. A alteração do rateio não significa que os leilões perdem automaticamente a atratividade, mas mexe em uma premissa relevante para a estruturação da contratação. A definição de quem paga, como os valores serão arrecadados e quais mecanismos garantirão o fluxo de recursos interfere na avaliação de riscos dos empreendimentos e pode influenciar os preços e as condições de financiamento. Uma mudança às vésperas da disputa exigiria ao menos uma reavaliação dessas condições. A aprovação posterior tampouco resolveria imediatamente o problema. Caso os certames sejam realizados sob a legislação atual e o Congresso altere o rateio antes da assinatura dos contratos, abre-se espaço para uma discussão sobre os efeitos da nova regra sobre um procedimento licitatório já realizado — e um horizonte de insegurança jurídica e regulatória sobre o primeiro leilão de baterias. Judicialização ainda não é consenso A possibilidade de recorrer à Justiça pedindo o adiamento do leilão por conta de uma possível revisão da remuneração já foi discutida por agentes do setor, mas não há consenso sobre a conveniência dessa estratégia. Na Associação Brasileira de Energia Eólica e Novas Tecnologias (Abeeólica), por exemplo, a hipótese de questionar judicialmente os leilões foi aventada, segundo fontes, mas encontrou resistência interna. A avaliação predominante é de que ainda há espaço para uma solução política, especialmente por meio da tramitação do projeto no Congresso. Dois partidos políticos também chegaram a sondar a possibilidade de questionamento da legislação na Justiça, segundo apurou o JOTA. Ainda assim, interlocutores avaliam que o caráter técnico da discussão e o prazo reduzido até dezembro tornam incerta a obtenção de uma eventual decisão cautelar capaz de suspender os certames. A Aneel, por sua vez, sustenta que a ausência de uma regulamentação definitiva do rateio não impede a realização dos leilões. O argumento é que os pagamentos começarão apenas com a entrada em operação dos sistemas, prevista para agosto de 2028. A agência já aprovou os editais e conduziu uma consulta pública específica sobre a metodologia de divisão do encargo entre os geradores, com alternativas que consideram a flexibilidade das usinas e sua contribuição para o atendimento do sistema. A separação da contratação entre armazenamento e outras formas de reserva de capacidade, como as termelétricas contratadas neste ano, deve ser feita apenas em 2026. O MME estabeleceu em portaria o planejamento dos leilões de 2027 a 2029 e passou a prever certames de reserva de capacidade que poderão considerar conjuntamente diferentes tecnologias, incluindo baterias, sistemas hidráulicos de armazenamento, hidrelétricas e termelétricas. artigo.texto: Gerando resumo A Associação Brasileira de Energia Eólica (Abeeólica) ingressou com uma ação civil pública, com pedido de tutela de urgência, para suspender a realização dos leilões de reserva de capacidade (LRCap) para contratação de sistemas de armazenamento por baterias, marcados para 2 e 4 de dezembro próximos, bem como os atos destinados à adjudicação, homologação e celebração dos contratos decorrentes do certame. A ação, apresentada na 17ª Vara Federal Cível do Distrito Federal contra a União e a Agência Nacional de Energia Elétrica (Aneel), questiona a legalidade da realização dos leilões sem a adequada definição do regime de custeio e, adicionalmente, a legitimidade da imposição desse encargo aos geradores de energia. Para a Abeeólica, o trecho da Lei nº 15.269/2025, conhecida como lei de modernização do setor elétrico, que determinou que o custo da contratação das baterias seja pago apenas pelos geradores de energia, ofende a ordem econômica, a isonomia, a legalidade e a segurança jurídica, por isso defende o reconhecimento de sua inconstitucionalidade. “Os leilões não podem ser realizados nas condições atuais. O vício está, antes de tudo, na própria regra que atribui aos geradores o custeio das baterias. O encargo que remunera as baterias tem natureza de preço público, e não de tributo. A consequência relevante dessa natureza é a exigência de nexo entre o custeio e a fruição ou o benefício da utilidade remunerada, o que inexiste no caso. Ao impor o custo a quem não é o beneficiário final, a lei produz transferência injustificada de ônus dos usuários finais aos geradores, por meio de medida desproporcional”, argumenta a ação, que cita que os custos de contratação de reserva de capacidade de maneira geral são arcados pelos usuários finais do sistema. Leia também - Bandeira tarifária em novembro segue verde, sem adicional na conta de luz - Moura estende parceria com chineses e investe R$ 200 milhões em fábrica de PE - Subsídios criam o modelo Robin Hood às avessas e deixam País com sobra de energia e risco de apagão A ação também aponta a existência de vício relacionado à estruturação dos leilões por falta de conclusão da regulamentação que definirá a metodologia de cálculo do montante que cada gerador pagará. “E a minuta da regulamentação em discussão pretende fazer alguns geradores pagarem até quatro vezes mais que outros, por critério que a lei não previu. Ao fazê-lo, a Aneel extrapola a delegação do § 6º e sua competência regulatória (art. 2º da Lei 9.427/1996). Esse vício diz respeito aos próprios leilões e subsistiria ainda que a lei fosse válida", diz. A presidente da Abeeólica, Elbia Gannoum, afirmou ao Estadão/Broadcast que a decisão de judicializar o leilão foi tomada a despeito do avanço de um projeto de lei que visa alterar a lei sobre o custeamento das baterias, em discussão no Congresso Nacional, devido ao prazo limite para entrar com a ação civil pública antes do certame. “Esse prazo limite se esgotou ontem, dia 16, e precisamos entrar com essa ação, e ela, de certa forma, reforça o sinal para o Legislativo resolver logo essa questão legal, porque existe essa ação civil pública e existe uma flagrante inconstitucionalidade nessa cobrança”, afirmou. Ela comentou que a Abeeólica também está preparando uma Ação Direta de Inconstitucionalidade (Adin) contra o trecho da lei que define os geradores como responsáveis por custear os sistemas de baterias. “A alocação do custo, por essa lei, foi totalmente equivocada, porque a bateria é um recurso que todo o sistema elétrico brasileiro recebe o benefício, o bônus, porém o ônus da bateria foi alocado só para os geradores de energia eólica e solar, então há um problema claríssimo de alocação ineficiente do custo, que o gerador não pode bancar, principalmente num sistema em que está gerando tanto curtailment (cortes de geração)”, disse, salientando que o sinal de investimento ficou deturpado, gerando insegurança entre empreendedores.

artigo.texto: Eight area emergency departments extinguished a Poynette garage fire just after noon on Sunday, Nov. 15. No one was injured by the blaze. According to an update from Carie Myers, public information officer for the Poynette-Dekora Fire Department, a call at 12:19 p.m. reported flames coming from a garage near Seward Street in the Village of Poynette. Fire units were enroute by 12:26 p.m. Both Poynette-Dekora EMS units were on calls at the time, so medical support was requested from Arlington EMS. “Our partners with the Poynette Police Department were first to arrive on the scene, locating the garage fire in the alley behind the residence,” wrote Myers on Facebook. “Our PPD officer immediately took action, initiating an aggressive attack on the fire with a fire extinguisher until fire resources arrived.” Crews kept the fire contained to the garage and the fire was reported under control by 12:53 p.m. Battery safety An official cause has not been determined, Myers wrote, but “preliminary information indicates the fire may have originated from an e-bike battery that was charging inside the garage.” She noted that the National Fire Protection Association (NFPA) has highlighted lithium-ion battery safety as part of its fire prevention education efforts, “Incidents like this serve as an important reminder of the potential dangers associated with these batteries when they are not property stored, charged or maintained,” she wrote. The NFPA advises consumers to stop using these batteries if they observe odor, a change in color, too much heat, a change in shape, leaking or odd noises. Lithium-ion batteries should not be disposed of in traditional recycling bins or they could ignite, the NFPA states. Instead, they should be taken to a safe battery recycling location, such as those listed at call2recycle.org.

artigo.texto: A expansão das fontes fotovoltaica e eólica na última década diversificou os modais do setor elétrico brasileiro (SEB), historicamente organizado em torno das hidrelétricas. Deste crescimento, porém, deriva o desafio de compatibilizar a geração de eletricidade a partir de fontes não despacháveis à flexibilidade do sistema, sem a qual a assincronia entre oferta de energia e oscilações de consumo exige cortes na geração. Chamados de curtailment, os cortes no sistema interligado nacional passaram de 18 TWh em 2024 para 58 TWh em 2025, segundo o ONS. O mesmo país que investe pesadamente na ampliação da oferta de energia, restringiu cerca de 20% da geração potencial solar e eólica no ano passado. Neste cenário, os sistemas de armazenamento de energia por baterias (“BESS”), assumem protagonismo no SEB. Eles guardam energia nos períodos de excedente, fornecendo-a nos horários de maior demanda. Desempenham parte das funções de flexibilidade associadas aos reservatórios hidrelétricos e às termelétricas. Enquanto a Lei Federal nº 15269/2025 garantiu reconhecimento institucional aos sistemas de armazenamento, a Portaria MME nº 136/2026 balizou as regras para os leilões de reserva de capacidade previstos para 2 e 4 de dezembro deste ano, criando condições para uma grande expansão do BESS no futuro próximo. Estes avanços institucionais, porém, contrastam com as regras ambientais, ainda em embrionária fase de construção. Diante disto, muitos agentes setoriais se apegam à crença de que o licenciamento do BESS será “simples” porquanto sua potencial associação a empreendimentos preexistentes reduziria a extensão das intervenções necessárias à implantação da nova tecnologia. Mesmo admitida a possibilidade de instalação do BESS em áreas antropizadas, os critérios adotados pelas oito unidades da federação que já regularam o enquadramento ambiental da tecnologia impõem limites às expectativas de simplicidade. Piauí e Rio Grande do Sul adotam a área útil, mas classificam o potencial poluidor como médio e baixo, respectivamente, e estabelecem limites distintos de não incidência de licenciamento. Bahia e Pará utilizam a potência; Ceará e Rio Grande do Norte, a capacidade de armazenamento. Goiás e Rio de Janeiro incluem baterias em categorias que também abrangem subestações. Em São Paulo e Minas Gerais, como na maioria dos estados, não foram identificados critérios de enquadramento para o BESS. Não surpreende, portanto, que as primeiras licenças ambientais emitidas para os sistemas de armazenamento de energia abranjam diferentes modalidades. Na Bahia, em julho de 2025, uma licença de alteração incluiu o sistema de armazenamento no Complexo Fotovoltaico Cedro. Em novembro do mesmo ano, o Rio Grande do Sul concedeu licenças prévias e de instalação unificadas aos BESS Pontal e Lagoa, vinculados a complexos eólicos. No dia 27 daquele mês, o Piauí emitiu licença prévia ao BESS Lagoa do Barro Associado, enquadrado em tipologia específica. Esses casos, além de contrariarem a doce ilusão de que a instalação das baterias em áreas intervindas afastaria automaticamente a incidência do rito ordinário, indicam que o BESS não será absorvido de modo homogêneo pelos órgãos licenciadores brasileiros. Os arranjos distintos (autônomo ou integrado) ajudam a explicar essa heterogeneidade, mas a ausência de diretrizes nacionais específicas pode submeter até mesmo projetos comparáveis a exigências severamente desiguais. Neste sentido, a normatização do licenciamento do BESS no Brasil aponta para um modelo híbrido. Sistemas diretamente associados a usinas solares, parques eólicos ou instalações de transmissão tendem a ser licenciados de forma integrada ao empreendimento principal, enquanto projetos standalone, especialmente aqueles voltados à oferta de potência e à prestação de outros serviços ao sistema, tendem ao enquadramento autônomo. A questão se torna particularmente sensível porque a expansão do BESS e a construção das regras ambientais específicas para a tecnologia coincidem com a reformulação do próprio licenciamento pela Lei Federal nº 15.190/2025. Com dispositivos do novo marco questionados no STF, os vultosos investimentos previstos para o BESS estão à mercê de algum grau de insegurança jurídica. Há, por fim, uma dimensão material que não pode ser subestimada. Baterias de íons de lítio apresentam riscos ambientais concretos (thermal runaway, incêndio e vazamento químico) e, após sua vida útil, tornam-se resíduos que exigem logística reversa, reciclagem e reprocessamento industrial. Essa estrutura permanece frágil no Brasil. O debate setorial avançou mais na dimensão operacional que na construção de uma cadeia robusta de pós-uso para baterias de grande porte. Assim, o desafio do licenciamento alcança tanto o BESS quanto a infraestrutura necessária ao tratamento e à destinação de suas baterias.

artigo.texto: Trinity Capital Inc. Provides $100 Million in Debt Financing to Accelerate Phononic's Growth and Manufacturing Expansion for AI Data Centers PHOENIX , Nov. 17, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Trinity Capital Inc. (NYSE: TRIN), a leading alternative asset manager, today announced the commitment of $100 million in debt financing to Phononic, a North Carolina-based company developing solid-state cooling solutions for AI data centers. The financing will support accelerated growth and manufacturing capacity expansion to meet increasing customer demand. Phononic's proprietary Thermal Control Systems™ provide software-defined cooling for AI infrastructure by combining high-performance thermoelectric devices with intelligent controls. Compact, solid-state devices and an integrated software control layer deliver precision cooling at the point of need for critical components, including GPUs, high-bandwidth memory, networking silicon, and the optical transceivers that connect them. Phononic's Thermal Fabric™ software layer monitors conditions throughout the data center and dynamically adjusts thermal control in real time as AI workloads change. Together, these solutions are designed to unlock greater AI infrastructure performance, optimize compute and facility capacity, and reduce energy and water consumption. "As AI hardware continues to evolve, we believe precise, real-time cooling at the chip level is becoming increasingly important," said Phil Gager, Senior Managing Director of Tech Lending at Trinity Capital. "Phononic has built the thermoelectric technology and software to address that need, and we're pleased to back their team as demand for their solutions continues to build." Phononic enters its next phase of growth as a profitable company backed by leading venture and growth-equity investors. With demand accelerating across AI infrastructure, the company is expanding manufacturing capacity to meet growing customer requirements and scale delivery of its intelligent thermal control solutions. "AI infrastructure is advancing at an unprecedented pace, and cooling has become a critical bottleneck to growth, limiting both facility capacity and compute and optical performance. Our customers are demanding disruptive thermal control solutions that can overcome these limitations at scale," said Dr. Tony Atti, CEO and Founder of Phononic. "Our partnership with Trinity Capital enables us to accelerate manufacturing capacity expansion to meet that demand and support the next wave of growth across AI infrastructure." About Trinity Capital Inc. Trinity Capital Inc. (NYSE: TRIN) is an alternative asset manager that seeks to deliver consistent returns for investors through access to private credit markets. Trinity Capital sources and structures investments in well-capitalized growth-oriented companies across five distinct lending verticals: Tech Lending, Equipment Finance, Healthcare & Life Sciences, Sponsor Finance, and Asset Based Lending. As a long-term, trusted partner for innovative companies seeking tailored debt solutions, Trinity Capital has deployed more than $6.8 billion across over 511 investments since inception in 2008 (as of September 30, 2026). Headquartered in Phoenix, Arizona, Trinity Capital's dedicated team is strategically located across the United States and Europe. For more information on Trinity Capital, please visit trinitycapital.com and stay connected to the latest activity via LinkedIn. About Phononic Phononic is a leader in software-defined thermal control for AI infrastructure, combining breakthrough solid-state cooling technology with intelligent hardware and software to unlock greater performance, efficiency, and reliability. Deployed across major U.S. hyperscalers, Phononic's solutions deliver precision thermal control at the source for optical connectivity, GPUs, high-bandwidth memory, and other critical AI components. Through its Thermal Control Systems™ and Thermal Fabric™ intelligence layer, Phononic enables real-time, workload-responsive thermal optimization that helps mitigate throttling, improve energy efficiency, and maximize AI infrastructure performance. For more information, visit www.phononic.com. artigo.texto: Residents urged to speak up as Salix weighs data center ordinances SALIX, Iowa (KTIV) - Community members gathered in Salix Monday evening for an informational meeting to discuss how local ordinances could shape the future of their community. This comes amid debate over a proposed Google data center. Attendees learned about data centers and asked questions about their potential local impact. Salix City Council members Gene Monk and Tim Skidmore attended the meeting. Organizers encouraged residents who want to see changes to continue speaking at City Council meetings and contacting elected leaders. “I think people need to show up. If there’s no one at the city council meeting, no one calling their numbers, they’re not going to change their minds,” said Jessica Mazour, conservation program coordinator for the Iowa Sierra Club. Woodbury County homeowner Janet Yanak said one of her biggest takeaways was the importance of getting local ordinances right. She also expressed concern about a data center’s potential impact on water and air quality. “The one thing that really did stick with me is how important it is to get these ordinances in and get them right,” Yanak said. “We really need some strict, some protective ordinances to protect not only the cities, but the citizens.” Residents were also encouraged to talk with their neighbors, write letters to the editor and contact state lawmakers about data center legislation. artigo.texto: Cirion lança Datrix para operar 12 data centers na América Latina Marca reúne instalações em seis países, incluindo o Brasil, e terá atuação voltada a hyperscalers, provedores de nuvem e aplicações de IA. A Cirion Technologies anunciou hoje (18) o lançamento da Datrix, marca que passa a identificar seu negócio de data centers na América Latina. A operação reúne 12 instalações distribuídas por Brasil, Argentina, Chile, Peru, Colômbia e Equador, com foco no atendimento à demanda por infraestrutura de nuvem, IA e computação de alta densidade. A criação da Datrix faz parte da intenção da Cirion em estabelecer uma identidade específica para suas operações de data centers, com liderança dedicada ao segmento. Nelson Fonseca ocupa o cargo de CEO da nova marca, enquanto Santiago Londoño permanece à frente da Cirion Technologies. A estrutura terá como público-alvo hyperscalers, provedores de serviços em nuvem, plataformas de conteúdo e empresas que necessitam de capacidade de processamento e armazenamento de dados em diferentes mercados latino-americanos. Modelo neutro de conectividade A Datrix atuará no modelo carrier-neutral, que permite aos clientes contratar serviços de conectividade de diferentes operadoras e fornecedores de redes. Nesse formato, as empresas instaladas nos data centers podem escolher seus prestadores de telecomunicações de acordo com suas necessidades operacionais. Segundo a Cirion, a nova marca utilizará a infraestrutura e os relacionamentos comerciais desenvolvidos pelo grupo na região para atender clientes atuais e novos. A estratégia contempla o fortalecimento da presença regional e a ampliação das capacidades de infraestrutura destinadas a organizações que buscam estabelecer ou expandir operações na América Latina. “A Datrix dá a essa experiência um foco claro no que vem pela frente: o rápido crescimento da nuvem e da inteligência artificial na América Latina”, afirmou Nelson Fonseca, CEO da Datrix. O lançamento ocorre em um contexto de expansão do setor na América Latina. Segundo dados da CBRE citados pela Cirion, o estoque regional de data centers cresceu 41,3% no primeiro trimestre de 2026, em comparação com o mesmo período do ano anterior, registrando a maior taxa de crescimento entre as regiões analisadas. A companhia associa esse movimento ao aumento da demanda por serviços de nuvem e aplicações de inteligência artificial, que exigem infraestrutura de processamento e armazenamento de dados. “O papel da América Latina na economia digital das próximas décadas será definido pela infraestrutura que construímos hoje”, declarou Santiago Londoño, CEO da Cirion Technologies. Com a Datrix, a Cirion passa a concentrar a identidade de suas operações de data centers em uma marca dedicada a esse mercado, mantendo a atuação regional e o modelo de infraestrutura neutra em relação aos fornecedores de conectividade. (Com assessoria de imprensa)

artigo.texto: Exchange Traded Concepts and Kiwoom Securities (USA) Launch KICK Space Data Center & Infrastructure Index ETF (Nasdaq: SDC) The second KICK ETF offers U.S. investors index-based exposure to the data center hardware and space infrastructure companies that may one day support computing in orbit. OKLAHOMA CITY , Nov. 18, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Exchange Traded Concepts, LLC ("ETC") and Kiwoom Securities (USA) Inc. today announced the launch of the KICK Space Data Center & Infrastructure Index ETF (Nasdaq: SDC), the second fund in the KICK ETFs lineup. SDC joins the KICK Korea Semiconductor Index ETF (NYSE Arca: KCHP), which began trading on September 15, 2026. AI is putting growing pressure on power grids. The International Energy Agency projects that global data center electricity demand will more than double by 2030, and grid connections have become a constraint for some new builds.1 That pressure has led some companies to explore whether data centers could one day operate in orbit, where certain orbits could offer near-constant sunlight, radiative cooling and no need for land.2,3 In October 2026, Google launched a prototype satellite carrying its AI chips and reported running an AI model on it in orbit.4,5 Starcloud, a privately held startup, has reported in December 2025 that it has trained an AI model on a GPU in space.6 The concept remains early-stage, with unresolved challenges in launch costs, radiation, maintenance and commercial viability.7 Putting computing in orbit would take more than a satellite. Data center hardware must process, move and store data, and space infrastructure would need to carry and support the equipment. SDC seeks to track, before fees and expenses, the Akros Space Data Center & Infrastructure Index ("the Index"), which holds up to 30 U.S.-listed companies across those two areas: data center hardware, including compute, networking and interconnect, and memory and storage; and space infrastructure, including launch, satellites and spacecraft, satellite services and ground equipment. Many of these companies may also serve ground data centers and other markets. Inclusion in the Index does not by itself mean a company operates an orbital data center or earns revenue from one. "Investors are being asked to make sense of AI infrastructure at a time when it is spreading in more directions than ever," said Garrett Stevens, Co-Founder and Chief Business Officer of Exchange Traded Concepts. "We believe they are better served when they know exactly which part of the buildout they own. KCHP offered investors focused access to Korea's semiconductor industry. SDC seeks to apply the same discipline to an earlier-stage frontier: the effort to extend data infrastructure into space." "Most of the conversation about AI infrastructure stays on the ground, with the chips, the power and the buildings," said Yoon Gu Eric Lee, President and Chief Executive Officer of Kiwoom Securities (USA) Inc. "The companies building the hardware and space systems that could support computing in orbit deserve a place in that conversation. With SDC, U.S. investors can access that segment through a rules-based index in a familiar ETF format." The Index is owned, calculated, administered and published by Akros Technologies, Inc.Akros ranks companies using NEXUS, its proprietary rubric-based framework that evaluates how central each company's business is to the Index theme. An Index committee reviews constituents for continued eligibility. The Index is reconstituted and rebalanced quarterly. The Index treats data center hardware and space infrastructure as separate sleeves and targets 15 companies in each. Each sleeve's share of Index weight is set by its number of constituents at every quarterly rebalance, and within each sleeve, companies are weighted by free-float market capitalization. Holdings and weights shift between rebalances, and current holdings are published daily at kicketfs.com/sdc. SDC seeks to track its Index by holding the stocks in the Index. Investors can buy and sell shares of the Fund through a standard brokerage account. About Kiwoom Securities (USA) Inc. Kiwoom Securities (USA) Inc. is the U.S. subsidiary of Kiwoom Securities Co., Ltd. Founded in 2000, Kiwoom Securities Co., Ltd. is a Korea-based financial services company offering securities brokerage, investment trading, discretionary investment and advisory services. The company is a core member of the Daou Kiwoom Group and serves investors through its online financial platform. Learn more about the parent company at www.kiwoom.com/h/ir/en/main and the KICK ETFs at www.KICKETFS.com. artigo.texto: Ekinops unveils PTM300 compact modular platform for ultra-high-capacity datacenter connectivity New 3RU* optical platform delivers up to 32 Tb/s capacity with ultra-low power consumption per bit, open management and multi-vendor interoperability PARIS , Nov. 16, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Ekinops (Euronext Paris - FR0011466069 – EKI), a leading provider of optical networks, connectivity and SASE cybersecurity solutions for telecom service providers and enterprises, today announces the release of PTM300, a new compact modular optical platform designed for high-capacity datacenter interconnect (DCI) and scale-across optical networking applications. Designed to bring carrier-class optical transport into a datacenter form factor, PTM300 delivers up to 32 Tb/s of client and line capacity in just 3RU, supporting up to 40 x 800 Gb/s coherent pluggable interfaces. The platform combines ultra-high density and ultra-low 0.08W per Gbps (watts per gigabit per second) power consumption with redundant power and cooling, front-to-back airflow, and Open management interface based on Openconfig and Netconf/Yang for easy integration into open, standards-based environments. It is also compatible with Ekinops' Celestis NMS for unified network management within an Ekinops optical network further simplifying integration. With PTM300, Ekinops is extending its optical networking portfolio to address increasing interconnection bandwidth requirements between datacenters with compact modular platforms that seamlessly enable the transition from the telco environment. High density without compromising openness and performance PTM300 can be deployed over direct fiber, existing Ekinops optical line systems or third-party infrastructure using alien wavelengths. Beyond DCI, it is designed to address metro, regional and long-haul transport applications as well as service regeneration for router-hosted IPoWDM applications. *RU = Rack Unit "The rapid growth of cloud and AI is creating unprecedented bandwidth requirements between data centers, as well a greater demand for service providers to deliver wavelength services to these locations. With PTM300, we are bringing together ultra-high capacity, ultra-low power consumption, operational simplicity and openness in a compact platform designed to help operators scale their optical networks while protecting existing infrastructure investments," said Philippe Moulin, Chief Operating Officer of Ekinops. PTM300 will be generally available in December 2026 with first customer deployments expected in Q1 2027. All press releases are published after Euronext Paris market close. artigo.texto: TECO Showcases AI Data Center and EV Powertrain Solutions in Poland WARSAW, Poland , Nov. 17, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- TECO Electric & Machinery Co., Ltd. (TWSE: 1504) will join the Taiwan Electrical and Electronic Manufacturers' Association (TEEMA) at the TEEMA Technology Park Industry Day – Poland, held November 17–18 in Warsaw. TECO will showcase its HULK 3.0 and HULK 6.0 Modular Data Center (MDC) solutions alongside next-generation EV powertrain systems, highlighting its integrated capabilities in AI infrastructure and electrification. HULK Series Accelerate AI Infrastructure Deployment HULK 3.0, designed for initial AI computing infrastructure deployment, features a 10-module configuration with an IT load capacity of 2.7 MW. It can accommodate 16 advanced computing systems and 12 IT racks. The cooling system combines Coolant Distribution Units (CDUs) and Computer Room Air Conditioning (CRAC) systems to support initial AI computing deployments. HULK 6.0, targeting high-density AI data center campuses, features a 22-module configuration with an IT load capacity of 4.2 MW per data hall. It can accommodate up to 16 advanced computing systems and 24 IT racks. The solution integrates power distribution, cooling, fire protection, and monitoring systems to meet the high reliability and electromechanical integration requirements of large-scale AI computing facilities. Through factory prefabrication and modular system integration, TECO reduces the complexity of on-site construction, enabling planned delivery timelines of as little as nine months for both solutions, with a design Power Usage Effectiveness (PUE) target of 1.2. These solutions allow hyperscale cloud providers, AI cloud and GPU computing service providers, and data center colocation operators to deploy infrastructure in phases, according to their evolving needs. High-Efficiency Hairpin Motors Drive Electrification TECO will also showcase its OD180 hairpin motor and EV powertrain portfolio, covering 50–410 kW and 250–800 V. Featuring high slot-fill windings, these motors deliver improved power density, reduced copper losses, enhanced cooling performance, and higher torque output within compact installation spaces. Applications include light commercial vehicles, 15–32-ton trucks, 9- and 12-meter electric buses, and off-highway equipment such as construction, agricultural, and mining machinery. By integrating motors, controllers, and reduction gearboxes, TECO provides complete EV powertrain solutions that improve efficiency, shorten development timelines, and support diverse commercial and industrial electrification needs. Through participation in the TEEMA exhibition, TECO aims to strengthen partnerships with Polish and European industries to expand opportunities in AI infrastructure and electrification markets. TECO has delivered nearly 1 GW of data center infrastructure worldwide and holds over 85% of Taiwan's electric bus powertrain market. artigo.texto: Hyperscale Data, Inc. Announces Intent to Launch Previously Announced Exchange Offer on or about November 20, 2026 LAS VEGAS , Nov. 17, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Hyperscale Data, Inc. (NYSE American: GPUS), an artificial intelligence ("AI") data center company ("Hyperscale Data" or the "Company"), today announced that it intends to commence its previously announced exchange offer to purchase up to 192,308,000 shares of its Class A Common Stock, $0.001 par value per share ("Common Stock") in exchange for units (the "Units") consisting of (a) $2.00 in cash and (b) one share of preferred stock with a stated value of $24.00 per share (the "Preferred Stock"), per 100 shares of Common Stock on or about November 20, 2026. The Company previously announced that it anticipated formally launching the exchange offer on or around November 17, 2026. Due to the recent global outages of various enterprise services, the Company is now anticipating formally launching the exchange offer on or about November 20, 2026, subject to board approval, regulatory approval and customary closing conditions. Details regarding the proposed exchange offer and instructions for stockholders interested in participating will be provided in the Offer to Exchange and related documents, which will be filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission (the "SEC") and distributed to the Company stockholders. The exchange offer will not be made to any person in any jurisdiction in which either the exchange offer, or solicitation or sale thereof, is unlawful. This press release is for informational purposes only and shall not constitute an offer to buy or sell Common Stock or any other securities. Any solicitation of offers to buy the Common Stock will only be made pursuant to an Offer to Exchange and related materials to be sent to the Company stockholders on the commencement of the exchange offer. Company stockholders should read such materials carefully when they become available because they will contain important information, including the terms and conditions of the proposed exchange offer. The tender offer documents will be available without charge at the SEC's website at http://www.sec.gov and will be delivered without charge to all stockholders of the Company who so request it. It is anticipated that the exchange offer will be made pursuant to the exemption from registration requirements of the Securities Act of 1933, as amended, contained in Section 3(a)(9) thereof. Under that exemption, if Common Stock exchanged is freely tradeable, the Preferred Stock received in exchange therefor will be freely tradeable. If the Common Stock is restricted, the Preferred Stock will be restricted to the same degree. Argentum is deploying NVIDIA B300 systems at the site in a fully Tier III environment, creating advanced, enterprise-grade infrastructure to run demanding AI applications at scale. Deployment is underway. The agreement provides Argentum access to a facility built for the power density of current-generation GPU systems and gives Argentum's customers a faster path to high-performance inference capacity. "Partnering with an established technology services and infrastructure provider like Kyndryl is an important milestone for Argentum AI," said Andrew Sobko, Founder & CEO, Argentum AI. "This agreement reflects our shared commitment to expanding secure, high-performance compute infrastructure and supporting the growing demands of enterprises embracing AI at scale." "Our agreement gives us a unique opportunity to put Kyndryl capacity to work in an innovative way, this coupled with our mission-critical capabilities, decades of operational and services experience will support Argentum as it creates capacity for its customers," said Jamie Rutledge, President, Kyndryl U.S. The facility welcomes a fast-growing, enterprise-grade AI inference company, whose technology powers some of the world's most widely used AI applications, as its flagship anchor tenant. Argentum AI and Kyndryl intend to broaden their collaboration to support Argentum's growth and evolving mission-critical enterprise AI infrastructure needs. About Argentum AI Argentum AI is a premium GPU cloud provider. The company originates, finances and operates GPU clusters, delivering dedicated bare metal GPU capacity to AI model builders, inference providers and enterprises. Argentum works with data center operators and builds capacity around customer demand, with a focus on speed of delivery, reliability and long-term partnerships. artigo.texto: Linxon and Fluence form Strategic Collaboration to advance integrated energy storage delivery Linxon and Fluence form Strategic Collaboration to advance integrated energy storage delivery - Collaboration combines Fluence's energy storage technology with Linxon's Mission Ready EPC approach, building on an initial 200 MWh project award in ERCOT. RALEIGH, N.C. and ARLINGTON, Va., November 17, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Linxon and Fluence Energy, Inc. today announced a strategic collaboration to pursue and deliver battery energy storage system projects through a more integrated OEM-EPC model. The collaboration combines Fluence's energy storage technology and expertise with Linxon's high-voltage engineering, grid integration and project execution capabilities. The collaboration has already contributed to securing a 200 MWh battery energy storage project in Texas'ERCOT market. Linxon and Fluence are also jointly pursuing additional opportunities across the energy storage and grid infrastructure markets. Linxon's high-voltage engineering, grid connection and complex EPC execution capabilities complement Fluence's energy storage technology and expertise. Together, the companies can address customer requirements spanning the battery energy storage system and the infrastructure required to connect it safely and reliably to the grid. Energy storage projects can separate technology supply, grid connection and EPC execution into distinct scopes, creating technical, commercial and schedule interfaces that must be resolved later in the project lifecycle. Linxon and Fluence intend to address these interfaces earlier by coordinating system requirements, engineering, constructability, procurement, commissioning and project execution from the development stage. By aligning technology, engineering, constructability, procurement, project execution and commissioning from the early stages of a project, Linxon and Fluence aim to reduce interfaces, anticipate risks and create a more competitive and predictable delivery model for customers. From managing interfaces to Engineering the Mission together At the center of the collaboration is a simple principle: align the battery system and grid infrastructure through a coordinated approach to planning, integration, and delivery. The objective is not simply to place two separate scopes alongside each other. It is to align technology, grid integration and project execution earlier, allowing the companies to identify interfaces, improve constructability and establish execution readiness before mobilization. Fluence brings its energy storage technology and expertise, while Linxon brings its EPC system integration and execution capabilities through its Mission Ready EPC approach. The collaboration incorporates Linxon's Mission Ready EPC approach, which focuses on preparing projects for successful execution before mobilization. Through early readiness planning, interface management, constructability reviews, risk identification, standardization and local capability development, Mission Ready EPC is designed to improve execution readiness and delivery predictability. The companies intend to apply these principles across future opportunities while maintaining the flexibility required to address customer specifications, market conditions and local project requirements. Together, the companies intend to create an integrated framework that can be applied across projects and markets, improving execution consistency while maintaining the flexibility required for specific customer needs. Building competitiveness before execution Earlier collaboration between the Fluence OEM and EPC is expected to create opportunities for standardized interfaces, repeatable engineering, improved constructability and more coordinated procurement and execution planning. The approach is also intended to support the progressive development of the engineering knowledge, training, field competencies and local delivery ecosystems required for future energy storage deployment. For customers, this can support earlier risk identification, clearer accountability and a more coordinated path from technology selection through grid connection and project delivery. "We want to redefine the traditional relationship between an OEM and an EPC," said Nicolas Sanloup, Managing Director Americas at Linxon . "This is not about one company providing technology and another executing around it. It is about engineering the mission together from the beginning. By combining Fluence's technology expertise with Linxon's Mission Ready EPC approach, our ambition is to anticipate interfaces, build competitiveness into the solution and develop local capabilities ahead of demand." "By bringing technology and EPC execution closer together from the outset, we have an opportunity to simplify project delivery and create a scalable and repeatable approach for our customers," said Jeff Monday, SVP and Chief Growth Officer, Fluence . "This collaboration reflects the purpose of Fluence PACE, our newly launched strategic partner program, which formalizes how we work with select partners whose capabilities complement our strengths. Our work with Linxon demonstrates how that model can support customers while creating opportunities for continued growth." A new way to deliver energy infrastructure The Linxon–Fluence collaboration is designed to move the OEM–EPC relationship from a transactional interface toward an integrated delivery ecosystem, combining technology, project integration and execution around a common mission. For customers, the ambition is clear: fewer interfaces, earlier alignment, greater competitiveness and more predictable execution. One technology strategy. One execution strategy. One mission.
