artigo.texto: O Brasil pode perder para o exterior a próxima onda de investimentos em data centers. A conclusão saiu de um painel em Lisboa que juntou a ANP, a agência que regula petróleo, gás natural e biocombustíveis, e a Eneva, do mercado de gás e energia, em torno das regras tributárias e energéticas do setor. O calendário aperta. Interlocutores ouvidos pela Agência iNFRA relatam que as tratativas dentro do Executivo avançaram e que o decreto do Redata, o Regime Especial de Tributação voltado aos Serviços de Data Center, deve sair ainda em novembro. Falta pacificar, porém, o ponto mais espinhoso do setor elétrico. Uma das hipóteses na mesa obriga os empreendimentos a contratar energia nova para se abastecer, exigência batizada de adicionalidade energética. Quem deu o tom do alerta foi Pietro Mendes, diretor da ANP, na Conferência Ibero-Brasileira de Energia (Coniben) 2026, em Lisboa, segundo apuração do site especializado Megawhat. Ele cobrou do governo federal celeridade para fechar as regras definitivas do programa. Na avaliação dele, o país já parte em desvantagem na disputa global por novos hubs de processamento de dados. Segundo ele, o país vai perdendo oportunidades e investimentos, e o capital acaba indo para outro lugar. O gás natural já consta da legislação do programa. Mendes, porém, criticou duas ideias em circulação, a de condicionar a participação das térmicas à captura e ao armazenamento de carbono e a de priorizar o biometano no abastecimento. A captura de carbono serve para mitigar os impactos da queima de combustíveis fósseis, mas vira barreira se transformada em obrigação, avaliou o diretor. Sobre o biometano, ele reconheceu papel relevante na transição energética e lembrou o limite atual, uma produção sem escala para usinas de grande porte. Critérios rígidos demais, na mesma leitura, castigariam o gás num país cuja matriz elétrica já tem peso enorme de fontes renováveis. Diretrizes engessadas, completou, espantam investidores internacionais de grande porte. O contraponto veio de Christiano Vieira, diretor de Regulação da Eneva. Para ele, a regulamentação precisa ir além da origem limpa da eletricidade contratada e contabilizar o custo de manter o abastecimento garantido. Data centers exigem eletricidade sem pausa, enquanto sol e vento variam ao longo do dia. Para Vieira, não faz sentido montar um modelo energético só com renováveis e deixar a conta da segurança do abastecimento para todos os usuários do sistema. O executivo defendeu preservar as metas de descarbonização e abrir caminho para que os empreendedores ofereçam potência e confiabilidade a preços competitivos, de térmicas a gás a sistemas de armazenamento. Citou empreendimentos que demandam entre 300 MW e 500 MW, escala que exige reforço no fornecimento. Baterias ajudam a dar qualidade à energia usada em aplicações de inteligência artificial. Não bastam, ponderou Vieira, para sustentar o funcionamento ininterrupto que os empreendimentos exigem. O decreto esperado para ainda este mês vai arbitrar o equilíbrio entre descarbonização, segurança de suprimento e custo. Errar a mão, na avaliação do diretor da ANP, empurra o capital para a concorrência internacional.

artigo.texto: - Owner’s-side partner will manage both ERCOT projects through commissioning to commercial operation date (COD), slated for 2027, strengthening grid resilience and helping lower power prices for Texas consumers. - Project wins build on boutique energy services firm’s expanding BESS portfolio in the Southwestern U.S. AUSTIN, Nov. 16, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Charge Power Inc.—the hands-on, owner’s-side energy storage partner—today announced it was awarded two battery energy storage system (BESS) projects in Texas to manage through commissioning: a 150-megawatt (MW) / 300-megawatt-hour (MWh) project and a 140 MW / 280 MWh project. Together, the projects will add 290 MW / 580 MWh of storage capacity to the ERCOT grid as Charge Power continues to build out its footprint in the rapidly expanding Southwestern U.S. energy storage market. On both projects, expected to reach commercial operation in 2027, Charge Power will integrate EPC contractors, project engineers, suppliers, documentation, and the ERCOT interconnection checklist—among other parties and processes—on the owner’s behalf. Its role is to close gaps in project delivery so that projects energize on time and earn from day one. During Charge Power’s involvement, both projects are also onboarding the WARAM platform for project governance, due diligence, and compliance. WARAM connects physical energy-asset requirements to the evidence that proves them, keeping that record current through ownership, certification, and transfer. “Texas is one of the most demanding storage markets in the country, and the stretch between construction and commercial operation is where a project either protects its returns or loses them,” said Ravi Pinnelli, founder and president of Charge Power. “We approach every project with an owner-operator mindset, so on these projects our decisions prioritize schedule, revenue, and long-term performance the way the owner would. Through shifting markets and an evolving energy landscape, our goal is to deliver execution certainty from day one to COD and beyond.” The wins extend Charge Power’s track record of protecting project outcomes for BESS owners. Since its founding in 2022, the company has commissioned 3 gigawatts (GW) / 7 gigawatt-hours (GWh) of energy storage, and its hands-on approach has saved owners more than $10 million in estimated avoided liquidated damages. Charge Power’s recent project awards come as energy storage demand in Texas continues to surge. Battery capacity on the ERCOT grid roughly doubled each year from 2020 through 2024 and grew another 76% in 2025, reaching 16.5 GW / 28.8 GWh by the end of June 2026, according to Modo Energy. Utility-scale storage captures lower-cost power when it is plentiful on the grid and delivers it when demand peaks, reducing the cost of power for consumers, cutting reliance on carbon-heavy peaker plants, and strengthening grid reliability. Batteries also respond in milliseconds to stabilize the grid and help it ride through extreme weather and sudden plant outages. According to an American Clean Power Association analysis, in Texas alone, storage deployed since 2023 has saved consumers over $750 million in electricity costs. About Charge Power Charge Power is the independent, hands-on, owner’s-side partner for energy storage. A boutique energy services firm with offices in Austin, Texas and Toronto, the company approaches every project with an owner-operator mindset from design through commissioning and beyond. It closes the gaps between contractors during project delivery, keeping everything aligned on the owner’s behalf, so projects energize on time and earn from day one. As a battery energy storage system (BESS) specialist with deep grid and market expertise, Charge Power optimizes long-term performance and fixes small problems before they become expensive ones, preserving revenue and uptime—and protecting project outcomes. The result: execution certainty in an evolving energy landscape. Founded in 2022 by BESS industry veterans, Charge Power has commissioned 3 GW / 7 GWh of energy storage across U.S. energy markets — including CAISO, ERCOT, MISO and PJM — as well as Canada, India, Japan and the U.K. Learn more at www.chargepowerinc.com. artigo.texto: EUA restringem venda de chips de IA para data centers no Brasil Nova norma exige licença governamental para exportação por suspeita de “desvios” em 5 países O Departamento de Comércio dos Estados Unidos publicou nesta 2ª feira (16.nov.2026) uma norma que exige licença governamental para a exportação, reexportação ou transferência de chips avançados de inteligência artificial destinados a data centers fora do território norte-americano. O Brasil está entre os 5 países com restrições imediatas. Leia a íntegra da norma provisória (PDF – 694 KB). A norma não impede o Brasil de adquirir chips norte-americanos. O que muda é a necessidade de aprovação prévia do governo dos EUA para cada operação. A regra foi elaborada pelo Departamento do Tesouro e pelo Conselho de Segurança Nacional dos EUA e publicada pelo BIS (Bureau of Industry and Security), órgão do Departamento de Comércio. O objetivo declarado é impedir que restrições já existentes ao acesso a tecnologias sensíveis fabricadas nos EUA sejam contornadas por meio de arranjos de computação remota em data centers instalados em outros países. Além do Brasil, Indonésia, Malásia, Singapura e Tailândia integram o grupo de países classificados como de “risco elevado de desvio de tecnologia”. Para essas nações, passa a ser obrigatória a autorização do governo norte-americano antes de qualquer exportação ou transferência de semicondutores avançados. “Esses países estão sendo incluídos em resposta a preocupações de que itens de computação avançada, sujeitos aos requisitos de licenciamento do EAR [Regulamentos de Administração de Exportações], estejam sendo desviados –sem autorização– para entidades e países que suscitam preocupações”, diz o documento do governo norte-americano. A exigência de licença não se aplica a chips destinados a empresas com sede ou cuja controladora final tenha sede nos Estados Unidos, desde que determinados requisitos de reporte sejam cumpridos. O secretário de Comércio pode incluir outros países na lista, mediante consulta ao secretário de Estado ou ao assessor de Segurança Nacional da presidência. O Departamento de Comércio afirmou que vai monitorar ativamente países que tolerem o descumprimento da norma. As consequências estabelecidas para casos de evasão são: - restrições a importações; - novos requisitos de licença para exportação de semicondutores avançados; - rebaixamento do status do país no regime de controle de exportações dos EUA; - proibições temporárias de exportação para pessoas físicas ou jurídicas estrangeiras envolvidas nessas atividades. Segundo o Departamento de Comércio, a medida responde ao avanço da computação em nuvem e da infraestrutura de “superinteligência”, que tornaram crescentemente possível o acesso remoto a capacidades computacionais avançadas dos EUA por meio de data centers localizados fora dos países sujeitos às restrições de exportação vigentes. CASO NVIDIA A norma foi publicada dias depois do escândalo envolvendo Jensen Huang, ex-CEO da Nvidia. A fabricante de chips abriu uma investigação interna para apurar se o executivo foi alvo de espionagem –a mulher com quem ele se relacionou fora do casamento é suspeita de ser uma espiã chinesa. Huang já criticou as restrições impostas pelos EUA à venda de chips para a China.

artigo.texto: SiTime Addresses $2 Billion Opportunity in Data Center Bandwidth Upgrades with Two New Clock Families FemtoClock 4 and VersaClock 8 Bring 20 Years of Heritage to 2X Faster Ethernet and Connectivity Standards SANTA CLARA, Calif.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Nov. 17, 2026-- SiTime Corporation (NASDAQ: SITM), the Precision Timing company, today introduced FemtoClock™ 4 and VersaClock® 8, two clock families designed for the latest connectivity protocols that double bandwidth over previous generations. The families are designed for networking and computing applications in the data center rack. Together they address a $2 billion serviceable addressable market (SAM) over the next five years. This press release features multimedia. View the full release here: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20261117222922/en/ FemtoClock 4 and VersaClock 8 Bring 20 Years of Heritage to 2X Faster Ethernet and Connectivity Standards “Insatiable demand for AI, along with rising performance requirements, is driving the need for greater density and speed,” said Piyush Sevalia, executive vice president and chief business officer of SiTime. “The FemtoClock and VersaClock families have a 20-year heritage and multiple generations of products. Over this period, they have led the industry in performance, density and shipments, and have become the default choice for many customer designs. Engineers know these architectures well. This familiarity enables them to design with confidence, get the most from these programmable clocks and reuse existing software. The result is higher-performance, denser AI hardware that generates revenue sooner. Built on this successful track record, FemtoClock 4 and VersaClock 8 extend SiTime’s lead in Precision Timing.” These clocks are built to solve the bandwidth challenge and the industry is tackling it right now; 224G serializer-deserializer (SerDes) links are being rapidly adopted in data center switches and AI servers to double Ethernet bandwidth, and PCI Express® (PCIe®) 7 is doing the same for interconnectivity between CPUs, xPUs, memory, storage and smart network interface cards (SmartNICs). In faster, denser systems, the margin for error is smaller. FemtoClock 4 delivers resilient clock signals for Ethernet networking with ultra-low jitter and high clock density in a single device. VersaClock 8 serves PCIe interconnectivity with a flexible, compact, low-power design that is ideal for hot and dense compute trays. According to Dell’Oro Group, 1.6 Tbps ports in AI back-end switches are expected to ramp at least five times faster than 800 Gbps, driven by adoption across scale-up, scale-out and scale-across networks. This bandwidth is critical to maximizing utilization of expensive xPU resources. “The AI infrastructure build-out is exposing bottlenecks that go well beyond GPU compute performance,” said Dave Altavilla, president and principal analyst at HotTech Vision and Analysis. “Moving data efficiently across increasingly complex systems is becoming a critical design challenge, particularly as Ethernet and PCIe bandwidth requirements continue to climb. Precision Timing plays an important role here, especially as higher signaling speeds leave less margin for jitter and signal degradation. SiTime’s latest clock families reflect how these underlying technologies are evolving to meet the precise needs of the next generation of AI data center architectures.” Product Features FemtoClock 4 is a jitter attenuator and clock generator for top-of-rack and spine switches built on 224G SerDes. Key features include: - 19 fs RMS phase jitter at 312.5 MHz in clock generator mode (12 kHz to 20 MHz, 4 MHz high-pass filter) - Up to six frequency domains across 18 outputs - Fewer devices for top-of-rack switches that generally need more than 40 clocks VersaClock 8 is a programmable clock generator providing reference clocks for CPUs, xPUs, memory and storage. Key features include: - About 10 fs reference clock jitter for PCIe 7 - 30 fs RMS phase jitter at 312.5 MHz (12 kHz to 20 MHz, 4 MHz high-pass filter) - Low power limits self-heating; operates at up to 105°C - 5-, 9- and 12-output variants in QFN packages from 4x4 mm to 6x6 mm - 12-output variant is about 40% smaller than a comparable solution Availability FemtoClock 4 and VersaClock 8 are in production and available now. FemtoClock 4 part numbers: RC38616, RC38412, RC32418 and RC32412. VersaClock 8 part numbers: RC31312A, RC31309A and RC31305A. Additional Resources About SiTime SiTime is the Precision Timing company. Our people and products help engineers build the impossible. Customers trust SiTime solutions in more than 400 applications, including AI hardware, autonomous vehicles, low Earth orbit satellites and wearables. Built on decades of innovation, our oscillators, clocks, resonators and software deliver higher system performance, greater resilience and better reliability. For more information, visit www.sitime.com. artigo.texto: O Brasil está abraçando uma oportunidade que ninguém quer deixar escapar. Com investimentos bilionários anunciados, a expansão acelerada da inteligência artificial e a crescente importância da capacidade computacional, atrair grandes data centers virou uma aposta de desenvolvimento econômico e tecnológico. Mas a pressa para entrar nessa corrida pode estar passando por cima de uma avaliação criteriosa sobre os ganhos e principalmente sobre as perdas para o país. Essa conta começa pelo que o conceito de "nuvem" esconde. O uso da IA mobiliza servidores que demandam muitíssima energia e refrigeração, apoiados em instalações que ocupam território e dependem de redes elétricas e de fontes de água. Por isso, a conveniência digital tem uma contrapartida material e ambiental. Esse tema ganhou outra dimensão durante o 2º Seminário de Inteligência Artificial, Meio Ambiente e Justiça Socioambiental, organizado pelo Lapin (Laboratório de Políticas Públicas e Internet) em Fortaleza, entre os dias 8 e 10. A programação incluiu uma visita ao território Anacé, nas proximidades do Complexo Industrial e Portuário do Pecém, onde está sendo construído um grande data center para o TikTok. Assim, a discussão deixou de ser apenas sobre tecnologia e ganhou endereço e rostos. Essa promessa foi encampada pelas propostas dos principais candidatos à presidência da República, incluindo as de Lula. Ampliar a capacidade computacional, desenvolver serviços de IA, estimular pesquisa e gerar empregos qualificados são objetivos legítimos. Mas investimentos bilionários não garantem, por si só, benefícios distribuídos nem ganhos tecnológicos proporcionais aos recursos que o Brasil oferece. Nos Estados Unidos, governos locais já impõem restrições aos data centers. Se quem recebe esses empreendimentos há mais tempo começa a impor limites, o Brasil precisa entender que questionamentos não representam necessariamente oportunidades perdidas, fazendo parte de uma busca pelo equilíbrio necessário. Veja esse artigo em vídeo: Esse equilíbrio exige questionar a ideia de que temos energia limpa sobrando. Nossa matriz elétrica é predominantemente renovável, mas há cortes por limitações da rede, segurança operacional e falta de demanda em certos horários. De janeiro a abril de 2026, eles atingiram 2.843 MW médios de geração eólica e solar, sendo 2.233 MW no Nordeste. Essa energia desperdiçada não pode ser automaticamente direcionada aos data centers, pois isso depende da localização, da capacidade da rede e de novos investimentos em transmissão e conexão. Além disso, data centers precisam dissipar o calor dos equipamentos e algumas tecnologias de refrigeração consomem volumes expressivos de água. Mesmo nos mais modernos, não basta medir a eficiência hídrica, pois uma instalação grande pode ter baixo consumo relativo e ainda retirar muita água do local. No Pecém, além da captação subterrânea, o projeto prevê 120 geradores de emergência a diesel, entre outros impactos sobre o território. - Assine gratuitamente minha newsletter sobre IA, experiência do cliente, mídia e transformação digital - Inscreva-se no meu podcast (escolha a plataforma): Spotify, Deezer, Apple Podcasts ou Soundcloud No dia 15 de setembro, o Brasil instituiu o Redata, regime que reduz tributos sobre equipamentos em troca de pesquisa no país, atendimento ao mercado interno, uso de energia renovável ou de baixa emissão e eficiência hídrica. Mas parte dos critérios depende de regulamentação, e é preciso demonstrar que o retorno público justifica a enorme vantagem privada. "Quando o governo fala de soberania digital e acha que trazer data centers para o território é garantia de soberania, ele está errado", afirma Cynthia Picolo, diretora-executiva do Lapin. Ela distingue as meras presenças físicas do controle sobre suas finalidades, a gestão dos recursos naturais e a governança. "Ter a infraestrutura no território não é o mesmo que controlá-la." Soberania também exige respeitar quem vive no território. Os Anacé afirmam que seu protocolo de consulta não foi respeitado, enquanto o Ministério Público Federal e a Defensoria Pública da União questionam a suficiência do licenciamento daquele data center. Ao defender a repartição justa de benefícios, a defensora pública Thalita Verônica ressaltou durante o evento que "isso não se confunde com escola, estrada, água potável, que já são uma obrigação do Estado". Fazendo do jeito certo Não se trata, portanto, de rejeitar a tecnologia ou de impedir investimentos, mas de estabelecer as condições para que eles beneficiem o país respeitando os direitos da população. "Para mim, é possível atrair data centers de uma forma sustentável, ética e segura", explica Edson Prestes, professor da Universidade Federal do Rio Grande do Sul. "Mas, para isso, a gente não pode 'colocar a carroça na frente dos bois'." Isso começa antes da aprovação e dos incentivos, avaliando a disponibilidade de água, a capacidade elétrica, a vegetação, as áreas protegidas e os direitos das comunidades tradicionais. Não basta examinar o terreno do data center, sendo necessário avaliar toda a infraestrutura que o sustenta e os impactos somados aos de outros empreendimentos. O licenciamento deve exigir estudos proporcionais ao porte e ao potencial de impacto, com participação pública. E a fiscalização não pode terminar na licença. As empresas envolvidas devem divulgar dados verificáveis sobre consumo e eficiência no uso de água e de energia, emissões e resíduos. Picolo defende o acompanhamento dos efeitos da disputa por recursos sobre as comunidades e outras atividades locais. Cabe ao poder público fiscalizar impactos e contrapartidas durante toda a operação, com verificação independente dos dados apresentados. Além disso, o investimento só se transforma em desenvolvimento quando deixa conhecimento e capacidade no país. Isso exige formar profissionais, fortalecer centros de pesquisa, transferir tecnologia e desenvolver fornecedores nacionais. Os recursos destinados à pesqui

artigo.texto: How Google's data center investment has impacted Pryor schools While some communities are weighing promises from data center developers, the City of Pryor has already spent years seeing what that kind of investment can mean for local schools. In Pryor, students can end the school day with a paddle in hand through after-school activities the district offers at no cost. Superintendent Lisa Muller said a stronger tax base, boosted by Google’s investment, has helped make programs like that possible. “We're able to provide that as a free program for our students after school,” Muller said. Google’s data center sits inside the Pryor school district, and Muller said the investment significantly increased school revenue. The funding comes in part from property taxes Google pays. In addition, Google has received tax breaks, and the state makes up for that tax revenue and sends it to Pryor schools. Pryor’s original agreement with Google included that money from the company’s tax exemptions going to the district. The impact extends beyond the school district. For the 2025 tax year, the Oklahoma Tax Commission lists about $34.2 million in Google-related reimbursements for Mayes County. That figure is countywide, but Pryor benefits as well. “It’s difficult to separate out, you know, what portion comes from the companies out at the, the industrial park versus what comes from other taxpayers within the district,” Muller said. The laws governing those incentives have changed since Google made its agreement in Pryor. Since 2021, new data centers can’t qualify under the same program. Certain existing facilities can still qualify for breaks on eligible equipment. “And so that's when we end up with these very different structures, that change over time just to fit the needs of the community,” said Trystine Payfer with Google. Payfer said new deals can include company payments in place of property taxes or other negotiated payments to the community, and what reaches schools depends on how each agreement divides those payments. “And this is all separate, of course, from the additional grants and scholarships and sponsorships that we do once we enter a community,” Payfer said. Muller said the additional revenue has helped Pryor keep classes small and pay staff above state minimums. “So just on the sort of the big picture question, like, does money matter? The answer is, is unambiguously yes,” Muller said. Northwestern economist Kirabo Jackson, who studies what happens when schools spend more, said how districts use additional funding is key. “You want to make sure that money is going towards things that improve instruction. You want to make sure that's going towards curriculum, that improves things. You want to make sure it's going towards reducing class size,” Jackson said. Muller said Pryor has seen academic improvement over time tied to the Google investment, and she pointed to staffing and class sizes as part of that progress. “We also maintain small class sizes here in Pryor and are able to pay our, our staff above the state minimums as well,” Muller said. The district’s state report card has continuously improved since the investment began, and the district has funding to provide opportunities and transportation for students and families even after the school day ends.

artigo.texto: SALT LAKE CITY — In response to significant public pushback, a draft policy has been unveiled on Utah's Capitol Hill seeking to regulate data centers. "Utahns have legitimate serious questions about the impacts of data centers," said Rep. Paul Cutler, R-Centerville, who is sponsoring a bill setting up new guardrails on them. Salt Lake City approves temporary data center pause: On Wednesday, the Utah State Legislature's Economic Development & Workforce Services Committee heard a presentation on the draft policy. Senate Majority Leader Chris Wilson, R-Logan, who is co-sponsoring the bill, called the policy proposal a "herculean effort." FOX 13 News reported on pending data center legislation last week. House Speaker Mike Schultz, R-Hooper, has tasked lawmakers with bills on the topic and has said in the past he is not supportive of mass data center development. The policy proposes to cut off some of the tax incentives offered lately to data center developers. It also strips entities like Utah's Military Installation Development Authority of their ability to approve the projects. Instead, decisions on data center approval will remain with local cities and counties. Ready for liftoff? Spaceport idea advances on Utah's Capitol Hill: "I assume when you say local control, that will mean that entities like MIDA and others won’t have super-authority over that?" Rep. Jim Dunnigan, R-Taylorsville, asked during Wednesday's hearing. "That’s the intent," replied Rep. Cutler. "That MIDA or the inland port could support and consult and help provide expertise, but the proposal has to be endorsed and come from a local community, either a municipality or a county. MIDA can’t override those." Elected or appointed officials will not be allowed to enter into nondisclosure agreements around data centers and there will be more disclosures demanded on environmental and energy impacts for the public, Rep. Cutler said. There will be a shift in tax money generated from data centers, earmarking some of it for local schools and environmental impact funds. Data centers will be required to provide "benefits" to water resources, including investments in things like donating water to the Great Salt Lake or Colorado River systems. They must also address air quality, noise, heat and other impacts to the environment. "The intent is to put in place policies to make sure data centers are water responsible in their use," Rep. Cutler told reporters after the hearing. "That only closed loop system or better technologies is allowed for cooling. No evaporative cooling is allowed." Massive opposition to data center projects led to some legislators losing their seats and new lawmakers being voted in. On Wednesday, some new lawmakers who have been data center critics were sitting in the committee with members of the public and lobbyists, watching the presentation. "I think there’s still a question of whether we want data centers at all," said Rep.-elect Kim James, D-Ogden. She told reporters that the proposed bill is "a great start in the conversation" and she appreciated local input, but still had a lot of questions about the proposal as no legislation had been formally introduced. Other environmental groups who sat in the audience watching declined to comment on Rep. Cutler's proposal without seeing additional language. Asked by FOX 13 News about the idea of allowing data center development with guardrails, Rep. Cutler replied: "Data centers will happen. But we can make sure that in Utah, only the best projects that respect our natural resources, that benefit our local communities happen in Utah." Deeda Seed with the Center for Biological Diversity told FOX 13 News the draft proposal is "window dressing" and she did not see substantive changes in how the state incentivizes data center projects. "These are the things that we as community members, people of Utah, need to ask for a statewide moratorium on data center development with real protections," she said. "Because what was described today provides no real protections." Sen. Wilson told reporters that there will be a lot of opportunity for public input on the bill when it's deliberated during the 2027 legislative session that begins in January. "We don’t have the public’s opinion yet, which will be very important as it comes to committee," he said. "We don’t have the input yet."

artigo.texto: Good afternoon! It’s Wednesday, and the midterm elections feel both a lifetime ago and like they happened just yesterday. My colleagues want to know your thoughts on our coverage to help shape our future plans. Here’s what you need to know today. 1. AI data centers are blocking pollution reduction and climate efforts in Illinois Under an ambitious law signed by Gov. JB Pritzker in 2021, the state set out to retire all fossil-fuel power plants between now and 2050. But big new data centers require so much electricity that it’s become difficult for the state to shut down all coal, gas and oil sources used to meet demand, a pair of state reports released this week found. As my colleague Brett Chase writes, the findings confirmed fears environmental and climate advocates have had for more than a year. Cleaner sources of power, including wind and solar farms, are not being built quickly enough to keep up with new demands from data centers being used to power artificial intelligence. That’s bad news for the planet because oil, gas and coal create carbon dioxide, the major contributor to global warming. The same pollution causing climate change is also bad for our health, causing respiratory problems and exacerbating a number of other threats. In central and southern Illinois, seven coal plants still operate. The goal has been to shut four of them down by 2030 and that goal remains, according to one of the two reports. Three publicly owned coal-fired plants have longer timelines before they are closed. Eleven so-called peaker plants, which burn oil or natural gas as power backups, were expected to close in 2030 or 2031. But those plants should continue to operate until 2033 to help prevent blackouts when demand peaks, such as on the hottest days of the year, the report recommends. In Chicago, peakers are still active at the long-closed Fisk coal-fired power plant in Pilsen. There are also peakers in Waukegan, where a former coal plant that has operated for more than 90 years will keep operating until 2033 under the state recommendation. [Chicago Sun-Times] After expensive campaigns where voters were pummeled with mailers, digital ads and, for the president’s race, incessant negative commercials, a WBEZ/Chicago Sun-Times analysis of Chicago Board of Election voter data shows how the winning candidates managed to rack up votes. Biggs, who won with 49% of the vote, did best in majority-white areas where fewer families send their children to public school. But she also outdid her two opponents in predominately Black areas, though she didn’t get a majority of votes. Biggs did particularly well on the North and Far Northwest sides, where voter turnout was high and people voted overwhelmingly for Biggs. In these areas, which include the wealthy Lincoln Park area and more grassroot liberal areas in Rogers Park, Biggs received more votes than both opponents combined. Black voters may have favored Biggs because, as a former teacher and principal serving on the board, she had the most experience in the education system, said Rufus Williams, a former school board president under Mayor Richard M. Daley and a host on WVON, a radio station that caters to Chicago’s Black community. But in parts of the South Side, West Side and majority-Latino neighborhoods on the Northwest Side, Hilario Dominguez and Victor Henderson combined got more votes than Biggs. Dominguez, who is Latino, alone received almost half of all votes in majority-Latino neighborhoods. [WBEZ/Chicago Sun-Times] New Pew Research Center projections show Muslims are poised to become one of the fastest-growing religious populations in North America. In west suburban Berwyn, a Latino-led mosque reflects the changing face of Islam, Christiana Freitag reports for the Chicago Sun-Times. In February, on the first day of Ramadan, Ojala Islamic Center opened as the Midwest’s first Latino-led mosque, offering converts a place to practice Islam while maintaining ties to their cultural heritage. Christopher AbdulKareem Pavlicek, the founder who serves as imam, said the congregation is as much “convert-led” as it is “Latino-led,” with much of its community made up of people from different religious and cultural backgrounds who are embracing Islam for the first time. Nelson Julio-Polanco, born in the Dominican Republic and raised Catholic, found a sense of belonging at Ojala, which offers services in Arabic, English and Spanish. As the only Muslim in his family, Julio-Polanco said speaking Spanish with other Muslims made the community especially welcoming. “When they founded this organization, I felt like, wow, I can speak Spanish to these people and they’re Muslims too,” he said. “We have the same culture.” [Chicago Sun-Times] 4. The David Byrne-backed ‘Theater of the Mind’ will end its Chicago run in January As WBEZ theater reporter Mike Davis writes, the fully immersive show opened in March as an experimental addition to the Goodman Theatre’s 100th season. The production, located in the Reid Murdoch building Downtown, received mostly positive reviews. (Davis wrote in March that the show “exists somewhere in the margins of creepy festival funhouse meets cool high school science experiment. It’s trippy. It’s unique. And somewhere buried in the cool head tricks there is a story about revisiting the pivotal moments of our lives and questioning if we can trust our own recollections.”) An ambitious project created by Byrne and Mala Gaonkar, “Theater of the Mind” takes audiences on a journey through their own memories. Directed by immersive theater aficionado Andrew Scoville, the production features lifelike sets, hands-on experiments and a tour guide named David clad in the fashion of a childhood David Byrne. The production utilized 19,000 square-feet of space to drive home the desired feeling of audiences being transported into another reality. Nearly 50,000 people have seen the 75-minute show, according to the Goodman. [WBEZ] 5. Here’s where to dine in and order

artigo.texto: Ford bets on CATL know-how to bring cheap LFP batteries to U.S. EVs Ford has started making lithium iron phosphate (LFP) battery cells in the United States with technology licensed from CATL, China’s battery giant. The Detroit automaker hopes the cells will help it build cheaper electric vehicles and challenge Chinese rivals. Ford said its first LFP prismatic cells have come off the line at BlueOval Battery Park Michigan in Marshall. They are headed to Louisville Assembly Plant in Kentucky to power prototypes of the Fathom, Ford’s upcoming midsize electric pickup. Ford says the milestone puts it “in the battery business” and claims it will be the first company to deliver LFP batteries in the U.S. for mainstream consumer vehicles. Cell production at the roughly 3 billion USD plant, about 100 miles west of Detroit, began last month. CATL supplies the technology and manufacturing support, but Ford owns and runs the plant. Why LFP, and why CATL LFP cells contain no nickel or cobalt, which keeps costs down, and they hold up well over many years of charging, according to Ford. The company picked rectangular prismatic cells because they fit directly into the chassis, allowing the battery pack to act as part of the vehicle’s structure and cutting structural costs. Ford said it spoke with battery makers around the world before choosing CATL. It wanted a technology that was “proven in the field, ready to manufacture at scale”, and CATL’s batteries power some 30 million vehicles worldwide. “If we want to get to being able to produce affordable EVs in the United States, we need to also do it the fastest way possible,” Alan Clarke, Ford’s vice president of advanced development projects, said during a tour of the plant. “CATL being the biggest in the world means that they’re the best supplier to get us that technology and help us learn ourselves how to produce LFP cells.” LFP chemistry was invented in the U.S. but commercialised mostly in China. CATL staff helped Ford ramp up the Marshall plant by providing training and manufacturing expertise. Capacity and timeline Ford says the Marshall lines can turn out 40 cells per minute, which it calls among the fastest LFP prismatic lines outside China, and that the site has room to expand. Workers use AI-powered image recognition to catch defects, with a goal of measuring the defect rate per billion cells rather than per million. That pace works out to about 20 gigawatt-hours a year for EVs and Ford’s energy storage business. The original plan was up to 40 GWh, but Ford scaled back as it and the broader industry slowed their EV push. Ford says it is still early in certifying its processes. It plans to increase cell output next year, ahead of the Fathom’s expected launch in the fourth quarter of 2027. A battery pack plant in Marshall is due to open in 2027. The Fathom will start at 28,350 USD for the standard-range model, and Ford plans to open preorders in early 2027. What Ford learns in Marshall is also feeding into Ford Energy’s plans for battery energy storage production in Glendale, Kentucky. Political headwinds The project has drawn criticism in Washington. Some lawmakers and Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy have objected to Ford’s ties with CATL. In September, Duffy wrote to Ford CEO Jim Farley expressing “profound concern” about the company’s links to Chinese firms. The White House praised Ford’s U.S. jobs and manufacturing the next day. In January, Rep. John Moolenaar, a Michigan Republican who chairs a House committee, asked Ford whether its CATL licensing terms had been “updated, expanded, or otherwise altered” to fit its new focus on energy storage and data centre batteries. Ford replied that expanding domestic LFP production is “an investment in American workers” and said it is confident the batteries meet tax credit requirements. The start of shipments comes the same week President Donald Trump is meeting Chinese leader Xi Jinping at the APEC summit in Shenzhen.

artigo.texto: German company wpd plans to repower one more of its wind farms in Croatia. The Orlice wind farm will not only have more powerful wind turbines, but also a 10 MW battery energy storage system. Wpd earlier initiated the procedure to repower its Trtar-Krtolin wind farm (11.2 MW), the second-oldest wind power plant in Croatia. In addition, the company has announced plans to convert the Katuni wind farm into a hybrid power plant by adding a solar park. Wpd is one of the pioneers in renewable energy in Croatia. The Orlice wind farm was commissioned in 2009 as the third wind power plant in the country. It comprises 11 Enercon wind turbines with a total installed capacity of 9.6 MW. It is located on the territory of the city of Šibenik, within Šibenik-Knin county. Repowered plant to feature three wind turbines The company plans to dismantle and remove the existing 11 wind turbines and install three new units with an individual capacity of 6 MW. Three new foundations will be constructed for the new turbines at the locations of the existing foundations. The planned total installed capacity of the wind farm upon repowering would reach up to 20 MW, according to the environmental protection study for the repowering project. The investor plans to revegetate, with indigenous flora, approximately 1,500 meters of access roads that will no longer be in use. Wpd’s newest wind farm was commissioned in 2017 The environmental protection study was submitted by the company Vjetroelektrana Orlice to the Ministry of Environmental Protection and Green Transition alongside a request for an environmental impact assessment (EIA) screening for the repowering of the Orlice wind farm. In Croatia, wpd also operates the Ponikve wind farm on the Pelješac peninsula. It is its largest one, at 38.6 MW. Wpd’s most recently commissioned facility is the 34.2 MW Katuni wind farm, which came online in 2017.

artigo.texto: Blackstone Digital Infrastructure Trust Announces $5 Billion Acquisition of Stabilized Data Center Portfolio NEW YORK--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Nov. 16, 2026-- Blackstone Digital Infrastructure Trust Inc. (NYSE: BXDC) today announced that it has signed a definitive agreement to acquire a 75% majority interest in two joint ventures with Amazon Web Services (“AWS”), in a transaction valued at approximately $5 billion reflecting an initial capitalization rate of 7.0%. The transaction represents BXDC’s inaugural investment and advances its strategy of acquiring and owning high-quality, stabilized data centers leased to leading cloud provider customers on long-term contracts. The joint ventures will own 13 newly constructed powered shells across two AWS data center campuses, with AWS retaining a 25% interest in the joint ventures. AWS will lease back 100% of the portfolio on a triple net basis with an initial lease term of 12 years and a fully extended lease term of 32 years. Nick Pell, Chief Executive Officer and President of BXDC, said, “We are thrilled to announce BXDC’s inaugural investment and our partnership with Amazon, a leading global technology company with a long-term commitment to innovation. The quality, basis and tenant profile of these assets make this an attractive match for the deployment of our IPO proceeds. Given the deep expertise across our platform, we believe BXDC is well positioned to capitalize on a highly compelling opportunity and deliver value for our shareholders.” "As we scale to meet growing demand for our customers, we're committed to building in a way that strengthens the communities where we operate,” said Prasad Kalyanaraman, VP of AWS Infrastructure. “We're focused on delivering long-term local benefits, from creating good jobs and free workforce training programs to supporting local priorities. Partnering with Blackstone allows us to continue expanding responsibly while keeping communities at the center of how we build.” The transaction is expected to close in the fourth quarter of 2026 and is subject to certain closing conditions. Morgan Stanley, CBRE Capital Markets, Citi, Goldman Sachs, J.P. Morgan, and Wells Fargo Bank, N.A. are serving as financial advisors on the transaction. Simpson Thacher & Bartlett LLP is serving as legal advisor to Blackstone. About Blackstone Digital Infrastructure Trust Blackstone Digital Infrastructure Trust (NYSE: BXDC) is a recently listed company focused on acquiring and owning mission-critical data center assets that power the modern digital economy. BXDC targets newly-constructed, income-generating, stabilized data center properties leased to investment-grade hyperscale tenants on long-term contracts. Our investment strategy is designed to generate stable, long-term cash flows and deliver current income to shareholders, with growth potential through contractual rent escalations and accretive acquisition opportunities. BXDC is externally managed by an affiliate of Blackstone (NYSE: BX), the world’s largest alternative asset manager and the largest financial investor in data center and digital infrastructure assets globally. Further information is available at www.bxdc.com. About Blackstone Blackstone is the world’s largest alternative asset manager. Blackstone seeks to deliver compelling returns for institutional and individual investors by strengthening the companies in which the firm invests. Blackstone’s nearly $1.4 trillion in assets under management include global investment strategies focused on real estate, private equity, credit, infrastructure, life sciences, growth equity, secondaries and hedge funds. Further information is available at www.blackstone.com. Follow @blackstone on LinkedIn, X (Twitter), and Instagram. artigo.texto: Stem and Copec Expand Partnership to Advance Energy Storage and Intelligent Energy Management Across Latin America Building on the Granja Solar project in Chile, the companies will jointly serve utility-scale and commercial and industrial customers across key regional markets HOUSTON--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Nov. 16, 2026-- Stem, Inc. (NYSE: STEM), a global leader in AI-enabled clean energy software and services, today announced a partnership agreement with Copec Flux, the renewable energy subsidiary of Copec S.A., to jointly deliver energy storage and energy management solutions, initially focusing on Chile, with plans to explore opportunities in Colombia and other Latin American markets. The agreement expands an existing relationship established through the Granja Solar project in Chile, where Copec Flux is deploying Stem's PowerTrack™ Energy Management System (EMS) as the master control system for a 135 MW solar facility being retrofitted with a 420 MWh battery energy storage system. Announced in May 2026, the project provides a foundation for extending the companies' collaboration to additional customers and markets. “Our partnership with Copec Flux is about making advanced energy technology more accessible to customers while simplifying how projects are deployed and operated,” said Arun Narayanan, Chief Executive Officer of Stem. “By combining our technology with Copec Flux's local capabilities, we can help customers bring projects online faster, improve operational performance, and maximize the long-term value of their energy investments.” Under the partnership, Stem will provide its PowerTrack software and controls technology, including EMS, power plant controls (PPC), and cloud-based monitoring and analytics, while Copec Flux will lead local engineering, project delivery, and operational services. The joint offering will serve utility-scale developers and asset owners as well as commercial and industrial (C&I) customers, providing a coordinated approach to deploying, monitoring, and managing solar, storage, and hybrid energy assets. “Energy storage is becoming critical for reliability across regional grids,” said Juan Cristóbal González, CEO of Copec Flux. “Collaborating with specialized technology providers like Stem allows us to test software capabilities at Granja Solar and identify the most efficient ways to support our clients' energy needs.” The expanded relationship reflects Stem's broader strategy to grow its international footprint through partnerships that combine its software and controls capabilities with established regional providers. As demand for flexible, intelligent energy infrastructure continues to grow, the companies see opportunities to extend the delivery model established at Granja Solar to additional projects and customers throughout Latin America. For more information on Stem and the PowerTrack, visit stem.com. About Stem Stem is a global leader in energy intelligence and the operating system for clean energy: where assets connect, sites are optimized, and value is captured. Powered by decades of operational experience and purpose-built AI, our PowerTrack™ platform is the layer that sits between raw data and confident action, making every decision-maker smarter, every asset more productive, and every transition more certain. From asset monitoring to portfolio optimization and control, PowerTrack delivers everything energy professionals need in one place. With projects managed across 55 countries, we have spent nearly 20 years empowering asset owners, operators, and developers to take command of what comes next, with the certainty to act, the trust to commit, and the intelligence to lead. Learn more at stem.com. About Copec and Copec Flux Copec is one of Chile's leading energy companies, with nearly 90 years of experience serving individuals, businesses, and industries across the country. Historically recognized for its leadership in fuel distribution and convenience services, the company is evolving into a broader energy and mobility platform, with growing investments in renewable energy, electromobility, and energy storage. As part of this strategy, its subsidiary Copec Flux develops, builds, and operates solar and energy storage projects across Chile, delivering integrated clean energy solutions for utility-scale, commercial, and industrial customers. Through its nationwide footprint, operational capabilities, and long-term commitment to innovation and sustainability, Copec seeks to play a key role in accelerating Chile’s energy transition and development. artigo.texto: ICE Launches New Tool to Quantify Data Center Construction Risk ATLANTA & NEW YORK--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Nov. 17, 2026-- Intercontinental Exchange, Inc. (NYSE: ICE), one of the world's leading providers of financial market technology and data powering global capital markets, today announced the launch of the ICE Data Center Site Analytics Tool. The tool helps developers, investors, lenders, and municipalities assess the feasibility and delay risk of data center projects before capital is committed. Data centers are among the largest components of U.S. private sector investment today, with cumulative global spending projected to reach $7 trillion by 2030 to meet the demand for compute power, according to McKinsey & Company. Although data centers have been a clear driver of U.S. economic growth, local factors such as utility costs, environmental concerns, and community opposition are increasing the probability of halted or delayed projects. Trained on thousands of data center permitting and project outcomes across the U.S., the ICE Data Center Construction Disruption Model, a key part of the ICE Data Center Site Analytics Tool, is designed to estimate the probability that data center construction may face disruption within 24 months. When tested against historical permit outcomes to analyze the probability of disruption, the model achieved 77% accuracy. “Data center capital is moving faster than local permitting and community consensus, and that gap is now a material financial risk,” said Larry Lawrence, Head of the Geospatial Intelligence team at ICE. “On a median-sized $2.7 billion project, a 12-month delay can cost $162 million to $270 million, so giving developers and communities a common, data-driven view of those costs can lead to better-informed agreements.” The ICE Data Center Site Analytics Tool covers more than 3,100 U.S. counties and tracks thousands of existing U.S. data centers across 47 embedded geospatial data layers, estimating disruption probability through three categories of inputs: - County permit history, including past delay and stoppage rates, filing volume and trends, project value, and fees. - Local site characteristics, including nearby electricity and water costs, plus tract-level education, broadband, poverty, and unemployment. - Market conditions, analyzing the ICE U.S . Mortgage Rate Lock Index at the time of filing. The ICE Data Center Site Analytics Tool is part of ICE Geospatial Intelligence, which links location-specific data to financial assets and securities. The platform spans 1.6 billion global building footprints, 13 million corporate asset locations, more than 100 million U.S. properties and more than 50,000 municipal bond issuers. Learn more about ICE Geospatial Intelligence: ICE Geospatial Intelligence | ICE About Intercontinental Exchange Intercontinental Exchange, Inc. (NYSE: ICE) is a Fortune 500 company that designs, builds, and operates digital networks that connect people to opportunity. We provide financial technology and data services across major asset classes helping our customers access mission-critical workflow tools that increase transparency and efficiency. ICE’s futures, equity, and options exchanges -- including the New York Stock Exchange -- and clearing houses help people invest, raise capital and manage risk. We offer some of the world’s largest markets to trade and clear energy and environmental products. Our fixed income, data services and execution capabilities provide information, analytics and platforms that help our customers streamline processes and capitalize on opportunities. At ICE Mortgage Technology, we are transforming U.S. housing finance, from initial consumer engagement through loan production, closing, registration and the long-term servicing relationship. Together, ICE transforms, streamlines, and automates industries to connect our customers to opportunity. Trademarks of ICE and/or its affiliates include Intercontinental Exchange, ICE, ICE block design, NYSE and New York Stock Exchange. artigo.texto: Proposed Lansing data center ban draws packed hearing, boos and debate A proposal to ban data centers and cryptocurrency mining facilities drew a packed auditorium Tuesday night, with supporters urging Lansing officials to protect local resources and opponents warning against closing the door to potential investment. 48 people signed up to speak at the public hearing at Lansing Middle School. Each was given two minutes, with a 9 p.m. cutoff for the proceedings. Many attendees wore red to show support for the ban. Some speakers opposing it, including TeraWulf representatives, were met with boos and shouted interruptions. Board members repeatedly asked the audience to stop shouting and clapping so speakers could continue. The debate comes amid opposition to TeraWulf’s proposed artificial intelligence data center at the former Cayuga Power Plant site near Cayuga Lake. The proposed zoning amendment would define data centers and cryptocurrency mining facilities but exclude them from the town’s list of permitted uses, making them prohibited under the zoning code. The change would apply townwide rather than serve as a decision on a single project application. Before the hearing, neighbors and community advocates held a press conference supporting the proposed ban. Speakers stood in front of signs reading “No Data Center on Cayuga Lake.” “We enthusiastically support the board moving forward with a ban on data centers and crypto mining facilities in the town,” said Renee Vogelsang, a member of the FLX Strong coalition. Supporters cited concerns about water resources, electricity demand, noise and the potential effects on nearby neighborhoods. Lisa Lincoln and Mark Zuss said they live approximately 3 1/2 miles from the proposed site. In a joint interview, they raised concerns about how the development could affect the lake and their quality of life, including potential noise from the facility. TeraWulf representatives urged the board to continue considering the project, arguing that development could generate new tax revenue and support schools, public services and infrastructure. One representative also discussed the possibility of a community benefits agreement providing recurring financial contributions toward local priorities. Those contributions were presented as potential benefits, rather than a finalized agreement. Another TeraWulf representative argued that opposing the ban should not be interpreted as endorsing the proposed development. “Voting no to this ban doesn’t mean automatic support of the data center,” the representative said. “It means we should thoughtfully review individual projects as they come along.” A resident speaking against the ban also urged officials to consider potential economic benefits and raised concerns about possible legal challenges. The hearing gave the board sharply differing views on whether Lansing should prohibit the facilities or continue reviewing proposals individually. A vote on the proposed zoning change was tentatively scheduled for Wednesday, Nov. 18, at Lansing Middle School.

artigo.texto: Aedan Looking Glass and Magnom Properties Announce US$750 Million Pinnacle Data Center at Forbes International Tower, Egypt Strategic collaboration with Trinidy AI and Turnkey Capital will establish advanced computing and digital infrastructure capabilities in The New Capital’s tower WASHINGTON--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Nov. 16, 2026-- Magnom Properties, developer of Forbes International Towerand onboarding member ofForbes Global Properties, and U.S.-based Aedan Looking Glass (ALG) announce a strategic partnership to support the development of Pinnacle Data Center, an advanced computing and digital infrastructure facility to be housed within the landmark tower. Located in Egypt's New Capital, Forbes International Tower sets a new benchmark for intelligent building technology and environmentally-responsive architecture, positioned to become the world’s first skyscraper to register for International Living Future Institute’s Zero Carbon Certificate. The agreement was formalized on November 10, 2026, in Washington, D.C. The signing coincided with B20 USA, an annual forum that aligns international real estate development and U.S. technology stakeholders to address the growing demand for high-performance computing, artificial intelligence infrastructure, and secure enterprise digital services. Serving as the digital backbone of Forbes International Tower, Pinnacle Data Center brings together the expertise of Magnom Properties, ALG, Trinidy AI, and Turnkey Capital Inc. (OTC: TKCI). Trinidy AI will serve as the data center operator, overseeing facility design, development, and ongoing operations, including the delivery of advanced AI computing services. ALG will lead technology and infrastructure delivery, while Turnkey Capital will participate as a strategic partner supporting the project's broader technology and infrastructure objectives. Pinnacle Data Center is being developed under a long-term commercial framework that aligns ALG’s investment in the facility with Magnom Properties’ long-term ownership of Forbes International Tower. Under that framework, ALG funds and delivers the facility, and Magnom Properties has a defined path to bring it fully within the tower’s ownership. Designed by Adrian Smith + Gordon Gill Architecture, Forbes International Tower will incorporate clean hydrogen energy, integrated solar technologies, intelligent building systems, and advanced security infrastructure. Aligning with the tower's broader environmental objectives, Pinnacle Data Center’s proposed design incorporates AI-driven energy management, modular infrastructure, and intelligent power and cooling systems to optimize operational efficiency and reduce unnecessary energy consumption. “Forbes International Tower represents a new generation of financial centers, integrating sustainable development, global business, and advanced digital infrastructure. As per Fitch’s August 2021 forecast, Egypt’s economy was projected to approach USD 1 trillion by 2030. Forbes International Tower is being developed to support this economic potential by connecting international capital with AI capabilities and high-value financial services, strengthening Egypt’s role as a regional hub for finance and the digital economy said Maged Marie, CEO, Magnom Properties, an onboarding member of Forbes Global Properties, operating as Egypt Forbes Global Properties. As demand for artificial intelligence, high-performance computing, and secure digital services continues to grow, the initiative reflects an opportunity to develop critical technology infrastructure with energy efficiency, resilience, and long-term sustainability in mind. “The Pinnacle Data Center brings together American technology expertise and international investment to establish critical computing infrastructure in one of the region’s most significant commercial developments,” said Eric Fitzgerald, Chairman of Aedan Looking Glass. “Our role is to deliver the technology and infrastructure needed to support secure, scalable AI computing operations. This partnership represents a significant step in expanding U.S. technology capabilities into international markets while supporting Egypt’s growing digital economy.” “The Forbes name has long been associated with people shaping the global business landscape. Forbes International Tower brings that legacy into the built environment, with the advanced digital infrastructure that these leaders increasingly require,” saidMichael Jalbert, CEO of Forbes Global Properties. “We are proud to be a part of this landmark project and to support the growth of Egypt’s New Capital.” By integrating advanced computing capabilities within a landmark commercial development, the initiative seeks to demonstrate how real estate, technology, and digital infrastructure can work together to support the next generation of enterprise activity. “The Pinnacle Data Center represents an opportunity to build a world-class AI computing facility designed to meet the demands of today while also anticipating the demands of tomorrow,” said Clifford Cruz, CEO of Trinidy AI. “As the data center operator, our focus is on delivering efficient, scalable infrastructure that supports the growing demand for AI computing while creating lasting economic value for the region and strengthening the country's technology infrastructure.” About Forbes International Tower Forbes International Tower is a landmark commercial development in Egypt’s New Capital, developed by Magnom Properties in partnership with Forbes and designed by Adrian Smith + Gordon Gill Architecture. Encompassing approximately 100,000 square meters, the tower combines distinctive architectural design with advanced building technologies and digital infrastructure, including Pinnacle Data Center. artigo.texto: Installed energy storage capacity in the United States has surpassed 200 GWh, according to the U.S. Energy Storage Market Outlook Q4 2026, produced by the Solar Energy Industries Association (SEIA) and Benchmark Mineral Intelligence. During the third quarter of 2026, 14.3 GWh of battery energy storage systems (BESS) entered operation. These additions brought total deployments during the first nine months of the year to 48.3 GWh, representing a 20% year-on-year increase. The volume installed between July and September was 1% lower than in the same quarter of 2025. However, the cumulative results for 2026 reflect growth in both grid-connected projects and behind-the-meter storage. Utility-scale projects account for most deployments Utility-scale projects represented most of the storage deployed during the first nine months of 2026, with 40.8 GWh, while the behind-the-meter segment added 7.5 GWh. In the third quarter alone, the utility-scale market added 12.2 GWh across 45 projects. Three projects with gigawatt-hour-scale capacity began operations during the period. Commercial and industrial storage added 1.3 GWh during the quarter, an increase of 29% year on year. Between January and September, this segment reached 5.4 GWh, exceeding the 4.8 GWh installed during the whole of 2025. SEIA and Benchmark attribute part of this growth to data centre expansion and the difficulties these consumers face in securing sufficient grid capacity. BESS can be combined with on-site solar or wind generation to manage demand, shift renewable output and provide short-duration backup power. Residential storage, meanwhile, added 746 MWh during the third quarter, up 16% year on year and the highest volume recorded for a third quarter. Nevertheless, installations through September remained 12% below the level recorded during the first nine months of 2025. Texas leads state-level deployment Texas led utility-scale energy storage deployment through the end of the third quarter, adding 12.3 GWh of capacity. Arizona ranked second with 7.7 GWh, followed by California with 6.8 GWh. Eleven states had already surpassed their previous annual energy storage installation records by the end of September: Colorado, Massachusetts, Utah, Michigan, Georgia, Mississippi, Virginia, Iowa, Montana, Alabama and Illinois. The report identifies a shift in state policy from setting storage targets to conducting procurement processes. During 2026, New York awarded contracts to eight projects totalling approximately 950 MW in its first bulk energy storage solicitation, while Illinois secured around 600 MW in its first dedicated procurement. A previous SEIA analysis attributed part of the reduction in average wholesale electricity prices between the summers of 2021 and 2026 to the combined growth of solar and energy storage: 42% in Texas and 51% in California. seia.org 2030 forecast increases to 708 GWh SEIA and Benchmark raised their forecast for cumulative US energy storage capacity in 2030 by 3.7%. The updated outlook expects the country to reach 708 GWh across grid-connected and behind-the-meter systems. The revision reflects the number of projects under development, state procurement programmes and the growing need for flexibility across the electricity system. Energy storage can shift electricity from periods of high production to hours of greater demand, respond to fluctuations in renewable generation and provide grid services. Its deployment can also reduce the need to use additional generation facilities during demand peaks. Battery cell manufacturing capacity reaches 92.4 GWh US manufacturing capacity for energy storage cells also increased during the third quarter. Production of lithium iron phosphate cells for stationary energy storage began at a facility in Tennessee in July. Another facility opened in Indiana in October, increasing total US cell manufacturing capacity to 92.4 GWh, a 50% rise. The report estimates that lithium iron phosphate (LFP) chemistry will represent 92% of lithium-ion BESS deployments in 2026, up from 77% in 2023. Overall, lithium-ion batteries are expected to account for more than 97% of installations. Industry calls for permitting reform The report’s publication coincides with a request from more than 300 solar and energy storage companies for Congress to approve the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act (BAAJA). The companies argue that the reform would shorten permitting procedures for energy infrastructure, reduce development costs and accelerate the connection of new projects. SEIA maintains that expanding energy storage infrastructure can increase the capacity available to meet electricity demand growth and support the integration of renewable generation into the US grid.

artigo.texto: - The Integrity Council has signed a cooperation agreement with South Korea’s Ministry of Economy and Finance and the Global Green Growth Institute. - The partnership will support the development of the Global Verified Carbon Market framework. - The work will focus on sharing expertise on carbon credit quality standards and the Integrity Council’s Core Carbon Principles. The Integrity Council for the Voluntary Carbon Market (Integrity Council, also known as ICVCM) has agreed to work with the Republic of Korea and the Global Green Growth Institute (GGGI) to help shape an emerging framework for international cooperation on carbon markets. The three parties signed a tripartite memorandum of understanding (MoU) on November 15, bringing together the te Integrity Council, South Korea’s Ministry of Economy and Finance and GGGI, which serves as the interim secretariat for the Global Verified Carbon Market (GVCM). The agreement is intended to support the framework’s development and help ensure that its design meets a global standard for high-integrity carbon credits. The benchmark will be based on the Integrity Council’s Core Carbon Principles (CCPs) and its Assessment Framework. Partnership Targets Common Standards The GVCM is an emerging initiative through which participating countries aim to cooperate on carbon markets. Under the arrangement, the Integrity Council will share technical expertise with GGGI and help countries participating in, or considering joining, the new framework understand the principles and assessment requirements. The cooperation reflects an effort to build integrity into the GVCM as it takes shape, rather than address shortcomings after the framework is established. Relevant: ICVCM Publishes Article 6 And Domestic Policy Framework Guide For Governments Amy Merrill, chief executive of the Integrity Council, said the partnership would contribute to the development of interconnected carbon markets while supporting a consistent international threshold for credit quality. GGGI Executive Director Sang-Hyup Kim said confidence in the credibility of emissions reductions was essential for carbon credits to channel finance into projects that cut emissions. Early collaboration with the Integrity Council, he added, could help prevent costly changes later and maintain the confidence of participating countries. artigo.texto: FNSB Planning Commission recommends data center moratorium FAIRBANKS, Alaska (KTUU/KTVF) - The Fairbanks North Star Borough Planning Commission approved Mayor Grier Hopkins’ proposed moratorium on permits for large-scale data centers in the borough on Tuesday, extending the mayor’s proposed 12-month timeframe to 18. On Oct. 22, the borough assembly voted unanimously to send the ordinance to the Planning Commission as part of its consent agenda, requiring a recommendation within 90 days. Approval from the commission sends the ordinance back to the assembly for final approval, with Hopkins saying a vote will likely take place on Jan. 14. “That’s when the clock will start for the 18-month moratorium, and so from there, we’ll move forward with working and trying to research what the regulations need to be for data centers,” Hopkins said. The goal of this moratorium is to allow the borough to research potential impacts from data centers, including effects on the electric grid, sound pollution, housing, traffic and property taxes, and come up with proposed regulations to be included in a future ordinance. “The sheer scale of what you see happening in other cities that pop up before they can take action is relatively terrifying if you love your community and don’t want to see that size of impacts without a voice from the public being put first and foremost,” Hopkins said, “So this is a really good step to be proactive before we have to say, ‘Oh no, this thing is already happening, and we’re not even ready.’” The commission also increased the timeline for the administration to research the subject and get back to them with recommendations from six months to 10. According to Hopkins, his office will partner with the Community Planning Department for the necessary research. “I would like to hold some public opportunities for open houses to bring in input, to do research into the small data centers that are already here, to talk to [Golden Valley Electric Association] about what their grid situation looks like, North Pole Water, that sort of things to make sure we’re taking a whole picture and a whole look of what our community wants,” he explained. While confident any proposed data centers outside of the Eielson Air Force Base fence would be under borough jurisdiction, Hopkins was unclear as to what extent the purpose of a data center on base would be subject to a moratorium. “If it comes in as purely for a government purpose, I believe that would be not subject to our moratorium and our regulations. If it’s for private sector use it might be different,” the mayor said. “We’re doing some research into that and trying to figure out how to turn that gray area black and white.” See a spelling or grammar error? artigo.texto: As ações de empresas americanas de tecnologia óptica subiram na terça-feira, após uma reportagem da Reuters indicar que o governo Trump pretende prosseguir com as restrições à importação de equipamentos chineses para centros de dados, apesar das objeções de várias grandes empresas de tecnologia americanas. As ações da Coherent Corp. (NYSE:COHR) subiram 10%, enquanto as da Applied Optoelectronics Inc. (NASDAQ:AAOI) ganharam 9%. A Lumentum Holdings Inc. (NASDAQ:LITE) teve alta de 8% e a Corning Inc. (NYSE:GLW) avançou 3,5%. As medidas propostas restringiriam as importações de novos modelos de transceptores ópticos chineses, componentes usados para transmitir dados em alta velocidade por meio de redes de fibra óptica em centros de dados. As restrições fazem parte de um esforço mais amplo dos EUA para abordar preocupações de segurança nacional associadas à infraestrutura de telecomunicações e informática fornecida por fabricantes chineses. Órgãos reguladores dos EUA expressam preocupação com a segurança dos transceptores ópticos A Comissão Federal de Comunicações (FCC) identificou potenciais riscos à segurança nacional associados aos transceptores ópticos chineses. Segundo as preocupações do órgão regulador, o equipamento poderia ser explorado para acessar informações sensíveis, introduzir software malicioso ou interromper as operações de centros de dados nos EUA. Os transceptores ópticos são usados para converter sinais elétricos em sinais ópticos e possibilitar a comunicação de alta velocidade entre servidores e equipamentos de rede. Os componentes são uma parte importante da infraestrutura que suporta a computação em nuvem e as aplicações de inteligência artificial. As restrições propostas se aplicariam a novos modelos de transceptores ópticos chineses, podendo afetar as decisões de aquisição por parte dos operadores de centros de dados dos EUA. Grandes empresas de tecnologia se opõem às restrições de importação propostas Segundo a Reuters, várias empresas de tecnologia dos EUA fizeram lobby contra as medidas propostas, citando preocupações sobre sua implementação e a disponibilidade de fornecedores alternativos. Amazon, Google, Meta, CoreWeave, Cisco e Microsoft estão entre as empresas que teriam manifestado objeções. Segundo relatos, executivos disseram a funcionários da Casa Branca que o cumprimento da exigência de substituir os equipamentos chineses poderia levar até uma década. Suas preocupações refletem a dimensão dos acordos de fornecimento existentes e os potenciais desafios associados à identificação de fabricantes alternativos capazes de atender à demanda. Apesar da oposição, o governo Trump pretende, segundo relatos, continuar a implementar as restrições. Os fabricantes chineses respondem pela maior parte do fornecimento global De acordo com a empresa de pesquisa Counterpoint Research, a China representa atualmente cerca de dois terços do mercado global de transceptores ópticos. Empresas chinesas, incluindo a Eoptolink e a Zhongji Innolight, estão entre os principais fornecedores desses componentes. Sua posição no mercado reflete a escala da capacidade de produção da China e seu papel consolidado nas cadeias de suprimento globais de equipamentos para data centers. Empresas americanas como a Coherent e a Lumentum competem no mercado de tecnologia óptica, embora sua capacidade de produção atual possa não ser suficiente para substituir imediatamente os fornecedores chineses. Um relatório da Fundação para a Inovação Americana indicou que os fabricantes nacionais atualmente não possuem a escala necessária para atender a todo o volume da demanda atendida pelas empresas chinesas. As restrições propostas podem, portanto, exigir mudanças na capacidade de produção e nos acordos de aquisição em todo o setor. As empresas de tecnologia óptica dos EUA poderiam se beneficiar das restrições? Os desdobramentos políticos relatados podem criar oportunidades comerciais adicionais para os fabricantes de equipamentos ópticos dos EUA, caso os operadores de data centers sejam obrigados a reduzir as compras de fornecedores chineses. As empresas Coherent, Lumentum, Applied Optoelectronics e Corning registraram ganhos no preço de suas ações após a reportagem da Reuters. Os investidores parecem estar avaliando o potencial de mudanças nos acordos de fornecimento para aumentar a demanda por equipamentos fornecidos por empresas sediadas nos EUA. No entanto, a extensão de qualquer benefício comercial dependerá dos requisitos regulamentares finais, dos cronogramas de implementação e da capacidade de fornecedores alternativos de expandir a produção. As limitações de capacidade existentes podem afetar a rapidez com que os fabricantes dos EUA conseguem responder ao aumento da demanda. Indústria alerta para possíveis restrições chinesas às exportações Empresas de tecnologia dos EUA também manifestaram preocupação com a possibilidade de medidas comerciais retaliatórias por parte da China. Segundo a Reuters, representantes da indústria alertaram que Pequim poderia responder restringindo as exportações de fosfeto de índio, um material usado na produção de certos transceptores ópticos. O fosfeto de índio é um importante material semicondutor para equipamentos de comunicação óptica de alta velocidade. Restrições à sua disponibilidade podem afetar fabricantes que dependem do material para a produção de componentes ópticos. A possibilidade de medidas retaliatórias aumenta a incerteza quanto aos potenciais efeitos das restrições de importação propostas pelos EUA nas cadeias de abastecimento globais. FCC mantém restrições mais amplas a equipamentos tecnológicos chineses A proposta mais recente segue outras medidas introduzidas pela FCC ao longo do último ano, relacionadas à importação de certos produtos tecnológicos chineses. Essas medidas incluíram restrições que afetaram novos drones, robôs, inversores de energia e roteadores chineses.
